78. Kilesasampayuttadukaṃ

78. The Dyad on States Associated with Defilements

1. Paṭiccavāro

1. The Dependence Chapter

73. Kilesasampayuttaṃ [V 4.0035] dhammaṃ paṭicca kilesasampayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – kilesasampayuttaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (1)

73. A state associated with defilements arises dependent on a state associated with defilements by way of root condition. Dependent on one aggregate associated with defilements, three aggregates arise... dependent on two aggregates... (1)

Kilesasampayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kilesavippayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – kilesasampayutte khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (2)

A state dissociated from defilements arises dependent on a state associated with defilements by way of root condition: Dependent on aggregates associated with defilements, mind-originated matter arises. (2)

(Kilesasampayuttadukaṃ saṃkiliṭṭhadukasadisaṃ, ninnānākaraṇaṃ.)

(The Dyad Associated with Defilements is similar to the Defiled Dyad; there is no difference in exposition.)

Kilesasampayuttadukaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Dyad Associated with Defilements is finished.

79. Kilesasaṃkilesikadukaṃ

79. The Dyad of Defilements and Defiling Phenomena

1. Paṭiccavāro

1. The Dependence Chapter

Hetupaccayo

The Root Condition

74. Kilesañceva saṃkilesikañca dhammaṃ paṭicca kileso ceva saṃkilesiko ca dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – lobhaṃ paṭicca moho diṭṭhi thinaṃ uddhaccaṃ ahirikaṃ anottappaṃ (cakkaṃ). (1)

74. Dependent on a phenomenon that is both a defilement and defiling, a phenomenon that is a defilement and defiling arises by way of root condition: dependent on greed, there arise delusion, wrong view, sloth, restlessness, shamelessness, and fearlessness of wrongdoing (as a cycle). (1)

Kilesañceva saṃkilesikañca dhammaṃ paṭicca saṃkilesiko ceva no ca kileso dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – kilese paṭicca sampayuttakā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ. (2)

Dependent on a phenomenon that is both a defilement and defiling, a phenomenon that is defiling but not a defilement arises by way of root condition: dependent on the defilements, the associated aggregates and mind-originated matter arise. (2)

Kilesañceva saṃkilesikañca dhammaṃ paṭicca kileso [T 4.0324] ceva saṃkilesiko ca saṃkilesiko ceva no ca kileso ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – lobhaṃ paṭicca moho diṭṭhi thinaṃ uddhaccaṃ ahirikaṃ anottappaṃ sampayuttakā ca khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ. (3)

Dependent on a phenomenon that is both a defilement and defiling, both phenomena that are defilements and defiling and phenomena that are defiling but not defilements arise by way of root condition: dependent on greed, there arise delusion, wrong view, sloth, restlessness, shamelessness, fearlessness of wrongdoing, the associated aggregates, and mind-originated matter. (3)

2-6. Sahajāta-paccaya-nissaya-saṃsaṭṭha-sampayuttavāro

2-6. The Co-nascence, Condition, Support, Association, and Conjunction Section

(Evaṃ [M 4.0030][V 4.0036] paṭiccavāropi sahajātavāropi paccayavāropi nissayavāropi saṃsaṭṭhavāropi sampayuttavāropi kilesadukasadisā. Ninnānākaraṇaṃ. Āmasanaṃ nānaṃ.)

(Thus, the Dependence Section, the Co-nascence Section, the Condition Section, the Support Section, the Association Section, and the Conjunction Section are similar to the Defilement Dyad. The method is not different. The application is varied.)

7. Pañhāvāro

7. The Question Section

1. Paccayānulomaṃ

1. Analysis of Conditions in Forward Order

1. Vibhaṅgavāro

1. The Analysis Section

Hetupaccayo

Root Condition

75. Kileso ceva saṃkilesiko ca dhammo kilesassa ceva saṃkilesikassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – kilesā ceva saṃkilesikā ca hetū sampayuttakānaṃ kilesānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo (evaṃ cattāri, kilesadukasadisaṃ.) (4)

75. A state that is both a defilement and defiling is a condition for a state that is both a defilement and defiling by way of root condition: the roots that are defilements and defiling are a condition for associated defilements by way of root condition. (Thus the four permutations are similar to the Defilement Dyad.) (4)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

Object Condition

76. Kileso ceva saṃkilesiko ca dhammo kilesassa ceva saṃkilesikassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – kilese ārabbha kilesā uppajjanti. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Kilese ārabbha saṃkilesikā ceva no ca kilesā khandhā uppajjanti. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Kilese ārabbha kilesā ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā uppajjanti. (3)

76. A state that is both a defilement and defiling is a condition for a state that is both a defilement and defiling by way of object condition: defilements arise having defilements as their object. (The root text should be supplied.) Aggregates that are defiling but not defilements arise having defilements as their object. (The root text should be supplied.) Defilements and their associated aggregates arise having defilements as their object. (3)

77. Saṃkilesiko ceva no ca kileso dhammo saṃkilesikassa ceva no ca kilesassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ…pe… pubbe suciṇṇāni…pe… jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā jhānaṃ paccavekkhati, assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati…pe… uddhaccaṃ uppajjati, jhāne parihīne [T 4.0325] vippaṭisārissa domanassaṃ uppajjati; ariyā gotrabhuṃ paccavekkhanti, vodānaṃ paccavekkhanti, cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ saṃkilesike ceva no ca kilese khandhe aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; dibbena cakkhunā [V 4.0037] rūpaṃ passati…pe… āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo (itare dve kilesadukasadisā, ghaṭanārammaṇāpi kilesadukasadisā).

77. A state that is defiling but not a defilement is a condition for a state that is defiling but not a defilement by way of object condition: one gives a gift… undertakes the precepts… observes the Uposatha… one reflects on past good deeds… Having emerged from jhāna, one reviews the jhāna, savors it, and delights in it. Taking that as object, lust arises… restlessness arises. When one has fallen away from jhāna, sorrow arises in one who feels remorse. Noble ones review the change-of-lineage consciousness; they review purification. One reviews the eye… the physical basis… the aggregates that are defiling but not defilements as impermanent… and sorrow arises. With the divine eye one sees a form… is a condition for adverting by way of object condition. (The other two permutations are similar to the Defilement Dyad; the application by way of object is also similar to the Defilement Dyad.)

Adhipatipaccayo

Dominance Condition

78. Kileso [M 4.0031] ceva saṃkilesiko ca dhammo kilesassa ceva saṃkilesikassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati… tīṇi.

78. A state that is both a defilement and defiling is a condition for a state that is both a defilement and defiling by way of dominance condition—by way of object-dominance… three.

Saṃkilesiko ceva no ca kileso dhammo saṃkilesikassa ceva no ca kilesassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ…pe… pubbe suciṇṇāni…pe… jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā jhānaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati, sekkhā gotrabhuṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti, vodānaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti; cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ saṃkilesike ceva no ca kilese khandhe garuṃ katvā saṃkilesikā ceva no ca kilesā khandhā uppajjanti. Sahajātādhipati – saṃkilesikā ceva no ca kilesādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (Itare dvepi kilesadukasadisā. Ghaṭanādhipatipi.)

A state that is defiling but not a defilement is a condition for a state that is defiling but not a defilement by way of dominance condition: by way of object-dominance and co-nascence dominance. Object-dominance: one gives a gift… undertakes the precepts… observes the Uposatha… one reflects on past good deeds… Having emerged from jhāna, one reviews the jhāna, holding it in high esteem. Trainees review the change-of-lineage consciousness, holding it in high esteem; they review purification, holding it in high esteem. Holding the eye… the physical basis… the aggregates that are defiling but not defilements in high esteem, aggregates that are defiling but not defilements arise. Co-nascence dominance: a dominant factor that is defiling but not a defilement is a condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter by way of dominance condition. (The other two permutations are also similar to the Defilement Dyad. Also the application by way of dominance.)

Anantarapaccayādi

Contiguity Condition, etc.

79. Kileso ceva saṃkilesiko ca dhammo kilesassa ceva saṃkilesikassa ca dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi (kilesadukasadisā).

79. A state that is both a defilement and defiling is a condition for a state that is both a defilement and defiling by way of contiguity condition… three (similar to the Defilement Dyad).

Saṃkilesiko ceva no ca kileso dhammo saṃkilesikassa ceva no ca kilesassa dhammassa [T 4.0326] anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā saṃkilesikā ceva no ca kilesā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ saṃkilesikānañceva no ca kilesānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; anulomaṃ gotrabhussa… anulomaṃ vodānassa… āvajjanā saṃkilesikānañceva no ca kilesānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo.

A state that is defiling but not a defilement is a condition for a state that is defiling but not a defilement by way of contiguity condition: preceding aggregates that are defiling but not defilements are a condition for succeeding aggregates that are defiling but not defilements by way of contiguity condition; adaptation consciousness is a condition for change-of-lineage consciousness… adaptation consciousness is a condition for purification consciousness… adverting is a condition for aggregates that are defiling but not defilements by way of contiguity condition.

(Itare dve anantarā kilesadukasadisā, ninnānākaraṇā. Ghaṭanānantarampi sabbe paccayā kilesadukasadisā[V 4.0038], ninnānākaraṇā. Upanissaye lokuttaraṃ natthi, idaṃ dukaṃ kilesadukasadisaṃ, ninnānākaraṇaṃ.)

(The other two contiguity permutations are similar to the Defilement Dyad, being undifferentiated. In the application by way of contiguity also, all conditions are similar to the Defilement Dyad, being undifferentiated. In decisive support condition, there is no supramundane; this dyad is similar to the Defilement Dyad, being undifferentiated.)

Kilesasaṃkilesikadukaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Dyad of Defilement and the Defiling is concluded.

Hetupaccayo

Root Condition

80. Kilesañceva [M 4.0032] saṃkiliṭṭhañca dhammaṃ paṭicca kileso ceva saṃkiliṭṭho ca dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – lobhaṃ paṭicca moho diṭṭhi thinaṃ uddhaccaṃ ahirikaṃ anottappaṃ (cakkaṃ). (1)

80. Dependent on a state that is both a defilement and defiled, a state that is both a defilement and defiled arises by way of root condition. For example, dependent on greed, delusion, wrong view, sloth, restlessness, shamelessness, and lack of moral dread arise (as a cycle). (1)

Kilesañceva saṃkiliṭṭhañca dhammaṃ paṭicca saṃkiliṭṭho ceva no ca kileso dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – kilese paṭicca sampayuttakā khandhā. (2)

Dependent on a state that is both a defilement and defiled, a state that is defiled but not a defilement arises by way of root condition. For example, dependent on defilements, the associated aggregates arise. (2)

Kilesañceva saṃkiliṭṭhañca dhammaṃ paṭicca kileso ceva saṃkiliṭṭho ca saṃkiliṭṭho ceva no ca kileso ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – lobhaṃ paṭicca moho diṭṭhi thinaṃ uddhaccaṃ ahirikaṃ anottappaṃ sampayuttakā ca khandhā [T 4.0327] (cakkaṃ). (3)

Dependent on a state that is both a defilement and defiled, a state that is both a defilement and defiled, and a state that is defiled but not a defilement, arise by way of root condition. For example, dependent on greed, delusion, wrong view, sloth, restlessness, shamelessness, lack of moral dread, and the associated aggregates arise (as a cycle). (3)

81. Saṃkiliṭṭhañceva no ca kilesaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca saṃkiliṭṭho ceva no ca kileso dhammo [V 4.0039] uppajjati hetupaccayā – saṃkiliṭṭhañceva no ca kilesaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (1)

81. Dependent on a state that is defiled but not a defilement, a state that is defiled but not a defilement arises by way of root condition. For example, dependent on one aggregate that is defiled but not a defilement, three aggregates arise; …and so on… dependent on two aggregates, the other two aggregates arise. (1)

Saṃkiliṭṭhañceva no ca kilesaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kileso ceva saṃkiliṭṭho ca dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – saṃkiliṭṭhe ceva no ca kilese khandhe paṭicca kilesā. (2)

Dependent on a state that is defiled but not a defilement, a state that is both a defilement and defiled arises by way of root condition. For example, dependent on aggregates that are defiled but not defilements, defilements arise. (2)

Saṃkiliṭṭhañceva no ca kilesaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kileso ceva saṃkiliṭṭho ca saṃkiliṭṭho ceva no ca kileso ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – saṃkiliṭṭhañceva no ca kilesaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā kilesā ca…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (3)

Dependent on a state that is defiled but not a defilement, a state that is both a defilement and defiled, and a state that is defiled but not a defilement, arise by way of root condition. For example, dependent on one aggregate that is defiled but not a defilement, three aggregates and defilements arise; …and so on… dependent on two aggregates, the other two aggregates and defilements arise. (3)

82. Kilesañceva saṃkiliṭṭhañca saṃkiliṭṭhañceva no ca kilesañca dhammaṃ paṭicca kileso ceva saṃkiliṭṭho ca dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – lobhañca sampayuttake ca khandhe paṭicca moho diṭṭhi thinaṃ uddhaccaṃ ahirikaṃ anottappaṃ (cakkaṃ). (1)

82. Dependent on a state that is both a defilement and defiled, and on a state that is defiled but not a defilement, a state that is both a defilement and defiled arises by way of root condition. For example, dependent on greed and the associated aggregates, delusion, wrong view, sloth, restlessness, shamelessness, and lack of moral dread arise (as a cycle). (1)

Kilesañceva [M 4.0033] saṃkiliṭṭhañca saṃkiliṭṭhañceva no ca kilesañca dhammaṃ paṭicca saṃkiliṭṭho ceva no ca kileso dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – saṃkiliṭṭhañceva no ca kilesaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca kilese ca paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe ca…pe…. (2)

Dependent on a state that is both a defilement and defiled, and on a state that is defiled but not a defilement, a state that is defiled but not a defilement arises by way of root condition. For example, dependent on one aggregate that is defiled but not a defilement and on defilements, three aggregates arise; …and so on… dependent on two aggregates and on defilements, the other two aggregates arise. (2)

Kilesañceva saṃkiliṭṭhañca saṃkiliṭṭhañceva no ca kilesañca dhammaṃ paṭicca kileso ceva saṃkiliṭṭho ca saṃkiliṭṭho ceva no ca kileso ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – saṃkiliṭṭhañceva no ca kilesaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca lobhañca paṭicca tayo khandhā moho diṭṭhi thinaṃ uddhaccaṃ ahirikaṃ anottappaṃ…pe… dve khandhe ca…pe… (cakkaṃ). (3)

Dependent on a state that is both a defilement and defiled, and on a state that is defiled but not a defilement, a state that is both a defilement and defiled, and a state that is defiled but not a defilement, arise by way of root condition. For example, dependent on one aggregate that is defiled but not a defilement and on greed, three aggregates, delusion, wrong view, sloth, restlessness, shamelessness, and lack of moral dread arise; …and so on… dependent on two aggregates and on greed, the other two aggregates, delusion, wrong view, sloth, restlessness, shamelessness, and lack of moral dread arise (as a cycle). (3)

83. Hetuyā [T 4.0328] nava, ārammaṇe nava (sabbattha nava), kamme nava, āhāre nava…pe… avigate nava.

83. By way of root, nine; by way of object, nine (in all cases, nine); by way of kamma, nine; by way of nutriment, nine… and so on… by way of non-disappearance, nine.

Nahetupaccayo

Non-Root Condition

84. Kilesañceva [V 4.0040] saṃkiliṭṭhañca dhammaṃ paṭicca kileso ceva saṃkiliṭṭho ca dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – vicikicchaṃ paṭicca vicikicchāsahagato moho, uddhaccaṃ paṭicca uddhaccasahagato moho. (1)

84. Dependent on a state that is both a defilement and defiled, a state that is both a defilement and defiled arises by way of non-root condition. For example, dependent on doubt, delusion accompanied by doubt arises; dependent on restlessness, delusion accompanied by restlessness arises. (1)

Saṃkiliṭṭhañceva no ca kilesaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kileso ceva saṃkiliṭṭho ca dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe paṭicca vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho. (1)

Dependent on a state that is defiled but not a defilement, a state that is both a defilement and defiled arises by way of non-root condition. For example, dependent on aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness, delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness arises. (1)

Kilesañceva saṃkiliṭṭhañca saṃkiliṭṭhañceva no ca kilesañca dhammaṃ paṭicca kileso ceva saṃkiliṭṭho ca dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe ca vicikicchañca uddhaccañca paṭicca vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho. (1)

Dependent on a state that is both a defilement and defiled, and on a state that is defiled but not a defilement, a state that is both a defilement and defiled arises by way of non-root condition. For example, dependent on aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness, and on doubt and restlessness, delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness arises. (1)

85. Nahetuyā [M 4.0034] tīṇi, naadhipatiyā nava, napurejāte nava, napacchājāte nava, naāsevane nava, nakamme tīṇi, navipāke nava, navippayutte nava.

85. By way of non-root, three; by way of non-dominance, nine; by way of non-prenascence, nine; by way of non-postnascence, nine; by way of non-repetition, nine; by way of non-kamma, three; by way of non-result, nine; by way of non-dissociation, nine.

Hetupaccayo

The Root Condition.

86. Kileso [V 4.0041] ceva saṃkiliṭṭho ca dhammo kilesassa ceva saṃkiliṭṭhassa ca dhammassa [T 4.0329] hetupaccayena paccayo – kilesā ceva saṃkiliṭṭhā ca hetū sampayuttakānaṃ kilesānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (1)

86. A phenomenon that is a defilement and defiled is a condition for a phenomenon that is a defilement and defiled by way of root condition. Roots that are defilements and defiled are a condition for associated defilements by way of root condition. (1)

Kileso ceva saṃkiliṭṭho ca dhammo saṃkiliṭṭhassa ceva no ca kilesassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – kilesā ceva saṃkiliṭṭhā ca hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo.

A phenomenon that is a defilement and defiled is a condition for a phenomenon that is defiled but not a defilement by way of root condition. Roots that are defilements and defiled are a condition for associated aggregates by way of root condition.

Kileso ceva saṃkiliṭṭho ca dhammo kilesassa ceva saṃkiliṭṭhassa ca saṃkiliṭṭhassa ceva no ca kilesassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – kilesā ceva saṃkiliṭṭhā ca hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kilesānañca hetupaccayena paccayo. (3)

A phenomenon that is a defilement and defiled is a condition for a phenomenon that is a defilement and defiled, and for a phenomenon that is defiled but not a defilement, by way of root condition. Roots that are defilements and defiled are a condition for associated aggregates and defilements by way of root condition. (3)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

The Object Condition.

87. Kileso ceva saṃkiliṭṭho ca dhammo kilesassa ceva saṃkiliṭṭhassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – kilese ārabbha kilesā uppajjanti. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Kilese ārabbha saṃkiliṭṭhā ceva no ca kilesā khandhā uppajjanti. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Kilese ārabbha kilesā ca sampayuttakā khandhā ca uppajjanti. (3)

87. A phenomenon that is a defilement and defiled is a condition for a phenomenon that is a defilement and defiled by way of object condition. Taking defilements as object, defilements arise. (The root should be applied.) Taking defilements as object, aggregates that are defiled but not defilements arise. (The root should be applied.) Taking defilements as object, defilements and associated aggregates arise. (3)

88. Saṃkiliṭṭho [M 4.0035] ceva no ca kileso dhammo saṃkiliṭṭhassa ceva no ca kilesassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – saṃkiliṭṭhe ceva no ca kilese khandhe ārabbha saṃkiliṭṭhā [V 4.0042] ceva no ca kilesā khandhā uppajjanti. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Saṃkiliṭṭhe ceva no ca kilese khandhe ārabbha kilesā uppajjanti. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Saṃkiliṭṭhe ceva no ca kilese khandhe ārabbha kilesā ca sampayuttakā khandhā ca uppajjanti. (3)

88. A phenomenon that is defiled but not a defilement is a condition for a phenomenon that is defiled but not a defilement by way of object condition. Taking as object aggregates that are defiled but not defilements, aggregates that are defiled but not defilements arise. (The root should be applied.) Taking as object aggregates that are defiled but not defilements, defilements arise. (The root should be applied.) Taking as object aggregates that are defiled but not defilements, defilements and associated aggregates arise. (3)

(Itarepi tīṇi kātabbā.)

(The other three should be applied.)

Adhipatipaccayo

The Dominance Condition.

89. Kileso ceva saṃkiliṭṭho ca dhammo kilesassa ceva saṃkiliṭṭhassa ca [T 4.0330] dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati… tīṇi.

89. A phenomenon that is a defilement and defiled is a condition for a phenomenon that is a defilement and defiled by way of dominance condition: object-dominance… three.

Saṃkiliṭṭho ceva no ca kileso dhammo saṃkiliṭṭhassa ceva no ca kilesassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – saṃkiliṭṭhe ceva no ca kilese khandhe garuṃ katvā…pe… tīṇi. (Dve adhipati tīṇipi kātabbā, itare dvepi tīṇi kātabbā.)

A defiled phenomenon that is not a defilement is a condition for a defiled phenomenon that is not a defilement by way of dominance condition: object-dominance, co-nascent dominance. Object-dominance: having made weighty the defiled aggregates that are not defilements… etc. … three. (The two dominance conditions should also be applied as three; the other two should also be applied as three.)

Anantarapaccayādi

The Contiguity Condition, and so on.

90. Kileso ceva saṃkiliṭṭho ca dhammo kilesassa ceva saṃkiliṭṭhassa ca dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo (navapi kātabbā, āvajjanāpi vuṭṭhānampi natthi)… samanantarapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… aññamaññapaccayena paccayo… nissayapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… nava pañhā (purejātapaccayo pacchājātapaccayopi natthi)… āsevanapaccayena paccayo.

90. A phenomenon that is a defilement and defiled is a condition for a phenomenon that is a defilement and defiled by way of contiguity condition (all nine should be applied; there is neither adverting nor emergence)… by way of proximity condition… by way of co-nascence condition… by way of mutuality condition… by way of support condition… by way of decisive support condition… nine questions (there is neither pre-nascence condition nor post-nascence condition)… by way of repetition condition.

Kammapaccayādi

The Kamma Condition, and so on.

91. Saṃkiliṭṭho ceva no ca kileso dhammo saṃkiliṭṭhassa ceva no ca kilesassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – saṃkiliṭṭhā ceva no ca kilesā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

91. A phenomenon that is defiled but not a defilement is a condition for a phenomenon that is defiled but not a defilement by way of kamma condition. Volitions that are defiled but not defilements are conditions for associated aggregates by way of kamma condition. (1)

Saṃkiliṭṭho [V 4.0043] ceva no ca kileso dhammo kilesassa ceva saṃkiliṭṭhassa ca dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – saṃkiliṭṭhā ceva no [M 4.0036] ca kilesā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ kilesānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (2)

Nahetuyā [V 4.0052] dve, naadhipatiyā dve, napurejāte dve, napacchājāte dve, naāsevane dve, nakamme dve, navipāke dve, najhāne ekaṃ, namagge ekaṃ, navippayutte dve.

Not by root condition: two; not by dominance condition: two; not by prenascent condition: two; not by postnascent condition: two; not by habituation condition: two; not by kamma condition: two; not by result condition: two; not by jhāna condition: one; not by path condition: one; not by dissociation condition: two.

Hetupaccayo

Root Condition

13. A phenomenon to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a phenomenon to be abandoned by seeing by way of root condition… three.

Nadassanena pahātabbo dhammo nadassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – nadassanena pahātabbā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

A phenomenon not to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a phenomenon not to be abandoned by seeing by way of root condition: roots not to be abandoned by seeing are a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena by way of root condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking…and so on. (1)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

Object Condition

14. Dassanena [M 4.0043] pahātabbo dhammo dassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo [V 4.0053] – dassanena pahātabbaṃ rāgaṃ assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha dassanena pahātabbo rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi…pe… vicikicchā [T 4.0338] uppajjati, dassanena pahātabbaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati; dassanena pahātabbaṃ diṭṭhiṃ assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha dassanena pahātabbo rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi…pe… vicikicchā…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; vicikicchaṃ ārabbha vicikicchā uppajjati, diṭṭhi…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; dassanena pahātabbaṃ domanassaṃ ārabbha dassanena pahātabbaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati, vicikicchā uppajjati. (1)

14. A phenomenon to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a phenomenon to be abandoned by seeing by way of object condition: one savors and delights in lust to be abandoned by seeing; taking that as an object, lust to be abandoned by seeing arises, wrong view…and so on… doubt arises, grief to be abandoned by seeing arises; one savors and delights in wrong view to be abandoned by seeing; taking that as an object, lust to be abandoned by seeing arises, wrong view…and so on… doubt…and so on… grief arises; taking doubt as an object, doubt arises, wrong view…and so on… grief arises; taking grief to be abandoned by seeing as an object, grief to be abandoned by seeing arises, wrong view arises, doubt arises. (1)

Dassanena pahātabbo dhammo nadassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – ariyā dassanena pahātabbe pahīne kilese paccavekkhanti, pubbe samudāciṇṇe…pe… dassanena pahātabbe khandhe aniccato…pe… vipassati, cetopariyañāṇena dassanena pahātabbacittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānāti, dassanena pahātabbā khandhā cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a phenomenon not to be abandoned by seeing by way of object condition: noble ones reflect on the defilements to be abandoned by seeing that have been abandoned, on those previously practiced…and so on… one has insight into the aggregates to be abandoned by seeing as impermanent…and so on… with the knowledge of others’ minds, one knows the mind of one who is endowed with a mind to be abandoned by seeing; the aggregates to be abandoned by seeing are a condition for the knowledge of others’ minds, for the knowledge of recollection of past lives, for the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their kamma, for the knowledge of the future, and for adverting, by way of object condition. (2)

15. Nadassanena pahātabbo dhammo nadassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ paccavekkhati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha nadassanena pahātabbo rāgo uppajjati; uddhaccaṃ…pe… nadassanena pahātabbaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati, pubbe suciṇṇāni…pe… jhānā …pe… ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ paccavekkhanti…pe… phalassa āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo; ariyā nadassanena pahātabbe pahīne kilese [T 4.0339] paccavekkhanti, vikkhambhite kilese…pe… pubbe…pe… cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ nadassanena pahātabbe khandhe aniccato…pe… vipassati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha nadassanena pahātabbo rāgo uppajjati, uddhaccaṃ…pe… nadassanena pahātabbaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati; dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati…pe… anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

15. A phenomenon not to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a phenomenon not to be abandoned by seeing by way of object condition: having given a gift…and so on… undertaken moral conduct…and so on… performed an act of observance, one reflects on it, savors it, delights in it; taking that as an object, lust not to be abandoned by seeing arises; restlessness…and so on… grief not to be abandoned by seeing arises; previously well-practiced deeds…and so on… jhānas…and so on… noble ones, having emerged from the path, reflect on the path…and so on… it is a condition for adverting to the fruition by way of object condition; noble ones reflect on the defilements not to be abandoned by seeing that have been abandoned, on the suppressed defilements…and so on… previously…and so on… the eye…and so on… the physical basis…and so on… one has insight into the aggregates not to be abandoned by seeing as impermanent…and so on… one savors and delights in them; taking them as an object, lust not to be abandoned by seeing arises, restlessness…and so on… grief not to be abandoned by seeing arises; with the divine eye one sees a form…and so on… these are a condition for the knowledge of the future and for adverting by way of object condition. (1)

Nadassanena [M 4.0044] pahātabbo dhammo dassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ…pe… pubbe…pe… jhānā…pe… cakkhuṃ [V 4.0054]…pe… vatthuṃ nadassanena pahātabbe khandhe assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha dassanena pahātabbo rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi…pe… vicikicchā…pe… dassanena pahātabbaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati. (2)

A phenomenon not to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a phenomenon to be abandoned by seeing by way of object condition: one savors and delights in a gift…and so on… moral conduct…and so on… an act of observance…and so on… previously…and so on… jhānas…and so on… the eye…and so on… the physical basis…and so on… the aggregates not to be abandoned by seeing; taking that as an object, lust to be abandoned by seeing arises, wrong view…and so on… doubt…and so on… grief to be abandoned by seeing arises. (2)

Adhipatipaccayo

Predominance Condition

16. Dassanena pahātabbo dhammo dassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dassanena pahātabbaṃ rāgaṃ garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā dassanena pahātabbo rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati, diṭṭhiṃ garuṃ katvā…pe…. Sahajātādhipati – dassanena pahātabbādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

16. A phenomenon to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a phenomenon to be abandoned by seeing by way of the Predominance Condition: object-predominance and conascence-predominance. Object-predominance: one regards the lust to be abandoned by seeing as important, savors it, and rejoices in it; making that important, the lust to be abandoned by seeing arises, wrong view arises; making wrong view important... Conascence-predominance: a predominance to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for its associated aggregates by way of the Predominance Condition. (1)

Dassanena pahātabbo dhammo nadassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – dassanena pahātabbādhipati cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a phenomenon not to be abandoned by seeing by way of the Predominance Condition. Conascence-predominance: a predominance to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for mind-originated material phenomena by way of the Predominance Condition. (2)

Dassanena pahātabbo dhammo [T 4.0340] dassanena pahātabbassa ca nadassanena pahātabbassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – dassanena pahātabbādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A phenomenon to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a phenomenon to be abandoned by seeing and for a phenomenon not to be abandoned by seeing by way of the Predominance Condition. Conascence-predominance: a predominance to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena by way of the Predominance Condition. (3)

17. Nadassanena pahātabbo dhammo nadassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ…pe… pubbe…pe… jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā jhānaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati, assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā nadassanena pahātabbo rāgo uppajjati, ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ garuṃ katvā…pe… phalassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo; cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ nadassanena pahātabbe khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā nadassanena pahātabbo rāgo uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – nadassanena pahātabbādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

17. A phenomenon not to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a phenomenon not to be abandoned by seeing by way of the Predominance Condition: object-predominance and conascence-predominance. Object-predominance: having given alms… observed virtue… performed the Uposatha… previously… having emerged from jhāna, one regards the jhāna as important, reviews it, savors it, and rejoices in it; making that important, the lust not to be abandoned by seeing arises. Having emerged from the noble path, one regards the path as important… this is a condition for the fruit by way of the Predominance Condition; the eye… the base… regarding the aggregates not to be abandoned by seeing as important, one savors and rejoices in them; making them important, the lust not to be abandoned by seeing arises. Conascence-predominance: a predominance not to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena by way of the Predominance Condition. (1)

Nadassanena [M 4.0045][V 4.0055] pahātabbo dhammo dassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ datvā…pe… jhānaṃ…pe… cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ nadassanena pahātabbe khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā dassanena pahātabbo rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. (2)

A phenomenon not to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a phenomenon to be abandoned by seeing by way of the Predominance Condition. Object-predominance: having given alms… jhāna… the eye… the base… regarding the aggregates not to be abandoned by seeing as important, one savors and rejoices in them. Making that important, the lust to be abandoned by seeing arises, and wrong view arises. (2)

Anantarapaccayo

Contiguity Condition

18. Dassanena pahātabbo dhammo dassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā dassanena pahātabbā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ dassanena pahātabbānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

18. A phenomenon to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a phenomenon to be abandoned by seeing by way of the Contiguity Condition. The earlier aggregates to be abandoned by seeing are a condition for the later aggregates to be abandoned by seeing by way of the Contiguity Condition. (1)

Dassanena pahātabbo dhammo nadassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo [T 4.0341] – dassanena pahātabbā khandhā vuṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Purimā purimā nadassanena pahātabbā khandhā…pe… phalasamāpattiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Āvajjanā dassanena pahātabbānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a phenomenon not to be abandoned by seeing by way of the Contiguity Condition: the aggregates to be abandoned by seeing are a condition for emergence by way of the Contiguity Condition. (The root should be supplied.) The earlier aggregates not to be abandoned by seeing… are a condition for fruition-attainment by way of the Contiguity Condition. (The root should be supplied.) Adverting is a condition for the aggregates to be abandoned by seeing by way of the Contiguity Condition. (2)

Samanantarapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… pañca… aññamaññapaccayena paccayo… dve… nissayapaccayena paccayo… satta.

By way of Immediate Contiguity Condition… by way of Conascence Condition… five… by way of Mutuality Condition… two… by way of Support Condition… seven.

Upanissayapaccayo

Decisive Support Condition

19. Dassanena pahātabbo dhammo dassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – dassanena pahātabbaṃ rāgaṃ upanissāya pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; dassanena pahātabbaṃ dosaṃ… mohaṃ… diṭṭhiṃ… patthanaṃ upanissāya pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; dassanena pahātabbo rāgo…pe… patthanā dassanena pahātabbassa rāgassa…pe… patthanāya upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

19. A phenomenon to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a phenomenon to be abandoned by seeing by way of the Decisive Support Condition: object-decisive support, contiguity-decisive support, natural decisive support… Natural decisive support: relying on the lust to be abandoned by seeing, one kills a living being… splits the Saṅgha; relying on the hatred… delusion… wrong view… longing to be abandoned by seeing, one kills a living being… splits the Saṅgha; the lust to be abandoned by seeing… longing is a condition for the lust… longing to be abandoned by seeing by way of the Decisive Support Condition. (1)

Dassanena pahātabbo dhammo nadassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo [V 4.0056] – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – dassanena pahātabbaṃ rāgaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti dassanena pahātabbaṃ dosaṃ… mohaṃ… diṭṭhiṃ… patthanaṃ upanissāya [M 4.0046] dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti; dassanena pahātabbo rāgo…pe… patthanā saddhāya…pe… paññāya nadassanena pahātabbassa rāgassa… dosassa… mohassa… mānassa [T 4.0342]… patthanāya… kāyikassa sukhassa…pe… phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a phenomenon not to be abandoned by seeing by way of the Decisive Support Condition: contiguity-decisive support, natural decisive support… Natural decisive support: relying on the lust to be abandoned by seeing, one gives alms… attains absorption; relying on the hatred… delusion… wrong view… longing to be abandoned by seeing, one gives alms… attains absorption; the lust to be abandoned by seeing… longing is a condition for faith… wisdom, for the lust… hatred… delusion… conceit… longing… bodily pleasure… and for fruition-attainment that are not to be abandoned by seeing, by way of the Decisive Support Condition. (2)

20. Nadassanena pahātabbo dhammo nadassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – saddhaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti, mānaṃ jappeti; sīlaṃ…pe… paññaṃ, nadassanena pahātabbaṃ rāgaṃ… dosaṃ… mohaṃ… mānaṃ… patthanaṃ… kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ…pe… senāsanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti, mānaṃ jappeti; saddhā…pe… paññā, nadassanena pahātabbo rāgo…pe… patthanā… kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ…pe… senāsanaṃ saddhāya…pe… paññāya nadassanena pahātabbassa rāgassa…pe… patthanāya… kāyikassa sukhassa… kāyikassa dukkhassa… maggassa, phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

20. A phenomenon not to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a phenomenon not to be abandoned by seeing by way of Decisive Support Condition: object-decisive support, contiguity-decisive support, natural decisive support…pe… Natural decisive support: relying on faith, one gives alms…pe… attains absorption, indulges in conceit; relying on virtue…pe… wisdom, lust… hatred… delusion… conceit… longing… bodily pleasure…pe… lodging not to be abandoned by seeing, one gives alms…pe… attains absorption, indulges in conceit. Faith…pe… wisdom, lust not to be abandoned by seeing…pe… longing… bodily pleasure…pe… lodging is a condition for faith…pe… wisdom, for lust not to be abandoned by seeing…pe… for longing… for bodily pleasure… for bodily pain… for the path, and for fruition-attainment by way of Decisive Support Condition. (2)

Nadassanena pahātabbo dhammo dassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – saddhaṃ upanissāya diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti; sīlaṃ…pe… paññaṃ upanissāya diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti, nadassanena pahātabbaṃ rāgaṃ… dosaṃ… mohaṃ… mānaṃ… patthanaṃ… kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ…pe… senāsanaṃ upanissāya pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; saddhā…pe… senāsanaṃ dassanena pahātabbassa rāgassa… dosassa… mohassa… diṭṭhiyā… patthanāya upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon not to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a phenomenon to be abandoned by seeing by way of Decisive Support Condition: object-decisive support, contiguity-decisive support, natural decisive support…pe… Natural decisive support: relying on faith, one grasps a wrong view; relying on virtue…pe… wisdom, one grasps a wrong view; relying on lust… hatred… delusion… conceit… longing… bodily pleasure…pe… lodging not to be abandoned by seeing, one kills a living being…pe… splits the Saṅgha. Faith…pe… lodging is a condition for lust… hatred… delusion… wrong view… longing to be abandoned by seeing by way of Decisive Support Condition. (2)

Purejātapaccayo

Pre-nascence Condition

21. Nadassanena pahātabbo dhammo nadassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa [T 4.0343] purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… vipassati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha nadassanena pahātabbo rāgo [V 4.0057]…pe… uddhaccaṃ…pe… nadassanena pahātabbaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati; dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti. Rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe…. Vatthupurejātaṃ – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa [M 4.0047] …pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… vatthu nadassanena pahātabbānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

21. A state not to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a state not to be abandoned by seeing by way of Pre-nascence Condition: object pre-nascence, base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: one contemplates the eye…pe… the physical base as impermanent…pe…; one delights in and rejoices at it. Taking it as object, lust…pe… restlessness…pe… grief not to be abandoned by seeing arises. With the divine eye one sees a form; with the divine ear-element one hears a sound. The form base is a condition for eye-consciousness…pe… the tangible base for body-consciousness…pe… Base pre-nascence: the eye base is a condition for eye-consciousness…pe… the body base for body-consciousness…pe… the physical base is a condition for the aggregates not to be abandoned by seeing by way of Pre-nascence Condition. (1)

Nadassanena pahātabbo dhammo dassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha dassanena pahātabbo rāgo…pe… diṭṭhi…pe… vicikicchā…pe… dassanena pahātabbaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati. Vatthupurejātaṃ – vatthu dassanena pahātabbānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state not to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a state to be abandoned by seeing by way of Pre-nascence Condition: object pre-nascence, base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: one relishes and delights in the eye…pe… the physical base; taking it as object, lust…pe… wrong views…pe… doubt…pe… grief to be abandoned by seeing arises. Base pre-nascence: the physical base is a condition for the aggregates to be abandoned by seeing by way of Pre-nascence Condition. (2)

Pacchājātāsevanapaccayā

Post-nascence and Repetition Conditions

22. Dassanena pahātabbo dhammo nadassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo (saṃkhittaṃ). (1)

22. A state to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a state not to be abandoned by seeing by way of Post-nascence Condition (in brief). (1)

Nadassanena pahātabbo dhammo nadassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo (saṃkhittaṃ)… āsevanapaccayena paccayo… dve.

A state not to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a state not to be abandoned by seeing by way of Post-nascence Condition (in brief)… by way of Repetition Condition… two.

Kammapaccayo

Kamma Condition

23. Dassanena pahātabbo dhammo dassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – dassanena pahātabbā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

23. A state to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a state to be abandoned by seeing by way of Kamma Condition: volition to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of Kamma Condition. (1)

Dassanena pahātabbo dhammo [T 4.0344] nadassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – dassanena pahātabbā cetanā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. Nānākkhaṇikā – dassanena pahātabbā cetanā vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a state not to be abandoned by seeing by way of Kamma Condition: co-nascent, different-moment. Co-nascent: volition to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for mind-originated materiality by way of Kamma Condition. Different-moment: volition to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for resultant aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality by way of Kamma Condition. (2)

Dassanena [V 4.0058] pahātabbo dhammo dassanena pahātabbassa ca nadassanena pahātabbassa ca dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – dassanena pahātabbā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a state to be abandoned by seeing and for a state not to be abandoned by seeing by way of Kamma Condition: volition to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by way of Kamma Condition. (3)

24. Nadassanena [M 4.0048] pahātabbo dhammo nadassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – nadassanena pahātabbā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Nānākkhaṇikā – nadassanena pahātabbā cetanā vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo.

24. A state not to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a state not to be abandoned by seeing by way of Kamma Condition: co-nascent, different-moment. Co-nascent: volition not to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for associated aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by way of Kamma Condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking…pe… Different-moment: volition not to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for resultant aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality by way of Kamma Condition.

Vipākapaccayādi

Resultant Condition, etc.

25. Nadassanena pahātabbo dhammo nadassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa vipākapaccayena paccayo… ekaṃ… āhārapaccayena paccayo… cattāri… indriyapaccayena paccayo… cattāri… jhānapaccayena paccayo… cattāri… maggapaccayena paccayo… cattāri… sampayuttapaccayena paccayo… dve.

25. A state not to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a state not to be abandoned by seeing by way of Resultant Condition… one… by way of Nutriment Condition… four… by way of Faculty Condition… four… by way of Jhāna Condition… four… by way of Path Condition… four… by way of Association Condition… two.

Vippayuttapaccayo

Dissociation Condition

26. Dassanena pahātabbo dhammo nadassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ). (1)

26. A state to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a state not to be abandoned by seeing by way of Dissociation Condition: co-nascent, post-nascent (in brief). (1)

Nadassanena [T 4.0345] pahātabbo dhammo nadassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ).

A state not to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a state not to be abandoned by seeing by way of Dissociation Condition: co-nascent, pre-nascent, post-nascent (in brief).

Nadassanena pahātabbo dhammo dassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – vatthu dassanena pahātabbānaṃ khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state not to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a state to be abandoned by seeing by way of Dissociation Condition. Pre-nascent: the base is a condition for the aggregates to be abandoned by seeing by way of Dissociation Condition. (2)

Atthipaccayādi

Presence Condition, and so on.

27. Dassanena [V 4.0059] pahātabbo dhammo dassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo (paṭiccasadisaṃ). Dassanena pahātabbo dhammo nadassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ). Dassanena pahātabbo dhammo dassanena pahātabbassa ca nadassanena pahātabbassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo (paṭiccavārasadisā). (3)

27. A state to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a state to be abandoned by seeing by way of Presence Condition (similar to the Dependent section). A state to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a state not to be abandoned by seeing by way of Presence Condition—co-nascence, post-nascence (in brief). A state to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a state to be abandoned by seeing and for a state not to be abandoned by seeing by way of Presence Condition (similar to the Dependent section). (3)

Nadassanena [M 4.0049] pahātabbo dhammo nadassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ). Nadassanena pahātabbo dhammo dassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… (saṃkhittaṃ, purejātasadisaṃ). (2)

A state not to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a state not to be abandoned by seeing by way of Presence Condition—co-nascence, pre-nascence, post-nascence, nutriment, faculty (in brief). A state not to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a state to be abandoned by seeing by way of Presence Condition. Pre-nascence: the eye…pe… (in brief, similar to the pre-nascence section). (2)

28. Dassanena pahātabbo ca nadassanena pahātabbo ca dhammā dassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – dassanena pahātabbo eko khandho ca vatthu ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca…pe…. (1)

28. Both a state to be abandoned by seeing and a state not to be abandoned by seeing are conditions for a state to be abandoned by seeing by way of Presence Condition—co-nascence, pre-nascence. Co-nascence: one aggregate to be abandoned by seeing and the base are conditions for the three aggregates by way of Presence Condition…pe… two aggregates…pe…. (1)

Dassanena pahātabbo ca nadassanena pahātabbo ca dhammā nadassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ[T 4.0346], indriyaṃ. Sahajātā – dassanena pahātabbā khandhā ca mahābhūtā ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – dassanena pahātabbā khandhā ca kabaḷīkāro āhāro ca imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – dassanena pahātabbā khandhā ca rūpajīvitindriyañca kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

Both a state to be abandoned by seeing and a state not to be abandoned by seeing are conditions for a state not to be abandoned by seeing by way of Presence Condition—co-nascence, post-nascence, nutriment, faculty. Co-nascence: the aggregates to be abandoned by seeing and the great elements are conditions for mind-originated materiality by way of Presence Condition. Post-nascence: the aggregates to be abandoned by seeing and physical nutriment are conditions for this body by way of Presence Condition. Post-nascence: the aggregates to be abandoned by seeing and the material life faculty are conditions for kamma-produced materiality by way of Presence Condition. (2)

Natthipaccayena paccayo, vigatapaccayena paccayo, avigatapaccayena paccayo.

Absence Condition, Disappearance Condition, Non-disappearance Condition.

Dassanena pahātabbo ca nadassanena pahātabbo ca dhammā dassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. (1)

35. Bhāvanāya [V 4.0062] pahātabbaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca bhāvanāya pahātabbo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā (yathā dassanadukaṃ, evaṃ vitthāretabbaṃ, ninnānākaraṇaṃ).

35. Depending on a phenomenon to be abandoned by cultivation, a phenomenon to be abandoned by cultivation arises by way of root condition (as with the Dyad of What is to be Abandoned by Seeing, so it should be elaborated, there being no difference in the method).

Hetuyā pañca…pe… avigate pañca.

By way of root condition: five... in non-disappearance condition: five.

Anulomaṃ.

The Direct Order.

Bhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca bhāvanāya pahātabbo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – uddhaccasahagate khandhe paṭicca uddhaccasahagato moho.

Depending on a phenomenon to be abandoned by cultivation, a phenomenon to be abandoned by cultivation arises by way of non-root condition: depending on the aggregates accompanied by restlessness, delusion accompanied by restlessness arises.

Nabhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nabhāvanāya pahātabbo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ nabhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ…pe… (yāva asaññasattā) vicikicchāsahagate khandhe paṭicca vicikicchāsahagato moho (saṃkhittaṃ).

Depending on a phenomenon not to be abandoned by cultivation, a phenomenon not to be abandoned by cultivation arises by way of non-root condition: one rootless aggregate not to be abandoned by cultivation... (up to non-percipient beings); depending on the aggregates accompanied by doubt, delusion accompanied by doubt arises (abbreviated).

Nahetuyā [T 4.0349] dve…pe… novigate tīṇi.

By way of non-root condition: two... in disappearance condition: three.

Paccanīyaṃ.

The Negative.

(Paccayavārapaccanīye [M 4.0052] nahetupaccaye uddhaccasahagate tīṇi, moho uddharitabbo. Sabbepi vārā dassanadukasadisā, uddhaccapaccanīyampi nānaṃ.)

(In the Negative of the Conditional Relations Section, under non-root condition, in the case of states accompanied by restlessness, there are three; delusion is to be excluded. All sections are similar to the Dyad of Seeing, and the negative case for restlessness is also different.)

Hetupaccayo

The Root Condition

36. Bhāvanāya [V 4.0063] pahātabbo dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – bhāvanāya pahātabbā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo… tīṇi.

36. A phenomenon to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for a phenomenon to be abandoned by cultivation by way of root condition. The roots to be abandoned by cultivation are conditions for the associated aggregates by way of root condition... three.

Nabhāvanāya pahātabbo dhammo nabhāvanāya pahātabbassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo (saṃkhittaṃ). (1)

A phenomenon not to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for a phenomenon not to be abandoned by cultivation by way of root condition (abbreviated). (1)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

The Object Condition

37. Bhāvanāya pahātabbo dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – bhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ rāgaṃ assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha bhāvanāya pahātabbo rāgo uppajjati, uddhaccaṃ uppajjati; bhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati; uddhaccaṃ ārabbha uddhaccaṃ uppajjati, bhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati; bhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ domanassaṃ ārabbha bhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati, uddhaccaṃ uppajjati. (1)

37. A phenomenon to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for a phenomenon to be abandoned by cultivation by way of object condition—one relishes and delights in lust to be abandoned by cultivation; taking that as object, lust to be abandoned by cultivation arises, restlessness arises, and sorrow to be abandoned by cultivation arises; taking restlessness as object, restlessness arises, and sorrow to be abandoned by cultivation arises; taking sorrow to be abandoned by cultivation as object, sorrow to be abandoned by cultivation arises, and restlessness arises. (1)

Bhāvanāya pahātabbo dhammo nabhāvanāya pahātabbassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – ariyā bhāvanāya pahātabbe pahīne kilese…pe… vikkhambhite kilese…pe… pubbe samudāciṇṇe…pe… bhāvanāya pahātabbe khandhe aniccato…pe… vipassati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha nabhāvanāya pahātabbo rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi…pe… vicikicchā…pe… nabhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati; cetopariyañāṇena [T 4.0350] bhāvanāya pahātabbacittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānāti, bhāvanāya pahātabbā khandhā cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa[V 4.0064], yathākammūpagañāṇassa[M 4.0053], anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for a phenomenon not to be abandoned by cultivation by way of object condition—noble ones review the defilements to be abandoned by cultivation as abandoned… as suppressed… as previously practiced… they see with insight the aggregates to be abandoned by cultivation as impermanent… and relish and delight in that; taking that as object, lust not to be abandoned by cultivation arises, wrong view… doubt… sorrow not to be abandoned by cultivation arises; with knowledge encompassing the minds of others, one knows the mind of a person endowed with a mind-state to be abandoned by cultivation; the aggregates to be abandoned by cultivation are a condition for knowledge encompassing the minds of others, for the knowledge of the recollection of past lives, for the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings according to their actions, for the knowledge of the future, and for adverting, by way of object condition. (2)

38. Nabhāvanāya pahātabbo dhammo nabhāvanāya pahātabbassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ paccavekkhati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha nabhāvanāya pahātabbo rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi…pe… vicikicchā…pe… nabhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati, pubbe…pe… jhānā…pe… ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā…pe… phalassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo; ariyā nabhāvanāya pahātabbe pahīne kilese…pe… cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ nabhāvanāya pahātabbe khandhe aniccato…pe… vipassati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha nabhāvanāya pahātabbo rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi…pe… vicikicchā…pe… nabhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati; dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati…pe… yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

38. A phenomenon not to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for a phenomenon not to be abandoned by cultivation by way of object condition—after giving a gift… undertaking the precepts… performing the observance-day act, one reviews, relishes, and delights in it; taking that as object, lust not to be abandoned by cultivation arises, wrong view… doubt… sorrow not to be abandoned by cultivation arises; previously… jhānas… noble ones having emerged from the noble paths review the path… fruition is a condition for adverting by way of object condition; noble ones review the defilements not to be abandoned by cultivation that have been abandoned… the eye… the physical base… they see the aggregates not to be abandoned by cultivation as impermanent… and relish and delight in them; taking them as object, lust not to be abandoned by cultivation arises, wrong view… doubt… sorrow not to be abandoned by cultivation arises; with the divine eye, one sees form… knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings according to their actions, knowledge of the future, and adverting are conditioned by way of object condition. (1)

Nabhāvanāya pahātabbo dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… jhānaṃ…pe… cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ nabhāvanāya pahātabbe khandhe assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha bhāvanāya pahātabbo rāgo uppajjati, uddhaccaṃ uppajjati, bhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati. (2)

A phenomenon not to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for a phenomenon to be abandoned by cultivation by way of object condition—one relishes and delights in a gift… virtue… jhāna… the eye… the physical base… the aggregates not to be abandoned by cultivation; taking that as object, lust to be abandoned by cultivation arises, restlessness arises, and sorrow to be abandoned by cultivation arises. (2)

Adhipatipaccayo

The Dominance Condition

39. Bhāvanāya pahātabbo dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena [T 4.0351] paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – bhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ rāgaṃ garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā bhāvanāya pahātabbo rāgo uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – bhāvanāya pahātabbādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

39. A phenomenon to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for a phenomenon to be abandoned by cultivation by way of dominance condition: object-dominance and conascence-dominance. Object-dominance: regarding as important the lust to be abandoned by cultivation, one savors it and delights in it; regarding that as important, lust to be abandoned by cultivation arises. Conascence-dominance: a dominant factor to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of dominance condition. (1)

Bhāvanāya pahātabbo dhammo nabhāvanāya pahātabbassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati[V 4.0065], sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – bhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ rāgaṃ garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā nabhāvanāya pahātabbo rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi [M 4.0054] uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – bhāvanāya pahātabbādhipati cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for a state not to be abandoned by cultivation by way of the dominant condition: dominance of object, dominance of conascence. Dominance of object: regarding as important the lust to be abandoned by cultivation, one savors it and delights in it; regarding that as important, the lust not to be abandoned by cultivation arises, and wrong view arises. Dominance of conascence: the dominance of a state to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for mind-originated material forms by way of the dominant condition. (2)

Bhāvanāya pahātabbo dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbassa ca nabhāvanāya pahātabbassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – bhāvanāya pahātabbādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition by way of the dominant condition for a state to be abandoned by cultivation and for a state not to be abandoned by cultivation. Dominance of conascence: The dominance of a state to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition by way of the dominant condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated material forms. (3)

40. Nabhāvanāya pahātabbo dhammo nabhāvanāya pahātabbassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā nabhāvanāya pahātabbo rāgo uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – nabhāvanāya pahātabbādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

40. A state not to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for a state not to be abandoned by cultivation by way of the dominant condition: dominance of object and dominance of conascence. Dominance of object: having given alms, observed morality... performed the Uposatha observance, one reviews it, regards it as important, savors it, and delights in it; regarding it as important, the lust not to be abandoned by cultivation arises. Dominance of conascence: The dominance of a state not to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for the associated aggregates and mind-originated material forms by way of the dominant condition. (1)

Nabhāvanāya pahātabbo dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbassa [T 4.0352] dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ…pe… jhānaṃ…pe… cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ nabhāvanāya pahātabbe khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā bhāvanāya pahātabbo rāgo uppajjati. (2)

A state not to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for a state to be abandoned by cultivation by way of the dominant condition. Dominance of object: Giving... jhāna... the eye... the base, regarding as important the aggregates not to be abandoned by cultivation, one savors them and delights in them; regarding that as important, the lust to be abandoned by cultivation arises. (2)

Anantarapaccayādi

Contiguity Condition, etc.

41. Bhāvanāya pahātabbo dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo… cattāri (dassanadukasadisā bhāvanā ninnānākaraṇā)… samanantarapaccayena paccayo… cattāri… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… pañca… aññamaññapaccayena paccayo… dve… nissayapaccayena paccayo… satta.

41. A state to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for a state to be abandoned by cultivation by way of the contiguity condition... four (similar to the dyad on seeing, with cultivation as the differentiating factor)... by way of the unbroken contiguity condition... four... by way of the conascence condition... five... by way of the mutuality condition... two... by way of the support condition... seven.

Upanissayapaccayo

Decisive Support Condition

42. Bhāvanāya [V 4.0066] pahātabbo dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – bhāvanāya pahātabbo rāgo… doso… moho… māno… patthanā bhāvanāya pahātabbassa rāgassa [M 4.0055]… dosassa… mohassa… mānassa… patthanāya upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

42. A state to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for a state to be abandoned by cultivation by way of the decisive support condition: decisive support by way of object, decisive support by way of contiguity, decisive support by way of nature... Decisive support by way of nature: the lust to be abandoned by cultivation... hatred... delusion... conceit... aspiration is a condition for the lust... hatred... delusion... conceit... aspiration to be abandoned by cultivation by way of the decisive support condition. (1)

Bhāvanāya pahātabbo dhammo nabhāvanāya pahātabbassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – bhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ rāgaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti, pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; bhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ dosaṃ… mohaṃ… mānaṃ… patthanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti, pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; bhāvanāya pahātabbo rāgo…pe… patthanā saddhāya…pe… paññāya [T 4.0353] nabhāvanāya pahātabbassa, rāgassa… dosassa… mohassa… diṭṭhiyā… patthanāya… kāyikassa sukhassa… kāyikassa dukkhassa… maggassa… phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for a state not to be abandoned by cultivation by way of the decisive support condition: decisive support by way of object, decisive support by way of contiguity, decisive support by way of nature... Decisive support by way of nature: relying on the lust to be abandoned by cultivation, one gives alms... attains absorption... kills a living being... splits the Sangha; relying on the hatred to be abandoned by cultivation... delusion... conceit... aspiration, one gives alms... attains absorption... kills a living being... splits the Sangha; the lust to be abandoned by cultivation... aspiration is a condition for faith... wisdom (which are states not to be abandoned by cultivation), for lust... hatred... delusion... wrong view... aspiration... bodily pleasure... bodily pain... the path... fruition-attainment by way of the decisive support condition. (2)

43. Nabhāvanāya pahātabbo dhammo nabhāvanāya pahātabbassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – saddhaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti, diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti; sīlaṃ…pe… paññaṃ, nabhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ rāgaṃ… dosaṃ… mohaṃ… diṭṭhiṃ… patthanaṃ… kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ… kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ…pe… senāsanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti, pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; saddhā…pe… senāsanaṃ saddhāya…pe… paññāya nabhāvanāya pahātabbassa rāgassa… dosassa… mohassa… diṭṭhiyā… patthanāya… kāyikassa sukhassa… kāyikassa dukkhassa… maggassa… phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

43. A state not to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for a state not to be abandoned by cultivation by way of the decisive support condition: decisive support by way of object, decisive support by way of contiguity, decisive support by way of nature... Decisive support by way of nature: relying on faith, one gives alms... attains absorption, grasps a view; relying on virtue... wisdom, lust not to be abandoned by cultivation... hatred... delusion... wrong view... aspiration... bodily pleasure... bodily pain... lodging, one gives alms... attains absorption... kills a living being... splits the Sangha; faith... lodging is a condition for faith... wisdom, for lust not to be abandoned by cultivation... hatred... delusion... wrong view... aspiration... bodily pleasure... bodily pain... the path... fruition-attainment by way of the decisive support condition. (1)

Nabhāvanāya pahātabbo dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo[V 4.0067], anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – saddhaṃ upanissāya mānaṃ jappeti…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… paññaṃ… rāgaṃ…pe… kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ… kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ… senāsanaṃ upanissāya mānaṃ jappeti; saddhā…pe… senāsanaṃ bhāvanāya pahātabbassa rāgassa… dosassa… mohassa… mānassa… patthanāya upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state not to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for a state to be abandoned by cultivation by way of the decisive support condition: decisive support by way of object, decisive support by way of contiguity, decisive support by way of nature... Decisive support by way of nature: relying on faith, one indulges in conceit... virtue... wisdom... lust... bodily pleasure... bodily pain... lodging, one indulges in conceit; faith... lodging is a condition for the lust, hatred, delusion, conceit, and aspiration to be abandoned by cultivation by way of the decisive support condition. (2)

Purejātapaccayādi

Pre-nascence Condition, etc.

44. Nabhāvanāya [M 4.0056] pahātabbo dhammo nabhāvanāya pahātabbassa dhammassa [T 4.0354] purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… vipassati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha nabhāvanāya pahātabbo rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati, vicikicchā uppajjati; nabhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati, dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe…. Vatthupurejātaṃ – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… vatthu nabhāvanāya pahātabbānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

44. A state not to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for a state not to be abandoned by cultivation by way of pre-nascence condition—object pre-nascence, base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: one contemplates the eye… and so on… the physical base as impermanent… and so on… relishes, delights in it; taking that as object, lust not to be abandoned by cultivation arises, wrong view arises, doubt arises; displeasure not to be abandoned by cultivation arises; with the divine eye, one sees a form… and so on… the tangible base for body-consciousness… and so on. Base pre-nascence: the eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness… and so on… the body-base is a condition for body-consciousness… and so on… the physical base is a condition for the aggregates not to be abandoned by cultivation by way of pre-nascence condition. (1)

Nabhāvanāya pahātabbo dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha bhāvanāya pahātabbo rāgo uppajjati, uddhaccaṃ uppajjati, bhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati. Vatthupurejātaṃ – vatthu bhāvanāya pahātabbānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state not to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for a state to be abandoned by cultivation by way of pre-nascence condition—object pre-nascence, base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: one relishes and delights in the eye… and so on… the physical base; taking that as object, lust to be abandoned by cultivation arises, restlessness arises, and displeasure to be abandoned by cultivation arises. Base pre-nascence: the physical base is a condition for the aggregates to be abandoned by cultivation by way of pre-nascence condition. (2)

45. Pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… dve, āsevanapaccayena paccayo… dve, kammapaccayena paccayo – bhāvanāya pahātabbā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Bhāvanāya pahātabbā cetanā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Bhāvanāya pahātabbā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (3)

45. By way of post-nascence condition… two; by way of repetition condition… two; by way of kamma condition: volition to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of kamma condition. (The root is to be done.) Volition to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for mind-originated materiality by way of kamma condition. (The root is to be done.) Volition to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for the associated aggregates and mind-originated materiality by way of kamma condition. (3)

Nabhāvanāya [V 4.0068] pahātabbo [T 4.0355] dhammo nabhāvanāya pahātabbassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – nabhāvanāya pahātabbā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Nānākkhaṇikā – nabhāvanāya pahātabbā cetanā vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo… vipākapaccayena paccayo… ekaṃ…pe… avigatapaccayena paccayo. (Sabbapaccayā dassanadukasadisā, bhāvanā ninnānākaraṇā.)

A state not to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for a state not to be abandoned by cultivation by way of kamma condition—conascent and different-moment. Conascent: volition not to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for the associated aggregates and mind-originated materiality by way of kamma condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking… and so on. Different-moment: volition not to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for the resultant aggregates and kamma-produced materiality by way of kamma condition… by way of result condition… one… and so on… by way of non-disappearance condition. (All conditions are similar to the dyad on seeing, with cultivation being the differentiating factor.)

1. Paccayānulomaṃ

1. Positive Application

2. Saṅkhyāvāro

2. Enumeration Chapter

Suddhaṃ

Unmixed

46. Hetuyā [M 4.0057] cattāri, ārammaṇe cattāri, adhipatiyā pañca, anantare cattāri, samanantare cattāri, sahajāte pañca, aññamaññe dve, nissaye satta, upanissaye cattāri, purejāte dve, pacchājāte dve, āsevane dve, kamme cattāri, vipāke ekaṃ, āhāre cattāri, indriye cattāri, jhāne cattāri, magge cattāri, sampayutte dve, vippayutte tīṇi, atthiyā satta, natthiyā cattāri, vigate cattāri, avigate satta.

46. In root condition, four; in object condition, four; in predominance condition, five; in contiguity condition, four; in immediate proximity condition, four; in conascence condition, five; in reciprocity condition, two; in support condition, seven; in strong dependence condition, four; in pre-nascence condition, two; in post-nascence condition, two; in repetition condition, two; in kamma condition, four; in result condition, one; in nutriment condition, four; in faculty condition, four; in jhāna condition, four; in path condition, four; in association condition, two; in dissociation condition, three; in presence condition, seven; in absence condition, four; in disappearance condition, four; in non-disappearance condition, seven.

(Paccanīyavibhaṅgo dassanadukasadiso vibhajitabbo. Evaṃ tīṇi gaṇanāpi gaṇetabbā.)

(The negative analysis should be analyzed similarly to the dyad on seeing. Thus, the three enumerations should also be counted.)

Bhāvanāyapahātabbadukaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Dyad on States to be Abandoned by Cultivation is concluded.

85. Dassanenapahātabbahetukadukaṃ

85. The Dyad on States with a Root to be Abandoned by Seeing
