90. Nahetuyā nava, naārammaṇe nava (sabbattha nava), noavigate nava.

90. In the no-root condition: nine; in the no-object condition: nine (nine everywhere); in the no-non-disappearance condition: nine.

3. Paccayānulomapaccanīyaṃ

3. The Affirmative-Negative Order of Conditions

91. Hetupaccayā [M 4.0076] naārammaṇe cha, naadhipatiyā cha, naanantare cha, nasamanantare cha, naaññamaññe dve, naupanissaye cha…pe… nasampayutte dve, navippayutte tīṇi, nonatthiyā cha, novigate cha.

91. By way of the root condition, in the no-object condition: six; in the no-dominance condition: six; in the no-contiguity condition: six; in the no-immediate contiguity condition: six; in the no-mutuality condition: two; in the no-decisive support condition: six… etc.… in the no-association condition: two; in the no-dissociation condition: three; in the no-absence condition: six; in the no-disappearance condition: six.

4. Paccayapaccanīyānulomaṃ

4. The Negative-Affirmative Order of Conditions

92. Nahetupaccayā ārammaṇe nava, adhipatiyā pañca (anulomamātikā)…pe… avigate nava.

92. By way of no-root condition, in the object condition: nine; in the dominance condition: five (as in the affirmative matrix)… etc.… in the non-disappearance condition: nine.

Dassanenapahātabbahetukadukaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Dyad of Roots to be Abandoned by Seeing is concluded.

86. Bhāvanāyapahātabbahetukadukaṃ

86. The Dyad of Roots to be Abandoned by Development

1-6. Paṭiccavārādi

1-6. The Dependence Section, etc.

93. Bhāvanāya [V 4.0090] pahātabbahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe….

93. A phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by development arises dependent on a phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by development by way of the root condition. Dependent on one aggregate with a root to be abandoned by development, three aggregates arise… etc.… dependent on two aggregates… etc.

2-6. Sahajāta-paccaya-nissaya-saṃsaṭṭha-sampayuttavāro

2-6. The Co-nascence, Condition, Dependence, Association, and Concomitance Sections.

(Evaṃ paṭiccavāropi sahajātavāropi paccayavāropi nissayavāropi saṃsaṭṭhavāropi sampayuttavāropi dassanena pahātabbahetukadukasadisā. Uddhaccasahagato moho vicikicchāsahagatamohaṭṭhāne ṭhapetabbo.)

(Thus, the sections on dependence, co-nascence, condition, support, association, and concomitance are similar to the dyad of roots to be abandoned by seeing. The delusion accompanied by restlessness should be placed in the position of delusion accompanied by doubt.)

7. Pañhāvāro

7. Question Section

1. Paccayānulomaṃ

1. The Analysis of Conditions in Forward Order

1. Vibhaṅgavāro

1. The Chapter on Distinctions

Hetupaccayo

The Root Condition

94. Bhāvanāya [T 4.0379] pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo… cha…pe… (dassanena pahātabbahetukadukasadisā).

94. A phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by development is a condition for a phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by development by way of the root condition… six… etc. (similar to the dyad of roots to be abandoned by seeing).

Ārammaṇapaccayo

The Object Condition

95. Bhāvanāya [M 4.0077] pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi (ārabbha dassanena pahātabbahetukadukasadisā).

95. A phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by development is a condition for a phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by development by way of the object condition… three (similar to the dyad of roots to be abandoned by seeing).

96. Nabhāvanāya [V 4.0091] pahātabbahetuko dhammo nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ paccavekkhati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi…pe… vicikicchā…pe… nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati, pubbe suciṇṇāni…pe… jhānā…pe… ariyā maggā…pe… phalassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo; ariyā nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuke pahīne kilese…pe… pubbe samudāciṇṇe…pe… cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuke khandhe ca mohañca aniccato…pe… vipassati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi…pe… vicikicchā…pe… nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati; dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati…pe… anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya, mohassa ca ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

96. A state whose root is not to be abandoned by development is a condition for a state whose root is not to be abandoned by development by way of object condition. Having performed acts of generosity... morality... observance of the Uposatha, one reflects upon it, savors it, and delights in it. Taking that as an object, lust whose root is not to be abandoned by development arises; wrong view... doubt... grief whose root is not to be abandoned by development arises. Previously performed wholesome deeds... meditative absorptions... noble paths... are a condition for fruition, for adverting, by way of object condition. Noble ones reflect on, savor, and delight in defilements whose roots are not to be abandoned by development that have been abandoned... in previously accumulated deeds... they see the eye... the base, the aggregates whose roots are not to be abandoned by development, and delusion as impermanent... Taking that as an object, lust whose root is not to be abandoned by development arises; wrong view... doubt... grief whose root is not to be abandoned by development arises. One sees a form with the divine eye... this is a condition for knowledge of the future, for adverting, and for delusion by way of object condition. (1)

Nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo [T 4.0380] – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… jhānaṃ…pe… cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuke khandhe ca mohañca assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko rāgo uppajjati, uddhaccaṃ…pe… bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati. (2)

A state whose root is not to be abandoned by development is a condition for a state whose root is to be abandoned by development by way of object condition. One savors and delights in generosity... morality... meditative absorption... the eye... the base, the aggregates whose roots are not to be abandoned by development, and delusion. Taking that as an object, lust whose root is to be abandoned by development arises; restlessness... grief whose root is to be abandoned by development arises. (2)

Nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuke khandhe ca mohañca ārabbha uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho ca uppajjanti (ghaṭanārammaṇā tīṇipi kātabbā). (3)

A state whose root is not to be abandoned by development is a condition for a state whose root is to be abandoned by development and for a state whose root is not to be abandoned by development by way of object condition. Taking the eye... the base, the aggregates whose roots are not to be abandoned by development, and delusion as an object, aggregates accompanied by restlessness and delusion arise (three types of object-connection should be made). (3)

Adhipatipaccayādi

Dominance condition, and so on.

97. Bhāvanāya [M 4.0078] pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukaṃ rāgaṃ garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko [V 4.0092] rāgo uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

97. A state whose root is to be abandoned by development is a condition for a state whose root is to be abandoned by development by way of dominance condition: object-dominance, co-nascence dominance. Object-dominance: having made much of lust whose root is to be abandoned by development, one savors and delights in it; having made much of that, lust whose root is to be abandoned by development arises. Co-nascence dominance: the dominant state whose root is to be abandoned by development is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of dominance condition. (1)

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukaṃ rāgaṃ garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukādhipati cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ [T 4.0381] rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state whose root is to be abandoned by development is a condition for a state whose root is not to be abandoned by development by way of dominance condition: object-dominance, co-nascence dominance. Object-dominance: having made much of lust whose root is to be abandoned by development, one savors and delights in it; having made much of that, lust whose root is not to be abandoned by development arises, wrong view arises. Co-nascence dominance: the dominant state whose root is to be abandoned by development is a condition for mind-originated matter by way of dominance condition. (2)

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state whose root is to be abandoned by development is a condition for a state whose root is to be abandoned by development and for a state whose root is not to be abandoned by development by way of dominance condition. Co-nascence dominance: the dominant state whose root is to be abandoned by development is a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter by way of dominance condition. (3)

98. Nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati, pubbe…pe… jhānā…pe… ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā…pe… phalassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo; cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuke khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

98. A state whose root is not to be abandoned by development is a condition for a state whose root is not to be abandoned by development by way of dominance condition: object-dominance, co-nascence dominance. Object-dominance: having performed acts of generosity... morality... observance of the Uposatha, one makes it paramount and reflects upon it, savors it, and delights in it; having made that paramount, lust whose root is not to be abandoned by development arises, wrong view arises. Formerly... meditative absorptions... having emerged from the noble paths... this is a condition for fruition by way of dominance condition. One makes the eye... the base, the aggregates whose roots are not to be abandoned by development paramount, and savors and delights in them; having made that paramount, lust whose root is not to be abandoned by development arises, wrong view arises. Co-nascence dominance: the dominant state whose root is not to be abandoned by development is a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter by way of dominance condition. (1)

Nabhāvanāya [M 4.0079] pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ…pe… jhānaṃ…pe… cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuke khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko rāgo uppajjati. (2)

A state whose root is not to be abandoned by development is a condition for a state whose root is to be abandoned by development by way of dominance condition—object-dominance: Having made generosity... meditative absorption... the eye... the base, the aggregates whose roots are not to be abandoned by development paramount, one savors and delights in them; having made that paramount, lust whose root is to be abandoned by development arises. (2)

(Anantarapaccaye [T 4.0382][V 4.0093] nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukakāraṇā vicikicchāsahagato moho na kātabbo, uddhaccasahagato moho kātabbo.) Samanantarapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… nava… aññamaññapaccayena paccayo… cha… nissayapaccayena paccayo… nava.

(In the proximity condition, delusion accompanied by doubt, which has a root not to be abandoned by development, should not be included, but delusion accompanied by restlessness should be included.) It is a condition by way of contiguity condition... by way of co-nascence condition... nine... by way of mutuality condition... six... by way of dependence condition... nine.

Upanissayapaccayo

Decisive support condition.

99. Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā khandhā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā khandhā nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca upanissayapaccayena paccayo; sakabhaṇḍe chandarāgo parabhaṇḍe chandarāgassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo; sakapariggahe chandarāgo parapariggahe chandarāgassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā khandhā uddhaccasahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (3)

99. A state whose root is to be abandoned by development is a condition for a state whose root is to be abandoned by development by way of decisive-support condition: object decisive support, immediately contiguous decisive support, natural decisive support… and so on. Natural decisive support: the aggregates whose root is to be abandoned by development are a condition for the aggregates whose root is to be abandoned by development by way of decisive-support condition. (The root should be applied.) The aggregates whose root is to be abandoned by development are a condition for the aggregates whose root is not to be abandoned by development and for delusion by way of decisive-support condition; desire-passion for one's own property is a condition for desire-passion for others' property by way of decisive-support condition; desire-passion for one's own acquisitions is a condition for desire-passion for others' acquisitions by way of decisive-support condition. (The root should be applied.) The aggregates whose root is to be abandoned by development are a condition for the aggregates accompanied by agitation and for delusion by way of decisive-support condition. (3)

100. Nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – saddhaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti, diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti; sīlaṃ…pe… paññaṃ… nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukaṃ rāgaṃ… dosaṃ… mohaṃ… diṭṭhiṃ… patthanaṃ… kāyikaṃ [T 4.0383] sukhaṃ… kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ…pe… senāsanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; saddhā…pe… senāsanaṃ saddhāya…pe… paññāya… nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa rāgassa [M 4.0080]… dosassa… mohassa… diṭṭhiyā… patthanāya… kāyikassa sukhassa…pe… phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

100. A state whose root is not to be abandoned by development is a condition for a state whose root is not to be abandoned by development by way of decisive-support condition: object decisive support, immediately contiguous decisive support, natural decisive support… and so on. Natural decisive support: relying on faith, one gives alms… and so on… attains meditative absorption, adopts a view; virtue… and so on… wisdom… lust whose root is not to be abandoned by development… hatred… delusion… view… longing… bodily pleasure… bodily pain… and so on. Relying on lodging, one gives alms… and so on… kills a living being… and so on… splits the Saṅgha. Faith… and so on… lodging… are a condition for faith… and so on… wisdom… lust whose root is not to be abandoned by development… hatred… delusion… view… longing… bodily pleasure… and so on… fruition-attainment by way of decisive-support condition. (1)

Nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – saddhaṃ upanissāya mānaṃ jappeti…pe… saddhā [V 4.0094]…pe… senāsanaṃ bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa rāgassa… dosassa… mohassa… mānassa… patthanāya upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state whose root is not to be abandoned by development is a condition for a state whose root is to be abandoned by development by way of decisive-support condition: object decisive support, immediately contiguous decisive support, natural decisive support… and so on. Natural decisive support: relying on faith, one harbors pride… and so on. Faith… and so on… lodging… are a condition for lust… hatred… delusion… pride… and aspiration whose root is to be abandoned by development by way of decisive-support condition. (2)

Nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – saddhā…pe… paññā… kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ…pe… senāsanaṃ uddhaccasahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca upanissayapaccayena paccayo (ghaṭanūpanissayāpi tīṇipi kātabbā). (3)

A state whose root is not to be abandoned by development is a condition for a state whose root is to be abandoned by development and a state whose root is not to be abandoned by development by way of decisive-support condition: object decisive support, immediately contiguous decisive support, natural decisive support… and so on. Natural decisive support: faith… and so on… wisdom… bodily pleasure… and so on… lodging… are a condition for the aggregates accompanied by agitation and for delusion by way of decisive-support condition (the three decisive supports should also be applied). (3)

Purejātapaccayādi

Pre-Nascence Condition, and so forth.

101. Nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi… āsevanapaccayena paccayo… nava… kammapaccayena paccayo (nabhāvanāya pahātabbabhājanakāraṇe nānākkhaṇikā labbhati [T 4.0384]) …pe… novigatapaccayena paccayo. (Saṃkhittaṃ. Yathā dassanena pahātabbahetukadukaṃ evaṃ bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukapaccayāpi paccanīyāpi vibhāgopi gaṇanāpi ninnānākaraṇā.)

101. A state whose root is not to be abandoned by development is a condition for a state whose root is not to be abandoned by development by way of pre-nascence condition… three items… by way of post-nascence condition… three items… by way of repetition condition… nine items… by way of kamma condition (in the case of states whose roots are not to be abandoned by development, diverse-moment kamma is obtained)… and so on… by way of non-disappearance condition. (In brief. Just as with the dyad of roots to be abandoned by seeing, so also the conditions, counter-conditions, analysis, enumeration, and non-differentiation should be understood for the roots to be abandoned by development.)

Nadassanena pahātabbo dhammo nadassanena pahātabbassa dhammassa…pe…. (Parantena sakabhaṇḍachandarāgopi kātabbo.)

A state not to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a state not to be abandoned by seeing… and so on. (At the end, desire-passion for one's own property should also be applied.)

Bhāvanāya pahātabbo dhammo nabhāvanāya pahātabbassa dhammassa…pe…. (Parantena “sakabhaṇḍachandarāgo”ti kātabbaṃ.)

A state to be abandoned by development is a condition for a state not to be abandoned by development… and so on. (At the end, 'desire-passion for one's own property' should be applied.)

Bhāvanāyapahātabbahetukadukaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Dyad of Roots to be Abandoned by Development is concluded.

87. Savitakkadukaṃ

87. The Dyad of Initial Thought

1. Paṭiccavāro

1. The Section on Conditions

1. Paccayānulomaṃ

1. The Forward Order of Conditions

1. Vibhaṅgavāro

1. The Section on Analysis

Hetupaccayo

The Root Condition

102. Savitakkaṃ [M 4.0081][V 4.0095] dhammaṃ paṭicca savitakko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – savitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Savitakkaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca avitakko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – savitakke khandhe paṭicca vitakko cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Savitakkaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca savitakko ca avitakko ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – savitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā vitakko ca cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (3)

102. Dependent on a state with initial thought, a state with initial thought arises by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate with initial thought, three aggregates arise… and so on… two aggregates arise… and so on… at the moment of rebirth-linking… and so on. Dependent on a state with initial thought, a state without initial thought arises by way of root condition: dependent on the aggregates with initial thought, initial thought and mind-originated materiality arise; at the moment of rebirth-linking… and so on. Dependent on a state with initial thought, both a state with initial thought and a state without initial thought arise by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate with initial thought, three aggregates, initial thought, and mind-originated materiality arise… and so on… two aggregates… and so on… at the moment of rebirth-linking… and so on. (3)

103. Avitakkaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca avitakko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – avitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo [T 4.0385] khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… vitakkaṃ paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ; paṭisandhikkhaṇe avitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā kaṭattā ca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… vitakkaṃ paṭicca kaṭattārūpaṃ, khandhe paṭicca vatthu, vatthuṃ paṭicca khandhā, vitakkaṃ paṭicca vatthu, vatthuṃ paṭicca vitakko, ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe…. (1)

103. Dependent on a state without initial thought, a state without initial thought arises by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate without initial thought, three aggregates and mind-originated materiality arise… and so on… two aggregates… and so on. Dependent on initial thought, mind-originated materiality arises; at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate without initial thought, three aggregates and kamma-originated materiality arise… and so on… two aggregates… and so on. Dependent on initial thought, kamma-originated materiality arises; dependent on the aggregates, the physical base arises; dependent on the physical base, the aggregates arise; dependent on initial thought, the physical base arises; dependent on the physical base, initial thought arises; dependent on one great element… and so on. (1)

Avitakkaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca savitakko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – vitakkaṃ paṭicca sampayuttakā khandhā; paṭisandhikkhaṇe vitakkaṃ paṭicca sampayuttakā khandhā, paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthuṃ paṭicca savitakkā khandhā. (2)

Dependent on a state without initial thought, a state with initial thought arises by way of root condition: dependent on initial thought, the associated aggregates arise; at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on initial thought, the associated aggregates arise; at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on the physical base, the aggregates with initial thought arise. (2)

Avitakkaṃ [V 4.0096] dhammaṃ paṭicca savitakko ca avitakko ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – vitakkaṃ paṭicca sampayuttakā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ, vitakkaṃ paṭicca savitakkā khandhā, mahābhūte paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ; paṭisandhikkhaṇe vitakkaṃ paṭicca sampayuttakā khandhā kaṭattā ca rūpaṃ, paṭisandhikkhaṇe vitakkaṃ paṭicca savitakkā khandhā, mahābhūte paṭicca kaṭattārūpaṃ, paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthuṃ paṭicca savitakkā khandhā, mahābhūte paṭicca kaṭattārūpaṃ, paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthuṃ paṭicca vitakko sampayuttakā ca khandhā. (3)

Dependent on a state without initial thought, both a state with initial thought and a state without initial thought arise by way of root condition: dependent on initial thought, the associated aggregates and mind-originated materiality arise; dependent on initial thought, the aggregates with initial thought arise; dependent on the great elements, mind-originated materiality arises; at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on initial thought, the associated aggregates and kamma-originated materiality arise; at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on initial thought, the aggregates with initial thought arise; dependent on the great elements, kamma-originated materiality arises; at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on the physical base, the aggregates with initial thought arise; dependent on the great elements, kamma-originated materiality arises; at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on the physical base, initial thought and the associated aggregates arise. (3)

104. Savitakkañca avitakkañca dhammaṃ paṭicca savitakko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – savitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca vitakkañca paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe [M 4.0082] …pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe savitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca vitakkañca paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe savitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca [T 4.0386] vatthuñca paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (1)

104. Dependent on a state with initial thought and a state without initial thought, a state with initial thought arises by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate with initial thought and initial thought, three aggregates arise…pe… two aggregates…pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate with initial thought and initial thought, three aggregates arise…pe… two aggregates…pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate with initial thought and the physical base, three aggregates arise…pe… two aggregates…pe…. (1)

Savitakkañca avitakkañca dhammaṃ paṭicca avitakko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – savitakke khandhe ca vitakkañca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ; paṭisandhikkhaṇe savitakke khandhe ca vitakkañca mahābhūte ca paṭicca kaṭattārūpaṃ, paṭisandhikkhaṇe savitakke khandhe ca vatthuñca paṭicca vitakko. (2)

Dependent on a state with initial thought and a state without initial thought, a state without initial thought arises by way of root condition: dependent on the aggregates with initial thought, initial thought, and the great elements, mind-originated materiality arises; at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on the aggregates with initial thought, initial thought, and the great elements, kamma-originated materiality arises; at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on the aggregates with initial thought and the physical base, initial thought arises. (2)

Savitakkañca avitakkañca dhammaṃ paṭicca savitakko ca avitakko ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – savitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca vitakkañca paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… savitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca vitakkañca paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… savitakke khandhe ca vitakkañca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ; paṭisandhikkhaṇe savitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca vitakkañca paṭicca tayo khandhā kaṭattā ca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe savitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca vitakkañca paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… savitakke khandhe ca vitakkañca mahābhūte ca paṭicca kaṭattārūpaṃ, paṭisandhikkhaṇe savitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca vatthuñca paṭicca tayo khandhā vitakko ca…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (3) (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

Dependent on a state with initial thought and a state without initial thought, both a state with initial thought and a state without initial thought arise by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate with initial thought and initial thought, three aggregates and mind-originated materiality arise…pe… two aggregates…pe… dependent on one aggregate with initial thought and initial thought, three aggregates arise…pe… two aggregates…pe… dependent on the aggregates with initial thought, initial thought, and the great elements, mind-originated materiality arises; at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate with initial thought and initial thought, three aggregates and kamma-originated materiality arise…pe… two aggregates…pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate with initial thought and initial thought, three aggregates arise…pe… two aggregates…pe… dependent on the aggregates with initial thought, initial thought, and the great elements, kamma-originated materiality arises; at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate with initial thought and the physical base, three aggregates and initial thought arise…pe… two aggregates…pe…. (3) (In brief.)

105. There are nine in the root condition, nine in the object condition, nine in the dominance condition…pe… nine in the proximate support condition, six in the prenascent condition, six in the repetition condition, nine in the kamma condition, nine in the result condition (nine everywhere), nine in the non-disappearance condition.

Nahetupaccayo

Non-root condition.

106. Savitakkaṃ [T 4.0387] dhammaṃ paṭicca savitakko dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ savitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe paṭicca [M 4.0083] vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho. (Savitakkamūlakā avasesā dve pañhā kātabbā, ahetukaṃ ninnānaṃ.) (3)

106. A state with initial thought arises dependent on a state with initial thought by way of non-root condition: dependent on a rootless single aggregate with initial thought, three aggregates arise…pe… two aggregates…pe… at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking…pe… dependent on the aggregates accompanied by doubt and agitation, delusion accompanied by doubt and agitation arises. (The remaining two questions based on initial thought should be made, to be determined as rootless.) (3)

Avitakkaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca avitakko dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ avitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… ahetukaṃ vitakkaṃ paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ; ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe vitakkaṃ paṭicca kaṭattārūpaṃ, vitakkaṃ paṭicca vatthu, vatthuṃ paṭicca vitakko, ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe…. (1)

A state without initial thought arises dependent on a state without initial thought by way of non-root condition: dependent on a rootless single aggregate without initial thought, three aggregates arise…pe… two aggregates…pe… dependent on rootless initial thought, mind-originated materiality arises; at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking, dependent on initial thought, kamma-originated materiality arises; dependent on initial thought, the physical base arises; dependent on the physical base, initial thought arises; dependent on one great element…pe…. (1)

Avitakkaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca savitakko dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ vitakkaṃ paṭicca sampayuttakā khandhā, ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe vitakkaṃ paṭicca sampayuttakā khandhā; paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthuṃ paṭicca ahetukā savitakkā khandhā, vitakkaṃ paṭicca vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho. (2)

A state with initial thought arises dependent on a state without initial thought by way of non-root condition: dependent on rootless initial thought, the associated aggregates arise; at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking, dependent on initial thought, the associated aggregates arise; at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on the physical base, the rootless aggregates with initial thought arise; dependent on initial thought, the delusion accompanied by doubt and agitation arises. (2)

Avitakkaṃ [V 4.0098] dhammaṃ paṭicca savitakko ca avitakko ca dhammā uppajjanti nahetupaccayā. (Saṃkhittaṃ. Hetupaccayasadisaṃ. “Ahetuka”nti niyāmetabbaṃ.) (3)

Both a state with initial thought and a state without initial thought arise dependent on a state without initial thought by way of non-root condition. (In brief. Similar to the root condition. It should be determined as 'rootless'.) (3)

Savitakkañca avitakkañca dhammaṃ paṭicca savitakko dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ savitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca vitakkañca paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe savitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca vitakkañca paṭicca tayo [T 4.0388] khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe savitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca vatthuñca vitakkañca paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe ca vitakkañca paṭicca vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho. (Avasesā dve pañhā hetupaccayasadisā ninnānā, ahetukanti niyāmetabbaṃ.) (3)

Dependent on a phenomenon accompanied by initial application and a phenomenon without initial application, a phenomenon accompanied by initial application arises by way of non-root condition: dependent on one rootless aggregate accompanied by initial application and initial application, three aggregates arise…pe… two aggregates…pe… at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate accompanied by initial application and initial application, three aggregates arise…pe… two aggregates…pe… at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate accompanied by initial application, the physical base, and initial application, three aggregates arise…pe… two aggregates…pe… dependent on the aggregates accompanied by doubt and agitation, and initial application, delusion accompanied by doubt and delusion accompanied by agitation arises. (The remaining two questions are similar to the root condition, without difference; it should be specified as 'rootless'.) (3)

107. 108. By root condition: by non-object, three; by non-dominance, nine; by non-immediacy, three…pe… by non-kamma, four; by non-result, nine; by non-concomitance, three; by non-dissociation, six; by non-absence, three; by non-disappearance, three.

Root Condition

110. Savitakkaṃ [V 4.0099] dhammaṃ paccayā savitakko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… tīṇi (paṭiccavārasadisā).

110. A phenomenon with initial application conditions a phenomenon with initial application by way of root condition… three. (Similar to the Section on Dependence.)

Avitakkaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā avitakko [T 4.0389] dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – avitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paccayā tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… vitakkaṃ paccayā cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ; paṭisandhikkhaṇe avitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paccayā tayo khandhā kaṭattā ca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe vitakkaṃ paccayā kaṭattārūpaṃ, khandhe paccayā vatthu, vatthuṃ paccayā khandhā, vitakkaṃ paccayā vatthu, vatthuṃ paccayā vitakko, ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paccayā tayo mahābhūtā…pe… vatthuṃ paccayā avitakkā khandhā, vatthuṃ paccayā vitakko.

A phenomenon without initial application conditions a phenomenon without initial application by way of root condition: one aggregate without initial application conditions three aggregates and mind-originated materiality…pe… two aggregates…pe… initial application conditions mind-originated materiality; at the moment of rebirth-linking, one aggregate without initial application conditions three aggregates and kamma-born materiality…pe… two aggregates…pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking, initial application conditions kamma-born materiality; the aggregates condition the physical base, the physical base conditions the aggregates, initial application conditions the physical base, the physical base conditions initial application, one great primary element conditions three great primary elements…pe… the physical base conditions the aggregates without initial application, the physical base conditions initial application.

Avitakkaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā savitakko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – vitakkaṃ paccayā sampayuttakā khandhā, vatthuṃ paccayā savitakkā khandhā (paṭisandhiyāpi dve).

A phenomenon without initial application conditions a phenomenon with initial application by way of root condition: initial application conditions the associated aggregates, the physical base conditions the aggregates with initial application (also two cases at rebirth-linking).

Avitakkaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā savitakko ca avitakko ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – vitakkaṃ paccayā [M 4.0085] sampayuttakā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ, vitakkaṃ paccayā sampayuttakā khandhā, mahābhūte paccayā cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, vatthuṃ paccayā savitakkā khandhā, mahābhūte [V 4.0100] paccayā cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, vatthuṃ paccayā vitakko sampayuttakā ca khandhā; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… (paṭisandhiyāpi pavattisadisāyeva). (3)

A phenomenon without initial application conditions both a phenomenon with initial application and a phenomenon without initial application by way of root condition: initial application conditions the associated aggregates and mind-originated materiality; initial application conditions the associated aggregates; the great primary elements condition mind-originated materiality; the physical base conditions the aggregates with initial application; the great primary elements condition mind-originated materiality; the physical base conditions initial application and the associated aggregates; at the moment of rebirth-linking…pe… (at rebirth-linking it is just like in the course of life). (3)

111. Savitakkañca avitakkañca dhammaṃ paccayā savitakko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – savitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca vitakkañca paccayā tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… savitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca vatthuñca paccayā tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… (paṭisandhikkhaṇe dve [T 4.0390] kātabbā). (1)

111. A phenomenon with initial application and a phenomenon without initial application condition a phenomenon with initial application by way of root condition: one aggregate with initial application and initial application condition three aggregates…pe… two aggregates…pe… one aggregate with initial application and the physical base condition three aggregates…pe… two aggregates…pe… (at the moment of rebirth-linking, two cases should be taken). (1)

Savitakkañca avitakkañca dhammaṃ paccayā avitakko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – savitakke khandhe ca vitakkañca paccayā cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, savitakke khandhe ca vitakkañca mahābhūte ca paccayā cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, savitakke khandhe ca vatthuñca paccayā vitakko; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… (tīṇi, paṭisandhiyāpi). (2)

A phenomenon with initial application and a phenomenon without initial application condition a phenomenon without initial application by way of root condition: the aggregates with initial application and initial application condition mind-originated materiality; the aggregates with initial application, initial application, and the great primary elements condition mind-originated materiality; the aggregates with initial application and the physical base condition initial application; at the moment of rebirth-linking…pe… (three cases, also at rebirth-linking). (2)

Savitakkañca avitakkañca dhammaṃ paccayā savitakko ca avitakko ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – savitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca vitakkañca paccayā tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… savitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca vitakkañca vatthuñca paccayā tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… savitakke khandhe ca vitakkañca mahābhūte ca paccayā cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, savitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca vatthuñca paccayā tayo khandhā vitakko ca…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (3)

A phenomenon with initial application and a phenomenon without initial application condition both a phenomenon with initial application and a phenomenon without initial application by way of root condition: one aggregate with initial application and initial application condition three aggregates and mind-originated materiality…pe… two aggregates…pe… one aggregate with initial application, initial application, and the physical base condition three aggregates…pe… two aggregates…pe… the aggregates with initial application, initial application, and the great primary elements condition mind-originated materiality; one aggregate with initial application and the physical base condition three aggregates and initial application…pe… two aggregates…pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking…pe…. (3)

The Root Condition

115. Savitakkaṃ dhammaṃ saṃsaṭṭho savitakko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – savitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ saṃsaṭṭhā tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Savitakkaṃ dhammaṃ saṃsaṭṭho savitakko ca avitakko ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – savitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ saṃsaṭṭhā tayo khandhā vitakko ca…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (3)

115. Associated with a state with initial application, a state with initial application arises by way of root condition: associated with one aggregate with initial application, three aggregates arise... two aggregates... at the moment of rebirth-linking.... Associated with a state with initial application, a state without initial application arises by way of root condition: initial application associated with aggregates with initial application; at the moment of rebirth-linking.... Associated with a state with initial application, both states with initial application and states without initial application arise by way of root condition: associated with one aggregate with initial application, three aggregates and initial application arise... two aggregates... at the moment of rebirth-linking.... (3)

Avitakkaṃ dhammaṃ saṃsaṭṭho avitakko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – avitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ saṃsaṭṭhā tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Avitakkaṃ dhammaṃ [V 4.0102] saṃsaṭṭho savitakko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – vitakkaṃ saṃsaṭṭhā sampayuttakā khandhā; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (2)

Associated with a state without initial application, a state without initial application arises by way of root condition: associated with one aggregate without initial application, three aggregates arise... two aggregates... at the moment of rebirth-linking.... Associated with a state without initial application, a state with initial application arises by way of root condition: the associated aggregates associated with initial application; at the moment of rebirth-linking.... (2)

Savitakkañca avitakkañca dhammaṃ saṃsaṭṭho savitakko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – savitakkaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca vitakkañca saṃsaṭṭhā tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1) (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

Associated with both a state with initial application and a state without initial application, a state with initial application arises by way of root condition: associated with one aggregate with initial application and initial application, three aggregates arise... two aggregates... at the moment of rebirth-linking.... (1) (Abbreviated.)

Hetuyā [T 4.0392] cha, ārammaṇe cha, adhipatiyā cha (sabbattha cha) avigate cha.

By way of root condition: six; by way of object condition: six; by way of dominance condition: six (six everywhere); by way of non-disappearance condition: six.

Anulomaṃ.

The Forward Order.

Savitakkaṃ [M 4.0087] dhammaṃ saṃsaṭṭho savitakko dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā. (Evaṃ cha pañhā kātabbā anulomasadisā, ahetukāti niyāmetabbā, tīṇiyeva, moho uddharitabbo.)

Associated with a state with initial application, a state with initial application arises not by way of root condition. (In this way, six questions should be made, similar to the forward order, and they should be determined as rootless. Only three are possible, and delusion should be excluded.)

Nahetuyā cha, naadhipatiyā cha, napurejāte cha, napacchājāte cha, naāsevane cha, nakamme cattāri, navipāke cha, najhāne ekaṃ, namagge cha, navippayutte cha.

Not by root condition: six; not by dominance condition: six; not by pre-existence condition: six; not by post-existence condition: six; not by repetition condition: six; not by kamma condition: four; not by result condition: six; not by jhāna condition: one; not by path condition: six; not by dissociation condition: six.

Paccanīyaṃ.

The Negative.

6. Sampayuttavāro

6. Association Section

(Evaṃ itare dve gaṇanāpi sampayuttavāropi kātabbo.)

(In this way, the other two enumerations and the association section should also be done.)

7. Pañhāvāro

7. Question Section

1. Paccayānulomaṃ
