1. The Analysis Section

Hetupaccayo

The Root Condition

116. Savitakko [V 4.0103] dhammo savitakkassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – savitakkā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Savitakko dhammo avitakkassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – savitakkā hetū vitakkassa cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Savitakkā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… (3)

116. A state with initial application is a condition for a state with initial application by way of root condition: roots with initial application are conditions for the associated aggregates by way of root condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking.... A state with initial application is a condition for a state without initial application by way of root condition: roots with initial application are conditions for initial application and for mind-originated material phenomena by way of root condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking.... (The root should be done.) Roots with initial application are conditions for the associated aggregates, for initial application, and for mind-originated material phenomena by way of root condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking.... (3)

Avitakko dhammo avitakkassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – avitakkā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

A state without initial application is a condition for a state without initial application by way of root condition: roots without initial application are conditions for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena by way of root condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking.... (1)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

The Object Condition

117. Savitakko [T 4.0393] dhammo savitakkassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – savitakke khandhe ārabbha savitakkā khandhā uppajjanti. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Savitakke khandhe ārabbha avitakkā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti[M 4.0088]. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Savitakke khandhe ārabbha savitakkā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. (3)

117. A state with initial application is a condition for a state with initial application by way of object condition: having taken the aggregates with initial application as object, aggregates with initial application arise. (The root should be done.) Having taken the aggregates with initial application as object, aggregates without initial application and initial application arise. (The root should be done.) Having taken the aggregates with initial application as object, aggregates with initial application and initial application arise. (3)

118. Avitakko dhammo avitakkassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – ariyā avitakkā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā avitakkaṃ jhānaṃ paccavekkhanti, maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ paccavekkhanti, phalā vuṭṭhahitvā phalaṃ paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ avitakkassa [V 4.0104] maggassa, phalassa, vitakkassa ca ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo; cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ avitakke khandhe ca vitakkañca aniccato…pe… vipassati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha vitakko uppajjati, dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti, cetopariyañāṇena avitakkacittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānāti, ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ…pe… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ…pe… rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ…pe… avitakkā khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, vitakkassa ca ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo; avitakke khandhe ca vitakkañca ārabbha avitakkā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. (1)

118. A state without initial application is a condition for a state without initial application by way of object condition: noble ones, having arisen from the jhānas without initial application, review the jhāna without initial application; having arisen from the path, they review the path; having arisen from the fruition, they review the fruition; they review Nibbāna. Nibbāna is a condition by way of object for the path without initial application, for the fruition, and for initial application. The eye... the base... one contemplates as impermanent... the aggregates without initial application and initial application, delights in, and rejoices in them; taking that as object, initial application arises. With the divine eye one sees forms; with the divine ear element one hears sounds; with knowledge of others' minds one knows the mind of one endowed with consciousness without initial application. The base of infinite space... the base of nothingness... the form base for eye-consciousness... the tangible base... the aggregates without initial application are conditions by way of object for knowledge of psychic powers, knowledge of others' minds, knowledge of past lives, knowledge of beings' destinies according to their kamma, knowledge of future events, and for initial application. Having taken the aggregates without initial application and initial application as object, aggregates without initial application and initial application arise. (1)

Avitakko dhammo savitakkassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – ariyā avitakkā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā…pe… maggā [T 4.0394] vuṭṭhahitvā…pe… phalā vuṭṭhahitvā phalaṃ paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, savitakkassa maggassa, phalassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo; cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ avitakke khandhe ca vitakkañca aniccato…pe… vipassati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; avitakke khandhe ca vitakkañca ārabbha savitakkā khandhā uppajjanti. (2)

A state without initial application is a condition for a state with initial application by way of object condition: noble ones, having arisen from the jhānas without initial application...pe... having arisen from the path...pe... having arisen from the fruition, review the fruition, review Nibbāna; Nibbāna is a condition by way of object for change-of-lineage, for purification, for the path with initial application, for the fruition, and for adverting; the eye...pe... the base... having seen the aggregates without initial application and initial application as impermanent...pe... one delights in and rejoices in them; taking that as object, lust arises...pe... displeasure arises; taking the aggregates without initial application and initial application as object, aggregates with initial application arise. (2)

Avitakko dhammo savitakkassa ca avitakkassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – ariyā avitakkā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā…pe… maggā vuṭṭhahitvā…pe… phalā vuṭṭhahitvā phalaṃ paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, savitakkassa maggassa, phalassa, āvajjanāya, vitakkassa ca ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo; cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ avitakke khandhe ca vitakkañca aniccato…pe… vipassati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha savitakkā [M 4.0089] khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti, avitakke khandhe ca vitakkañca ārabbha savitakkā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. (3)

A state without initial application is a condition for a state with initial application and a state without initial application by way of object condition: noble ones, having arisen from the jhānas without initial application...pe... having arisen from the path...pe... having arisen from the fruition, review the fruition, review Nibbāna; Nibbāna is a condition by way of object for change-of-lineage, for purification, for the path with initial application, for the fruition, for adverting, and for initial application; the eye...pe... the base... having seen the aggregates without initial application and initial application as impermanent...pe... one delights in and rejoices in them; taking that as object, aggregates with initial application and initial application arise; taking the aggregates without initial application and initial application as object, aggregates with initial application and initial application arise. (3)

119. Savitakko ca avitakko ca dhammā savitakkassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – savitakke khandhe ca vitakkañca ārabbha savitakkā khandhā uppajjanti. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ[V 4.0105].) Savitakke khandhe ca vitakkañca ārabbha avitakkā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Savitakke khandhe ca vitakkañca ārabbha savitakkā khandhā ca vitakko [T 4.0395] ca uppajjanti. (3)

119. A state with initial application and a state without initial application are a condition for a state with initial application by way of object condition: taking aggregates with initial application and initial application as object, aggregates with initial application arise. (The root should be done.) Taking aggregates with initial application and initial application as object, aggregates without initial application and initial application arise. (The root should be done.) Taking aggregates with initial application and initial application as object, aggregates with initial application and initial application arise. (3)

Adhipatipaccayo

Dominance Condition

120. Savitakko dhammo savitakkassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – savitakke khandhe garuṃ katvā savitakkā khandhā uppajjanti. Sahajātādhipati – savitakkādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

120. A state with initial application is a condition for a state with initial application by way of dominance condition: object-dominance and co-nascence dominance. Object-dominance: having regarded aggregates with initial application as important, aggregates with initial application arise. Co-nascence dominance: dominance with initial application is a condition for its associated aggregates by way of dominance condition. (1)

Savitakko dhammo avitakkassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – savitakke khandhe garuṃ katvā vitakko uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – savitakkādhipati vitakkassa ca cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state with initial application is a condition for a state without initial application by way of dominance condition: object-dominance and co-nascence dominance. Object-dominance: having regarded aggregates with initial application as important, initial application arises. Co-nascence dominance: dominance with initial application is a condition for initial application and for mind-originated matter by way of dominance condition. (2)

Savitakko dhammo savitakkassa ca avitakkassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – savitakke khandhe garuṃ katvā savitakkā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. Sahajātādhipati – savitakkādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state with initial application is a condition for a state with initial application and a state without initial application by way of dominance condition: object-dominance and co-nascence dominance. Object-dominance: having regarded aggregates with initial application as important, aggregates with initial application and initial application arise. Co-nascence dominance: dominance with initial application is a condition for its associated aggregates, for initial application, and for mind-originated matter by way of dominance condition. (3)

121. Avitakko dhammo avitakkassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – ariyā avitakkā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā…pe… maggā vuṭṭhahitvā…pe… phalā vuṭṭhahitvā phalaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ avitakkassa maggassa, phalassa, vitakkassa ca adhipatipaccayena paccayo; cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ avitakke khandhe ca vitakkañca [T 4.0396] garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā vitakko uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – avitakkādhipati [M 4.0090][V 4.0106] sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

121. A state without initial application is a condition for a state without initial application by way of dominance condition: object-dominance and co-nascence dominance. Object-dominance: noble ones, having arisen from the jhānas without initial application…pe… having arisen from the path…pe… having arisen from the fruition, review the fruition, regarding it as important; they review Nibbāna, regarding it as important. Nibbāna is a condition for the path without initial application, for the fruition, and for initial application by way of dominance condition. Having regarded the eye…pe… the base, and the aggregates without initial application and initial application as important, one savors and delights in them; having regarded that as important, initial application arises. Co-nascence dominance: dominance without initial application is a condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter by way of dominance condition. (1)

Avitakko dhammo savitakkassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – ariyā avitakkā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā…pe… maggā vuṭṭhahitvā…pe… phalā vuṭṭhahitvā phalaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, savitakkassa maggassa, phalassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo; cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ avitakke khandhe ca vitakkañca garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati, avitakke khandhe ca vitakkañca garuṃ katvā savitakkā khandhā uppajjanti. (2)

A state without initial application is a condition for a state with initial application by way of dominance condition. Object-dominance: noble ones, having arisen from the jhānas without initial application…pe… having arisen from the path…pe… having arisen from the fruition, review the fruition, regarding it as important; they review Nibbāna, regarding it as important. Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage, for purification, for the path with initial application, and for the fruition by way of dominance condition. Having regarded the eye…pe… the base, and the aggregates without initial application and initial application as important, one savors and delights in them; having regarded that as important, lust arises, wrong view arises; having regarded the aggregates without initial application and initial application as important, aggregates with initial application arise. (2)

Avitakko dhammo savitakkassa ca avitakkassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – ariyā avitakkā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā…pe… maggā vuṭṭhahitvā…pe… phalā vuṭṭhahitvā phalaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, savitakkassa maggassa, phalassa, vitakkassa ca adhipatipaccayena paccayo; cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ avitakke khandhe ca vitakkañca garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati; avitakke khandhe ca vitakkañca garuṃ katvā savitakkā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. (3)

A thought-free phenomenon is a condition for both thought-accompanied and thought-free phenomena by way of the dominance condition. Object dominance: noble ones, having emerged from thought-free jhānas…pe… having emerged from the path…pe… having emerged from the fruition, review the fruition, regarding it as important; they review Nibbāna, regarding it as important. Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage consciousness, purification, the thought-accompanied path, the fruition, and thought by way of the dominance condition. Making the eye…pe… the base, and the thought-free aggregates and thought important, one savors and delights in them; making that important, lust arises, wrong view arises; making the thought-free aggregates and thought important, thought-accompanied aggregates and thought arise. (3)

Savitakko ca avitakko [T 4.0397] ca dhammā savitakkassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – savitakke khandhe ca vitakkañca garuṃ katvā savitakkā khandhā uppajjanti. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Savitakke khandhe ca vitakkañca garuṃ katvā vitakko uppajjati. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Savitakke khandhe ca vitakkañca garuṃ katvā savitakkā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. (3)

Both thought-accompanied and thought-free phenomena are conditions for a thought-accompanied phenomenon by way of the dominance condition. Object dominance: making the thought-accompanied aggregates and thought important, thought-accompanied aggregates arise. (The root should be supplied.) Making the thought-accompanied aggregates and thought important, thought arises. (The root should be supplied.) Making the thought-accompanied aggregates and thought important, thought-accompanied aggregates and thought arise. (3)

Anantarapaccayādi

Contiguity Condition, etc.

122. Savitakko [V 4.0107] dhammo savitakkassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā savitakkā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ savitakkānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

122. A thought-accompanied phenomenon is a condition for a thought-accompanied phenomenon by way of the contiguity condition. The preceding thought-accompanied aggregates are a condition for the succeeding thought-accompanied aggregates by way of the contiguity condition. (1)

Savitakko [M 4.0091] dhammo avitakkassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā savitakkā khandhā pacchimassa pacchimassa vitakkassa anantarapaccayena paccayo; savitakkaṃ cuticittaṃ avitakkassa upapatticittassa anantarapaccayena paccayo; āvajjanā pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; savitakkā khandhā avitakkassa vuṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo; dutiyassa jhānassa parikammaṃ dutiyassa jhānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo; tatiyassa jhānassa parikammaṃ…pe… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa parikammaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa…pe… dibbassa cakkhussa parikammaṃ…pe… dibbāya sotadhātuyā parikammaṃ…pe… iddhividhañāṇassa parikammaṃ…pe… cetopariyañāṇassa parikammaṃ…pe… pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa parikammaṃ…pe… yathākammūpagañāṇassa parikammaṃ yathākammūpagañāṇassa…pe… anāgataṃsañāṇassa parikammaṃ anāgataṃsañāṇassa anantarapaccayena [T 4.0398] paccayo. Gotrabhu avitakkassa maggassa… vodānaṃ avitakkassa maggassa… anulomaṃ avitakkāya phalasamāpattiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A thought-accompanied phenomenon is a condition for a thought-free phenomenon by way of the contiguity condition. The preceding thought-accompanied aggregates are a condition for the subsequent thought by way of the contiguity condition; the death consciousness with applied thought is a condition for the rebirth consciousness without applied thought by way of the contiguity condition; advertence is a condition for the five sense-consciousnesses by way of the contiguity condition; the thought-accompanied aggregates are a condition for emergence without applied thought by way of the contiguity condition; the preliminary work for the second jhāna is a condition for the second jhāna by way of the contiguity condition; the preliminary work for the third jhāna…pe… the preliminary work for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a condition for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception…pe… the preliminary work for the divine eye…pe… the preliminary work for the divine ear element…pe… the preliminary work for the knowledge of psychic powers…pe… the preliminary work for the knowledge of others’ minds…pe… the preliminary work for the knowledge of past lives…pe… the preliminary work for the knowledge of the destiny of beings according to their actions…pe… the preliminary work for the knowledge of the future is a condition for the knowledge of the future by way of the contiguity condition. Change-of-lineage consciousness is a condition for the path without applied thought by way of the contiguity condition… purification is a condition for the path without applied thought by way of the contiguity condition… adaptation is a condition for the fruition-attainment without applied thought by way of the contiguity condition. (2)

Savitakko dhammo savitakkassa ca avitakkassa ca dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā savitakkā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ savitakkānaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A thought-accompanied phenomenon is a condition for both a thought-accompanied phenomenon and a thought-free phenomenon by way of the contiguity condition. The preceding thought-accompanied aggregates are a condition for the succeeding thought-accompanied aggregates and for thought by way of the contiguity condition. (3)

123. Avitakko dhammo avitakkassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimo purimo vitakko pacchimassa pacchimassa vitakkassa anantarapaccayena paccayo; purimā purimā avitakkā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ avitakkānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; avitakko maggo avitakkassa phalassa…pe… avitakkaṃ phalaṃ avitakkassa phalassa [V 4.0108]…pe… nirodhā vuṭṭhahantassa nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ avitakkāya phalasamāpattiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

123. A thought-free phenomenon is a condition for a thought-free phenomenon by way of the contiguity condition. A preceding thought is a condition for a subsequent thought by way of the contiguity condition; preceding thought-free aggregates are a condition for subsequent thought-free aggregates by way of the contiguity condition; the path without applied thought is a condition for fruition without applied thought by way of the contiguity condition…pe… the fruition without applied thought is a condition for fruition without applied thought by way of the contiguity condition…pe… emerging from cessation, the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a condition for the fruition-attainment without applied thought by way of the contiguity condition. (1)

Avitakko dhammo savitakkassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimo purimo vitakko pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ savitakkānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; avitakkaṃ cuticittaṃ savitakkassa upapatticittassa, avitakkaṃ bhavaṅgaṃ āvajjanāya, avitakkā khandhā savitakkassa vuṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A thought-free phenomenon is a condition for a thought-accompanied phenomenon by way of the contiguity condition. The preceding thought is a condition for the subsequent thought-accompanied aggregates by way of the contiguity condition; death consciousness without applied thought is a condition for rebirth consciousness with applied thought by way of the contiguity condition; the life-continuum without applied thought is a condition for advertence by way of the contiguity condition; aggregates without applied thought are a condition for emergence with applied thought by way of the contiguity condition. (2)

Avitakko [M 4.0092] dhammo savitakkassa ca avitakkassa ca dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimo purimo vitakko pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ savitakkānaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A thought-free phenomenon is a condition for both a thought-accompanied phenomenon and a thought-free phenomenon by way of the contiguity condition. The preceding thought is a condition for the succeeding thought-accompanied aggregates and for thought by way of the contiguity condition. (3)

124. Savitakko ca avitakko ca dhammā savitakkassa [T 4.0399] dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā savitakkā khandhā ca vitakko ca pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ savitakkānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

124. Both thought-accompanied and thought-free phenomena are conditions for a thought-accompanied phenomenon by way of the contiguity condition. The preceding thought-accompanied aggregates and thought are a condition for the succeeding thought-accompanied aggregates by way of the contiguity condition. (1)

Savitakko ca avitakko ca dhammā avitakkassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā savitakkā khandhā ca vitakko ca pacchimassa pacchimassa vitakkassa anantarapaccayena paccayo; savitakkaṃ cuticittañca vitakko ca avitakkassa upapatticittassa…pe… āvajjanā ca vitakko ca pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ…pe… savitakkā khandhā ca vitakko ca avitakkassa vuṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo; dutiyassa jhānassa parikammañca vitakko ca…pe… (heṭṭhā likhitaṃ lekhaṃ iminā kāraṇena daṭṭhabbaṃ); anulomañca vitakko ca avitakkāya phalasamāpattiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

Phenomena with applied thought and phenomena without applied thought are a condition by way of immediacy for a phenomenon without applied thought. The preceding aggregates with applied thought and applied thought are a condition by way of immediacy for the succeeding applied thought; the death-consciousness with applied thought and applied thought are a condition by way of immediacy for the rebirth-consciousness without applied thought… the advertence and applied thought are a condition by way of immediacy for the five consciousnesses… the aggregates with applied thought and applied thought are a condition by way of immediacy for emergence without applied thought; the preliminary work for the second jhāna and applied thought… (the text written below should be understood for this reason); adaptation and applied thought are a condition by way of immediacy for the fruition-attainment without applied thought. (2)

Savitakko ca avitakko ca dhammā savitakkassa ca avitakkassa ca dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā savitakkā khandhā ca vitakko ca pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ savitakkānaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. (3)

Phenomena with applied thought and phenomena without applied thought are a condition by way of immediacy for a phenomenon with applied thought and for a phenomenon without applied thought. The preceding aggregates with applied thought and applied thought are a condition by way of immediacy for the succeeding aggregates with applied thought and for applied thought. (3)

Samanantarapaccayena [V 4.0109] paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… nava… aññamaññapaccayena paccayo… nava… nissayapaccayena paccayo… nava.

A condition by way of contiguity… a condition by way of conascence… nine… a condition by way of mutuality… nine… a condition by way of support… nine.

Upanissayapaccayo

Decisive Support Condition

125. Savitakko dhammo savitakkassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – savitakkā khandhā savitakkānaṃ khandhānaṃ upanissayapaccayena [T 4.0400] paccayo. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Savitakkā khandhā avitakkānaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Savitakkā khandhā savitakkānaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (3)

125. A phenomenon with applied thought is a condition by way of decisive support for a phenomenon with applied thought: by way of object decisive support, immediacy decisive support, natural decisive support… By way of natural decisive support: the aggregates with applied thought are a condition by way of decisive support for the aggregates with applied thought. (The root section is to be applied.) The aggregates with applied thought are a condition by way of decisive support for the aggregates without applied thought and for applied thought. (The root section is to be applied.) The aggregates with applied thought are a condition by way of decisive support for the aggregates with applied thought and for applied thought. (3)

126. Avitakko [M 4.0093] dhammo avitakkassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – avitakkaṃ saddhaṃ upanissāya avitakkaṃ jhānaṃ uppādeti, maggaṃ uppādeti, abhiññaṃ uppādeti, samāpattiṃ uppādeti; avitakkaṃ sīlaṃ…pe… paññaṃ… kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ… kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ… utuṃ… bhojanaṃ… senāsanaṃ vitakkaṃ upanissāya avitakkaṃ jhānaṃ uppādeti, maggaṃ…pe… abhiññaṃ…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti; avitakkā saddhā…pe… senāsanaṃ vitakko ca avitakkāya saddhāya…pe… paññāya… kāyikassa sukhassa… kāyikassa dukkhassa… avitakkassa maggassa… phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

126. A phenomenon without applied thought is a condition by way of decisive support for a phenomenon without applied thought: by way of object decisive support, immediacy decisive support, natural decisive support… By way of natural decisive support: relying on faith without applied thought, one produces jhāna without applied thought, produces the path, produces higher knowledge, produces attainment; relying on virtue without applied thought… wisdom… bodily pleasure… bodily pain… climate… food… lodging, one produces jhāna without applied thought, the path… higher knowledge… attainment; faith without applied thought… lodging, and applied thought are a condition by way of decisive support for faith without applied thought… wisdom… bodily pleasure… bodily pain… the path without applied thought… the attainment of fruition. (1)

Avitakko dhammo savitakkassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo (tīṇipi upanissayā sabbattha kātabbā). Avitakkaṃ saddhaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti, sīlaṃ samādiyati, uposathakammaṃ karoti; savitakkaṃ jhānaṃ uppādeti, vipassanaṃ…pe… maggaṃ…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti, mānaṃ jappeti, diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti; avitakkaṃ sīlaṃ…pe… senāsanaṃ vitakkaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti, pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; avitakkā saddhā…pe… senāsanaṃ vitakko ca savitakkāya saddhāya…pe… paññāya… rāgassa…pe… patthanāya savitakkassa maggassa, phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon without applied thought is a condition by way of decisive support for a phenomenon with applied thought (all three decisive supports are to be applied everywhere). Relying on faith without applied thought, one gives alms, undertakes precepts, performs the Uposatha observance; one produces jhāna with applied thought, insight… the path… attainment; one generates conceit, grasps wrong views. Relying on virtue without applied thought… lodging, one gives alms… produces attainment, kills living beings… splits the Sangha; faith without applied thought… lodging, and applied thought are a condition by way of decisive support for faith with applied thought… wisdom… lust… aspiration, for the path with applied thought, and for the fruition-attainment. (2)

Avitakko dhammo savitakkassa ca avitakkassa ca dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – avitakkaṃ saddhaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… (dutiyavāre likhitapadā sabbe kātabbā) samāpattiṃ uppādeti, mānaṃ jappeti, diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti; sīlaṃ…pe… paññaṃ…pe… senāsanaṃ vitakkaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; avitakkā saddhā…pe… senāsanaṃ vitakko ca savitakkāya saddhāya…pe… paññāya… rāgassa [V 4.0110]…pe… patthanāya savitakkassa maggassa[T 4.0401], phalasamāpattiyā vitakkassa ca upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A phenomenon without applied thought is a condition by way of decisive support for a phenomenon with applied thought and for a phenomenon without applied thought. Relying on faith without applied thought, one gives alms… (all the terms written in the second section are to be applied) produces attainment, generates conceit, grasps wrong views; relying on virtue… wisdom… lodging, one gives alms… kills living beings… splits the Sangha; faith without applied thought… lodging, and applied thought are a condition by way of decisive support for faith with applied thought… wisdom… lust… aspiration, for the path with applied thought, for the fruition-attainment, and for applied thought. (3)

127. Savitakko ca avitakko ca dhammā savitakkassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – savitakkā khandhā ca vitakko ca savitakkānaṃ khandhānaṃ upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Savitakkā khandhā ca vitakko ca avitakkānaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ [M 4.0094] kātabbaṃ.) Savitakkā khandhā ca vitakko ca savitakkānaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (3)

127. Phenomena with applied thought and phenomena without applied thought are a condition by way of decisive support for a phenomenon with applied thought. The aggregates with applied thought and applied thought are a condition by way of decisive support for the aggregates with applied thought. (The root section is to be applied.) The aggregates with applied thought and applied thought are a condition by way of decisive support for the aggregates without applied thought and for applied thought. (The root section is to be applied.) The aggregates with applied thought and applied thought are a condition by way of decisive support for the aggregates with applied thought and for applied thought. (3)

Purejātapaccayo

Pre-nascence Condition

128. Avitakko dhammo avitakkassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… vipassati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha vitakko uppajjati, dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe…. Vatthupurejātaṃ – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ [T 4.0402] kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… vatthu avitakkānaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca purejātapaccayena paccayo.

128. A phenomenon without applied thought is a condition for a phenomenon without applied thought by way of pre-nascence: object pre-nascence and base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: one discerns the eye… the base as impermanent… one savors and delights in it; taking that as object, applied thought arises. With the divine eye, one sees a form… the tangible-object base for body-consciousness… Base pre-nascence: the eye base for eye-consciousness… the body base for body-consciousness… the base is a condition for the aggregates without applied thought and for applied thought by way of pre-nascence.

Avitakko dhammo savitakkassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… vipassati [V 4.0111] assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha savitakkā khandhā uppajjanti. Vatthupurejātaṃ – vatthu savitakkānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo.

A thought-free phenomenon is a condition for a thought-accompanied phenomenon by way of pre-nascence condition: object pre-nascence and base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: one discerns the eye...etc.... the base as impermanent...etc.... savors and delights in it; with reference to that, thought-accompanied aggregates arise. Base pre-nascence: the base is a condition for thought-accompanied aggregates by way of pre-nascence condition.

Avitakko dhammo savitakkassa ca avitakkassa ca dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… vipassati, assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha savitakkā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. Vatthupurejātaṃ – vatthu savitakkānaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca purejātapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A thought-free phenomenon is a condition for a thought-accompanied phenomenon and for a thought-free phenomenon by way of pre-nascence condition: object pre-nascence and base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: one discerns the eye...etc.... the base as impermanent...etc.... savors and delights in it; with reference to that, thought-accompanied aggregates and thought arise. Base pre-nascence: the base is a condition for thought-accompanied aggregates and for thought by way of pre-nascence condition. (3)

Pacchājātāsevanapaccayā

The Post-nascence and Repetition Conditions.

129. Savitakko dhammo avitakkassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo (tīṇi, pacchājātā)… āsevanapaccayena paccayo… nava.

129. A thought-accompanied phenomenon is a condition for a thought-free phenomenon by way of post-nascence condition (three, post-nascence)...by way of repetition condition...nine.

Kammapaccayādi

The Kamma Condition, etc.

130. Savitakko dhammo savitakkassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – savitakkā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Nānākkhaṇikā – savitakkā cetanā vipākānaṃ savitakkānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (Evaṃ cattāri, sahajātāpi nānākkhaṇikāpi kātabbā.)

130. A thought-accompanied phenomenon is a condition for a thought-accompanied phenomenon by way of kamma condition: co-nascence and non-simultaneous. Co-nascence: thought-accompanied volition is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of kamma condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking...etc.... Non-simultaneous: thought-accompanied volition is a condition for the resultant thought-accompanied aggregates by way of kamma condition. (Thus four, both co-nascence and non-simultaneous should be stated.)

Vipākapaccayena [M 4.0095] paccayo… nava… āhārapaccayena paccayo… cattāri… indriyapaccayena [T 4.0403] paccayo… cattāri… jhānapaccayena paccayo… nava… maggapaccayena paccayo… nava… sampayuttapaccayena paccayo… cha.

By way of result condition...nine...by way of nutriment condition...four...by way of faculty condition...four...by way of jhāna condition...nine...by way of path condition...nine...by way of association condition...six.

131. Savitakko dhammo savitakkassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ). (1)

131. A thought-accompanied phenomenon is a condition for a thought-accompanied phenomenon by way of dissociation condition: co-nascence, post-nascence (abbreviated). (1)

Avitakko dhammo avitakkassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ[V 4.0112], pacchājātaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ). Avitakko dhammo savitakkassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ). Avitakko dhammo savitakkassa ca avitakkassa ca dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajātaṃ – paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthu vitakkassa sampayuttakānañca khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – vatthu vitakkassa sampayuttakānañca khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A thought-free phenomenon is a condition for a thought-free phenomenon by way of dissociation condition: co-nascence, pre-nascence, and post-nascence (abbreviated). A thought-free phenomenon is a condition for a thought-accompanied phenomenon by way of dissociation condition: co-nascence and pre-nascence (abbreviated). A thought-free phenomenon is a condition for a thought-accompanied phenomenon and for a thought-free phenomenon by way of dissociation condition: co-nascence and pre-nascence. Co-nascence: at the moment of rebirth-linking, the base is a condition for thought and the associated aggregates by way of dissociation condition. Pre-nascence: the base is a condition for thought and the associated aggregates by way of dissociation condition. (3)

Savitakko ca avitakko ca dhammā avitakkassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ).

A thought-accompanied phenomenon and a thought-free phenomenon are a condition for a thought-free phenomenon by way of dissociation condition: co-nascence, post-nascence (abbreviated).

Atthipaccayādi

The Presence Condition, etc.

132. Savitakko dhammo savitakkassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo (ekaṃ, paṭiccasadisaṃ). Savitakko dhammo avitakkassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ). Savitakko dhammo savitakkassa ca avitakkassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo (paṭiccasadisaṃ). (3)

132. A thought-accompanied phenomenon is a condition for a thought-accompanied phenomenon by way of presence condition (one, similar to the dependent condition). A thought-accompanied phenomenon is a condition for a thought-free phenomenon by way of presence condition: co-nascence and post-nascence (abbreviated). A thought-accompanied phenomenon is a condition for a thought-accompanied phenomenon and for a thought-free phenomenon by way of presence condition (similar to the dependent condition). (3)

Avitakko dhammo avitakkassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ). Avitakko dhammo savitakkassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ). Avitakko dhammo savitakkassa ca avitakkassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – vitakko sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo; paṭisandhikkhaṇe vitakko sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca [M 4.0096] rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo, paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthu vitakkassa sampayuttakānañca khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… vipassati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha vitakko ca sampayuttakā ca khandhā uppajjanti, vatthu vitakkassa sampayuttakānañca khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A thought-free phenomenon is a condition for a thought-free phenomenon by way of presence condition: co-nascence, pre-nascence, post-nascence, nutriment, faculty (abbreviated). A thought-free phenomenon is a condition for a thought-accompanied phenomenon by way of presence condition: co-nascence, pre-nascence (abbreviated). A thought-free phenomenon is a condition for a thought-accompanied phenomenon and for a thought-free phenomenon by way of presence condition: co-nascence and pre-nascence. Co-nascence: thought is a condition by way of presence condition for the associated aggregates and mind-originated material phenomena; at the moment of rebirth-linking, thought is a condition by way of presence condition for the associated aggregates and kamma-born material phenomena; at the moment of rebirth-linking, the base is a condition by way of presence condition for thought and the associated aggregates. Pre-nascence: one discerns the eye...etc.... the base as impermanent...etc.... savors and delights in it; with reference to that, thought and the associated aggregates arise; the base is a condition by way of presence condition for thought and the associated aggregates. (3)

133. Savitakko ca avitakko ca dhammā savitakkassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – savitakko eko khandho ca vitakko ca tiṇṇannaṃ [V 4.0113] khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca…pe…. Sahajāto – savitakko eko khandho ca vatthu ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca…pe… (paṭisandhikkhaṇe sahajātāpi dvepi kātabbā). (1)

133. A thought-accompanied phenomenon and a thought-free phenomenon are a condition for a thought-accompanied phenomenon by way of presence condition: co-nascence, pre-nascence. Co-nascence: one thought-accompanied aggregate and thought are a condition for three aggregates by way of presence condition...etc.... two aggregates...etc.... Co-nascence: one thought-accompanied aggregate and the base are a condition for three aggregates by way of presence condition...etc.... two aggregates...etc.... (at the moment of rebirth-linking, both co-nascence should be stated). (1)

Savitakko ca avitakko ca dhammā avitakkassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Sahajātā – savitakkā khandhā ca vitakko ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātā – savitakkā khandhā ca vatthu ca vitakkassa atthipaccayena paccayo (paṭisandhikkhaṇe, tīṇi). Pacchājātā – savitakkā [T 4.0405] khandhā ca vitakko ca purejātassa imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – savitakkā khandhā ca vitakko ca kabaḷīkāro āhāro ca imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – savitakkā khandhā ca vitakko ca rūpajīvitindriyañca kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (3)

Both thought-accompanied and thought-free phenomena are conditions for a thought-free phenomenon by way of presence condition: co-nascence, pre-nascence, post-nascence, nutriment, faculty. Co-nascence: thought-accompanied aggregates and initial application are conditions for mind-originated material phenomena by way of presence condition. Co-nascence: thought-accompanied aggregates and the base are conditions for initial application by way of presence condition (at the moment of rebirth-linking, three). Post-nascence: thought-accompanied aggregates and initial application are conditions for this pre-arisen body by way of presence condition. Post-nascence: thought-accompanied aggregates, initial application, and edible food are conditions for this body by way of presence condition. Post-nascence: thought-accompanied aggregates, initial application, and the material life faculty are conditions for kamma-born material phenomena by way of presence condition. (3)

Savitakko ca avitakko ca dhammā savitakkassa ca avitakkassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – savitakko eko khandho ca vitakko ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca…pe…. Sahajāto – savitakko eko khandho ca vatthu ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca…pe… (paṭisandhiyāpi dve). (3)

Both thought-accompanied and thought-free phenomena are conditions for both thought-accompanied and thought-free phenomena by way of presence condition: co-nascence, pre-nascence.
