312. Niyyānikaṃ [T 4.0504] dhammaṃ saṃsaṭṭho niyyāniko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – niyyānikaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ saṃsaṭṭhā tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (1)

312. Conjoined with an emancipatory phenomenon, an emancipatory phenomenon arises by way of root condition—three aggregates are conjoined with one emancipatory aggregate… and so on… two aggregates… and so on. (1)

Aniyyānikaṃ [M 4.0174][V 4.0205] dhammaṃ saṃsaṭṭho aniyyāniko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – aniyyānikaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ saṃsaṭṭhā tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

Conjoined with a non-emancipatory phenomenon, a non-emancipatory phenomenon arises by way of root condition—three aggregates are conjoined with one non-emancipatory aggregate… and so on… two aggregates… and so on… at the moment of rebirth-linking… and so on. (1)

Hetuyā dve, ārammaṇe dve (sabbattha dve), vipāke ekaṃ…pe… avigate dve (anulomaṃ).

In root, two; in object, two (in all, two); in result, one… and so on… in non-disappearance, two (positive).

Nahetuyā ekaṃ, naadhipatiyā dve, napurejāte dve, napacchājāte dve, naāsevane ekaṃ, nakamme dve, navipāke dve, najhāne ekaṃ, namagge ekaṃ, navippayutte dve (paccanīyaṃ).

In non-root, one; in non-predominance, two; in non-pre-nascence, two; in non-post-nascence, two; in non-repetition, one; in non-kamma, two; in non-result, two; in non-jhāna, one; in non-path, one; in non-dissociation, two (negative).

6. Sampayuttavāro

6. Associated Section

(Evaṃ itare dve gaṇanāpi sampayuttavāropi kātabbo.)

(The other two enumerations and the Associated Section should also be done in the same way.)

7. Pañhāvāro

7. Question Section

1. Paccayānulomaṃ

1. Conditional Positive

1. Vibhaṅgavāro

1. Analysis Section

Hetupaccayo

The Root Condition

313. Niyyāniko dhammo niyyānikassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – niyyānikā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Niyyānikā hetū cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Niyyānikā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (3)

313. An emancipatory phenomenon is a condition for an emancipatory phenomenon by way of root condition—emancipatory roots are a condition for the associated aggregates by way of root condition. (The root section should be done.) Emancipatory roots are a condition for mind-originated materiality by way of root condition. (The root section should be done.) Emancipatory roots are a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by way of root condition. (3)

Aniyyāniko dhammo aniyyānikassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – aniyyānikā hetū [V 4.0206] sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo[T 4.0505]; paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

A non-emancipatory phenomenon is a condition for a non-emancipatory phenomenon by way of root condition—non-emancipatory roots are a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by way of root condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking… and so on. (1)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

The Object Condition

314. Niyyāniko dhammo aniyyānikassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ paccavekkhanti, cetopariyañāṇena niyyānikacittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānāti, niyyānikā khandhā cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

314. An emancipatory phenomenon is a condition for a non-emancipatory phenomenon by way of object condition—the noble ones, having emerged from the path, review the path; with knowledge of others’ minds, one knows the mind of one endowed with emancipatory consciousness; the emancipatory aggregates are a condition for knowledge of others’ minds, for knowledge of recollection of past lives, for knowledge of the future, and for adverting, by way of object condition. (1)

Aniyyāniko [M 4.0175] dhammo aniyyānikassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ paccavekkhati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; pubbe suciṇṇāni…pe… jhānā…pe… ariyā phalaṃ paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, phalassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo; ariyā pahīne kilese…pe… vikkhambhite…pe… pubbe samudāciṇṇe…pe… cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniyyānike khandhe aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati; dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti, cetopariyañāṇena aniyyānikacittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānāti, ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanassa…pe… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa…pe… rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… aniyyānikā khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo.

A non-emancipatory phenomenon is a condition for a non-emancipatory phenomenon by way of object condition—having given a gift… having undertaken the moral precepts… having performed the observance day duties, one reviews it, delights in it, and rejoices in it; taking that as object, lust arises… and so on… grief arises; previously well-practiced deeds… and so on… jhānas… and so on… the noble ones review the fruition, they review Nibbāna; Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage, for purification, for fruition, and for adverting, by way of object condition; the noble ones review the defilements that have been abandoned… that have been suppressed… that have been previously accumulated… and so on… the eye… and so on… the base… the non-emancipatory aggregates as impermanent… and so on… grief arises; with the divine eye, one sees a form; with the divine ear-element, one hears a sound; with knowledge of others’ minds, one knows the mind of one endowed with non-emancipatory consciousness; the base of infinite space is a condition for the base of infinite consciousness… and so on… the base of nothingness is a condition for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception… and so on… the form-base is a condition for eye-consciousness… and so on… the tangible-base is a condition for body-consciousness… and so on… the non-emancipatory aggregates are a condition for knowledge of psychic powers, for knowledge of others’ minds, for knowledge of recollection of past lives, for knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings, for knowledge of the future, and for adverting, by way of object condition.

Aniyyāniko [T 4.0506] dhammo niyyānikassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – nibbānaṃ maggassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A non-emancipatory phenomenon is a condition for an emancipatory phenomenon by way of object condition—Nibbāna is a condition for the path by way of object condition. (2)

Adhipatipaccayo

The Predominance Condition

315. Niyyāniko [V 4.0207] dhammo niyyānikassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – niyyānikādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Niyyāniko dhammo aniyyānikassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti. Sahajātādhipati – niyyānikādhipati cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Niyyānikādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (3)

315. A leading-out phenomenon is a condition for a leading-out phenomenon by way of dominant condition. Conascence dominant condition—the leading-out dominant factor is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of dominant condition. A leading-out phenomenon is a condition for a non-leading-out phenomenon by way of dominant condition—object dominant condition, conascence dominant condition. Object dominant condition—the noble ones, having emerged from the path, review the path with esteem. Conascence dominant condition—the leading-out dominant factor is a condition for mind-originated matter by way of dominant condition. The leading-out dominant factor is a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter by way of dominant condition. (3)

316. Aniyyāniko dhammo aniyyānikassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati, pubbe suciṇṇāni…pe… jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā…pe… ariyā phalaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti[M 4.0176], nibbānaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, phalassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo; cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniyyānike khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – aniyyānikādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ [T 4.0507] adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Aniyyāniko dhammo niyyānikassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – nibbānaṃ maggassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (2)

316. A non-leading-out phenomenon is a condition for a non-leading-out phenomenon by way of dominant condition—object dominant condition, conascence dominant condition. Object dominant condition—having performed generosity… morality… the observance-day practice, one reflects upon that with respect, delights in that, and rejoices in that; making that an object of respect, lust arises, wrong view arises. Previously well-performed deeds… having emerged from jhānas… the noble ones reflect upon the fruition with respect, they reflect upon Nibbāna with respect. Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage, purification, and fruition by way of dominant condition; the eye… the base… the non-leading-out aggregates [are made an object of respect], one delights in them and rejoices in them; making them an object of respect, lust arises, wrong view arises. Conascence dominant condition—the non-leading-out dominant factor is a condition for the associated aggregates and mind-originated matter by way of dominant condition. A non-leading-out phenomenon is a condition for a leading-out phenomenon by way of dominant condition. Object dominant condition—Nibbāna is a condition for the path by way of dominant condition. (2)

Anantarapaccayādi

Proximity Condition, etc.

317. Niyyāniko dhammo aniyyānikassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – maggo phalassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

317. A leading-out phenomenon is a condition for a non-leading-out phenomenon by way of proximity condition—the path is a condition for the fruition by way of proximity condition. (1)

Aniyyāniko dhammo aniyyānikassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā aniyyānikā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ aniyyānikānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; anulomaṃ gotrabhussa… anulomaṃ vodānassa… phalaṃ phalassa… anulomaṃ phalasamāpattiyā [V 4.0208]… nirodhā vuṭṭhahantassa nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ phalasamāpattiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. Aniyyāniko dhammo niyyānikassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo… gotrabhu maggassa; vodānaṃ maggassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A non-leading-out phenomenon is a condition for a non-leading-out phenomenon by way of proximity condition—the preceding non-leading-out aggregates are a condition for the subsequent non-leading-out aggregates by way of proximity condition; adaptation for change-of-lineage… adaptation for purification… the fruition for the fruition… adaptation for fruition-attainment… for one emerging from cessation, the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a condition for fruition-attainment by way of proximity condition. A non-leading-out phenomenon is a condition for a leading-out phenomenon by way of proximity condition… change-of-lineage is a condition for the path; purification is a condition for the path by way of proximity condition. (2)

Samanantarapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… pañca… aññamaññapaccayena paccayo… dve… nissayapaccayena paccayo… satta.

Contiguity condition… conascence condition… five… mutuality condition… two… support condition… seven.

Upanissayapaccayo

Decisive Support Condition

318. Niyyāniko dhammo niyyānikassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Pakatūpanissayo – paṭhamo maggo dutiyassa maggassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo…pe… tatiyo maggo catutthassa maggassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Niyyāniko dhammo aniyyānikassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo[T 4.0508], pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – ariyā maggaṃ upanissāya anuppannaṃ samāpattiṃ uppādenti, uppannaṃ samāpajjanti, saṅkhāre aniccato…pe… vipassanti, maggo ariyānaṃ atthapaṭisambhidāya…pe… paṭibhānapaṭisambhidāya ṭhānāṭhānakosallassa [M 4.0177] upanissayapaccayena paccayo, maggo phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

318. A leading-out phenomenon is a condition for a leading-out phenomenon by way of decisive support condition. Natural decisive support: the first path is a condition for the second path by way of decisive support condition… the third path is a condition for the fourth path by way of decisive support condition. A leading-out phenomenon is a condition for a non-leading-out phenomenon by way of decisive support condition: object decisive support, proximity decisive support, natural decisive support… Natural decisive support: the noble ones, depending on the path, give rise to unarisen attainments, enter upon arisen ones, contemplate formations as impermanent… The path is a condition for the noble ones’ analytical knowledge of meaning… analytical knowledge of ready wit, and skill in the possible and the impossible, by way of decisive support condition. The path is a condition for fruition-attainment by way of decisive support condition. (2)

319. Aniyyāniko dhammo aniyyānikassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – aniyyānikaṃ saddhaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti, sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ karoti, jhānaṃ uppādeti… vipassanaṃ… abhiññaṃ… samāpattiṃ uppādeti… mānaṃ jappeti… diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti; aniyyānikaṃ sīlaṃ…pe… paññaṃ… rāgaṃ…pe… patthanaṃ… utuṃ… bhojanaṃ… senāsanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti, pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; aniyyānikā saddhā…pe… senāsanaṃ aniyyānikāya saddhāya…pe… patthanāya… kāyikassa sukhassa… kāyikassa dukkhassa… phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Aniyyāniko dhammo niyyānikassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – paṭhamassa maggassa parikammaṃ paṭhamassa [V 4.0209] maggassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo…pe… catutthassa maggassa parikammaṃ catutthassa maggassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

319. A non-leading-out phenomenon is a condition for a non-leading-out phenomenon by way of decisive support condition: object decisive support, proximity decisive support, natural decisive support… Natural decisive support: relying on non-leading-out faith, one gives alms, observes morality… performs the Uposatha observance, produces jhāna… insight… higher knowledge… produces attainment… indulges in conceit… grasps views; relying on non-leading-out morality… wisdom… lust… aspiration… weather… food… lodging, one gives alms… produces attainment, kills living beings… splits the Saṅgha; non-leading-out faith… lodging is a condition for non-leading-out faith… aspiration… bodily pleasure… bodily pain… fruition-attainment by way of decisive support condition. A non-leading-out phenomenon is a condition for a leading-out phenomenon by way of decisive support condition: object decisive support, proximity decisive support, natural decisive support… Natural decisive support: the preliminary practice for the first path is a condition for the first path by way of decisive support condition… the preliminary practice for the fourth path is a condition for the fourth path by way of decisive support condition. (2)

Purejātapaccayādi

Prenascence Condition, etc.

320. Aniyyāniko [T 4.0509] dhammo aniyyānikassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo… dve (arūpadukasadisā kātabbā)… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… dve… āsevanapaccayena paccayo… dve.

320. A non-leading-out phenomenon is a condition for a non-leading-out phenomenon by way of prenascence condition… two (to be treated like the immaterial dyads)… by way of postnascence condition… two… by way of repetition condition… two.

Kammapaccayo

Kamma Condition

321. Niyyāniko dhammo niyyānikassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – niyyānikā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. Niyyāniko dhammo aniyyānikassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – niyyānikā cetanā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. Nānākkhaṇikā – niyyānikā cetanā phalassa kammapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ) niyyānikā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (3)

321. A leading-out phenomenon is a condition for a leading-out phenomenon by way of kamma condition: leading-out volition is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of kamma condition. A leading-out phenomenon is a condition for a non-leading-out phenomenon by way of kamma condition: co-nascent and at different moments. Co-nascent: leading-out volition is a condition for mind-originated material phenomena by way of kamma condition. At different moments: leading-out volition is a condition for the result by way of kamma condition. (The root should be made) Leading-out volition is a condition for the associated aggregates and mind-originated material phenomena by way of kamma condition. (3)

322. Aniyyāniko [M 4.0178] dhammo aniyyānikassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā (saṃkhittaṃ). Nānākkhaṇikā – aniyyānikā cetanā vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo… vipākapaccayena paccayo… ekaṃyeva… āhārapaccayena paccayo… cattāri… indriyapaccayena paccayo… cattāri… jhānapaccayena paccayo… cattāri… maggapaccayena paccayo… cattāri… sampayuttapaccayena paccayo… dve… vippayuttapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi (arūpadukasadisā kātabbā)… atthipaccayena paccayo… satta (arūpadukasadisā kātabbā, āmasanā nānāpadāyeva)… natthipaccayena paccayo… tīṇi… vigatapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi… avigatapaccayena paccayo… satta.

322. A non-leading-out phenomenon is a condition for a non-leading-out phenomenon by way of kamma condition: co-nascent and at different moments. Co-nascent (in brief). At different moments: non-leading-out volition is a condition for resultant aggregates and kamma-originated material phenomena by way of kamma condition… by way of result condition… one only… by way of nutriment condition… four… by way of faculty condition… four… by way of jhāna condition… four… by way of path condition… four… by way of association condition… two… by way of dissociation condition… three (to be treated like the immaterial dyads)… by way of presence condition… seven (to be treated like the immaterial dyads, the application has different terms)… by way of absence condition… three… by way of disappearance condition… three… by way of non-disappearance condition… seven.

1. Paccayānulomaṃ

1. The Forward Order of Conditions

2. Saṅkhyāvāro

2. Numerical Section

323. Hetuyā [T 4.0510][V 4.0210] cattāri, ārammaṇe tīṇi, adhipatiyā pañca, anantare tīṇi, samanantare tīṇi, sahajāte pañca, aññamaññe dve, nissaye satta, upanissaye cattāri, purejāte dve, pacchājāte dve, āsevane dve, kamme cattāri, vipāke ekaṃ, āhāre cattāri, indriye cattāri, jhāne cattāri, magge cattāri, sampayutte dve, vippayutte tīṇi, atthiyā satta, natthiyā tīṇi, vigate tīṇi, avigate satta.

323. By way of root, four; by way of object, three; by way of predominance, five; by way of contiguity, three; by way of immediacy, three; by way of co-nascence, five; by way of mutuality, two; by way of dependence, seven; by way of decisive support, four; by way of pre-nascence, two; by way of post-nascence, two; by way of repetition, two; by way of kamma, four; by way of result, one; by way of nutriment, four; by way of faculty, four; by way of jhāna, four; by way of path, four; by way of association, two; by way of dissociation, three; by way of presence, seven; by way of absence, three; by way of disappearance, three; by way of non-disappearance, seven.

Anulomaṃ.

Forward Order.

Paccanīyuddhāro

Summary of Opposing Factors

324. Niyyāniko dhammo niyyānikassa dhammassa sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Niyyāniko dhammo aniyyānikassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. Niyyāniko dhammo niyyānikassa ca aniyyānikassa ca dhammassa sahajātapaccayena paccayo. (3)

324. A leading-out phenomenon is a condition for a leading-out phenomenon by way of co-nascence condition... by way of decisive support condition. A leading-out phenomenon is a condition for a non-leading-out phenomenon by way of object condition... by way of co-nascence condition... by way of decisive support condition... by way of post-nascence condition. A leading-out phenomenon is a condition for leading-out and non-leading-out phenomena by way of co-nascence condition. (3)

325. Aniyyāniko dhammo aniyyānikassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena [M 4.0179] paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena paccayo… āhārapaccayena paccayo… indriyapaccayena paccayo. Aniyyāniko dhammo niyyānikassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

325. A non-leading-out phenomenon is a condition for a non-leading-out phenomenon by way of object condition... by way of co-nascence condition... by way of decisive support condition... by way of pre-nascence condition... by way of post-nascence condition... by way of kamma condition... by way of nutriment condition... by way of faculty condition. A non-leading-out phenomenon is a condition for a leading-out phenomenon by way of decisive support condition... by way of pre-nascence condition. (2)

Niyyāniko ca aniyyāniko ca dhammā niyyānikassa dhammassa sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Niyyāniko [T 4.0511] ca aniyyāniko ca dhammā aniyyānikassa dhammassa sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. (3)

Leading-out and non-leading-out phenomena are conditions for a leading-out phenomenon by way of co-nascence and pre-nascence. Leading-out and non-leading-out phenomena are conditions for a non-leading-out phenomenon by way of co-nascence, post-nascence, nutriment, and faculty. (3)

2. Paccayapaccanīyaṃ

2. Conditional Relations and Their Negatives

2. Saṅkhyāvāro

2. Numerical Section

326. Nahetuyā [V 4.0211] satta, naārammaṇe satta, naadhipatiyā satta, naanantare nasamanantare satta, nasahajāte pañca, naaññamaññe pañca, nanissaye pañca, naupanissaye satta, napurejāte cha, napacchājāte satta…pe… nasampayutte pañca, navippayutte cattāri, noatthiyā cattāri, nonatthiyā satta, novigate satta, noavigate cattāri.

326. Not by root condition, seven; not by object, seven; not by predominance, seven; not by contiguity, not by immediacy, seven; not by co-nascence, five; not by mutuality, five; not by dependence, five; not by decisive support, seven; not by pre-nascence, six; not by post-nascence, seven... not by association, five; not by dissociation, four; not by presence, four; not by absence, seven; not by disappearance, seven; not by non-disappearance, four.

3. Paccayānulomapaccanīyaṃ

3. Positive-Negative Enumeration

327. Hetupaccayā naārammaṇe cattāri, naadhipatiyā cattāri, naanantare nasamanantare cattāri, naaññamaññe dve, naupanissaye cattāri …pe… nasampayutte dve, navippayutte dve, nonatthiyā cattāri, novigate cattāri.

327. By root condition, not by object condition, four; not by predominance condition, four; not by contiguity condition, not by immediacy condition, four; not by mutuality condition, two; not by decisive support condition, four... not by association condition, two; not by dissociation condition, two; not by absence condition, four; not by disappearance condition, four.

4. Paccayapaccanīyānulomaṃ

4. Negative-Positive Enumeration

328. Nahetupaccayā ārammaṇe tīṇi, adhipatiyā pañca (anulomamātikā vitthāretabbā)…pe… avigate satta.

328. Not by root condition, by object, three; by predominance, five (the forward order matrix should be expanded)... by non-disappearance, seven.

Niyyānikadukaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Leading-out Dyad is finished.

98. Niyatadukaṃ

98. The Fixed Dyad

1-6. Paṭiccavārādi

1-6. Dependent Origination, etc.

329. Niyataṃ [M 4.0180] dhammaṃ paṭicca niyato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā [T 4.0512] – niyataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. Niyataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca aniyato dhammo uppajjati [V 4.0212] hetupaccayā – niyate khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ. Pañcapi pañhā kātabbā. Yathā niyyānikadukaṃ evaṃ paṭiccavāropi sahajātavāropi paccayavāropi nissayavāropi saṃsaṭṭhavāropi sampayuttavāropi kātabbā, ninnānākaraṇaṃ āmasanaṃ nānaṃ).

329. A fixed phenomenon arises dependent on a fixed phenomenon by way of root condition—dependent on one fixed aggregate, three aggregates arise…pe… dependent on two aggregates…pe…. A non-fixed phenomenon arises dependent on a fixed phenomenon by way of root condition—dependent on fixed aggregates, mind-originated form arises (condensed). The fivefold method should be applied. Just as with the Leading-out Dyad, so also the Dependent Origination Section, the Co-nascence Section, the Condition Section, the Dependence Section, the Conjunction Section, and the Association Section should be treated similarly, with no differentiation; the application is not different.

7. Pañhāvāro

7. Question Section

1. Paccayānulomaṃ

1. The Forward Order of Conditions

1. Vibhaṅgavāro

1. The Chapter on Distinctions

Hetupaccayo

The Root Condition

330. Niyato dhammo niyatassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo… cattāri (niyyānikadukasadisā ninnānākaraṇā).

330. A fixed phenomenon is a condition for a fixed phenomenon by way of root condition... four (similar to the Leading-out Dyad, without differentiation).

Ārammaṇapaccayo

The Object Condition

331. Niyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ paccavekkhanti, niyate pahīne kilese paccavekkhanti, pubbe samudāciṇṇe…pe… niyate khandhe aniccato…pe… vipassati, cetopariyañāṇena niyatacittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānāti, niyatā khandhā cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

331. A fixed phenomenon is a condition for a non-fixed phenomenon by way of object condition—noble ones, having emerged from the path, review the path; they review the fixed abandoned defilements; previously practiced… and so on… one discerns the fixed aggregates as impermanent… and so on… with the knowledge of others’ minds, one knows the mind of one endowed with a fixed mind; the fixed aggregates are a condition for the knowledge of others’ minds, for the knowledge of past lives, for the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their deeds, for the knowledge of the future, and for adverting, by way of object condition. (1)

Aniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ…pe… pubbe suciṇṇāni…pe… jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā jhānaṃ paccavekkhati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha aniyato rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi…pe… vicikicchā…pe… uddhaccaṃ…pe… aniyataṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati, ariyā phalaṃ paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ [T 4.0513] paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa[M 4.0181], vodānassa, phalassa, āvajjanāya [V 4.0213] ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo; ariyā aniyate pahīne kilese paccavekkhanti, vikkhambhite kilese…pe… pubbe samudāciṇṇe…pe… cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniyate khandhe aniccato…pe… vipassati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha aniyato rāgo…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati, dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati…pe… āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Aniyato dhammo niyatassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo; nibbānaṃ maggassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo; rūpajīvitindriyaṃ mātughātikammassa… pitughātikammassa… arahantaghātikammassa… ruhiruppādakammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo; yaṃ vatthuṃ āmasantassa micchattaniyatā khandhā uppajjanti, taṃ vatthu micchattaniyatānaṃ khandhānaṃ ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A non-fixed phenomenon is a condition for a non-fixed phenomenon by way of object condition—having given a gift, observed moral precepts... performed the Uposatha observance... previously well-practiced... emerging from jhāna, one reviews the jhāna, enjoys it, welcomes it; taking that as object, non-fixed lust arises, wrong view... doubt... restlessness... non-fixed displeasure arises. Noble ones review fruition, review Nibbāna; Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage, for purification, for fruition, and for adverting, by way of object condition. Noble ones review the non-fixed abandoned defilements, the suppressed defilements... previously practiced... the eye... the physical basis; one discerns the non-fixed aggregates as impermanent... enjoys them, welcomes them; taking them as object, non-fixed lust... displeasure arises. With the divine eye one sees a form... for adverting, it is a condition by way of object condition. A non-fixed phenomenon is a condition for a fixed phenomenon by way of object condition. Nibbāna is a condition for the path by way of object condition. The material life faculty is a condition for the act of matricide... for the act of patricide... for the act of killing an arahant... for the act of shedding a Buddha's blood, by way of object condition. That physical basis which, when one misappropriates it, gives rise to aggregates fixed in wrongness—that physical basis is a condition for the aggregates fixed in wrongness by way of object condition. (2)

Adhipatipaccayo

Dominance Condition

332. Niyato dhammo niyatassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – niyatādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Niyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti. Sahajātādhipati – niyatādhipati cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Niyato dhammo niyatassa ca aniyatassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – niyatādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ [T 4.0514] khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (3)

332. A fixed phenomenon is a condition for a fixed phenomenon by way of dominance condition. Conascence-dominance: a fixed dominant factor is a condition for its associated aggregates by way of dominance condition. A fixed phenomenon is a condition for a non-fixed phenomenon by way of dominance condition: object-dominance, conascence-dominance. Object-dominance: noble ones, having emerged from the path, review the path, holding it in high esteem. Conascence-dominance: a fixed dominant factor is a condition for mind-originated matter by way of dominance condition. A fixed phenomenon is a condition for a fixed phenomenon and for a non-fixed phenomenon by way of dominance condition. Conascence-dominance: a fixed dominant factor is a condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter by way of dominance condition. (3)

333. Aniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā aniyato rāgo uppajjati… diṭṭhi uppajjati; pubbe…pe… jhānā…pe… ariyā phalaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, phalassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo; cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniyate khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā aniyato rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – aniyatādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca [M 4.0182] rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena [V 4.0214] paccayo. Aniyato dhammo niyatassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – nibbānaṃ maggassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (2)

333. A non-fixed phenomenon is a condition for a non-fixed phenomenon by way of dominance condition: object-dominance, conascence-dominance. Object-dominance: having given a gift, undertaken morality… performed the Uposatha observance, one reviews it, holding it in high esteem, enjoys it, and delights in it. Holding it in high esteem, non-fixed lust arises… wrong view arises; previously… jhānas… noble ones review fruition, holding it in high esteem; they review Nibbāna, holding it in high esteem. Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage, for purification, and for fruition by way of dominance condition. The eye… the physical basis; holding the non-fixed aggregates in high esteem, one enjoys them and delights in them. Holding them in high esteem, non-fixed lust arises, wrong view arises. Conascence-dominance: a non-fixed dominant factor is a condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter by way of dominance condition. A non-fixed phenomenon is a condition for a fixed phenomenon by way of dominance condition. Object-dominance: Nibbāna is a condition for the path by way of dominance condition. (2)

Anantarapaccayādi

Proximity Condition, etc.

334. Niyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – maggo phalassa anantarapaccayena paccayo, niyatā khandhā vuṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

334. A fixed phenomenon is a condition for a non-fixed phenomenon by way of proximity condition—the path is a condition for fruition by way of proximity condition; the fixed aggregates are a condition for emergence by way of proximity condition. (1)

Aniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā aniyatā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ aniyatānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; anulomaṃ gotrabhussa… anulomaṃ vodānassa… phalaṃ phalassa… anulomaṃ phalasamāpattiyā… nirodhā vuṭṭhahantassa nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ phalasamāpattiyā [T 4.0515] anantarapaccayena paccayo. Aniyato dhammo niyatassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – aniyataṃ domanassaṃ niyatassa domanassassa, aniyatā micchādiṭṭhi niyatamicchādiṭṭhiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo; gotrabhu maggassa… vodānaṃ maggassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A non-fixed phenomenon is a condition for a non-fixed phenomenon by way of proximity condition—preceding non-fixed aggregates are a condition for subsequent non-fixed aggregates by way of proximity condition; adaptation is a condition for change-of-lineage… adaptation is a condition for purification… fruition is a condition for fruition… adaptation is a condition for fruition attainment… for one emerging from cessation, the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a condition for fruition attainment by way of proximity condition. A non-fixed phenomenon is a condition for a fixed phenomenon by way of proximity condition—non-fixed displeasure is a condition for fixed displeasure; non-fixed wrong view is a condition for fixed wrong view by way of proximity condition; change-of-lineage is a condition for the path… purification is a condition for the path by way of proximity condition. (2)

Samanantarapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… pañca… aññamaññapaccayena paccayo… dve… nissayapaccayena paccayo… satta.

Contiguity Condition… Conascence Condition… five… Mutuality Condition… two… Support Condition… seven.

Upanissayapaccayo

Decisive Support Condition

335. Niyato dhammo niyatassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Pakatūpanissayo – mātughātikammaṃ mātughātikammassa… pitughātikammassa… arahantaghātikammassa… ruhiruppādakammassa… saṅghabhedakammassa, niyatamicchādiṭṭhiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo (cakkaṃ). Paṭhamo maggo dutiyassa maggassa…pe… tatiyo maggo catutthassa maggassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Niyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – mātaraṃ jīvitā voropetvā…pe… saṅghaṃ bhinditvā tassa paṭighātatthāya dānaṃ deti, sīlaṃ samādiyati, uposathakammaṃ [M 4.0183] karoti, ariyā [V 4.0215] maggaṃ upanissāya anuppannaṃ samāpattiṃ uppādenti, uppannaṃ samāpajjanti…pe… ṭhānāṭhānakosallassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo; maggo phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

335. A determinate phenomenon is a condition for a determinate phenomenon by way of decisive support condition. Natural Decisive Support: The act of matricide is a condition for the act of matricide… for the act of patricide… for the act of killing an Arahant… for the act of causing the Buddha's blood to flow… for the act of causing a schism in the Saṅgha, and for determinate wrong view by way of decisive support condition (a cycle). The first path is a condition for the second path… the third path is a condition for the fourth path by way of decisive support condition. A determinate phenomenon is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon by way of decisive support condition: Object Decisive Support, Proximity Decisive Support, Natural Decisive Support… and so on. Natural Decisive Support: Having deprived one's mother of life… having caused a schism in the Saṅgha, one gives alms to counter that, undertakes precepts, performs the Uposatha observance. The noble ones arouse unarisen attainments by relying on the path, and attain the arisen ones… and so on; skill in what is possible and what is not possible is a condition by way of decisive support condition; the path is a condition for fruition attainment by way of decisive support condition. (2)

336. Aniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena [T 4.0516] paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – aniyataṃ saddhaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti, sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ karoti, jhānaṃ uppādeti, vipassanaṃ…pe… abhiññaṃ…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti, mānaṃ jappeti… diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti; aniyataṃ sīlaṃ…pe… paññaṃ… rāgaṃ…pe… patthanaṃ… kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ… kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ… utuṃ… bhojanaṃ… senāsanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti, pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… nigamaghātaṃ karoti, aniyatā saddhā…pe… senāsanaṃ aniyatāya saddhāya…pe… patthanāya… kāyikassa sukhassa… kāyikassa dukkhassa, phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

336. An indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon by way of decisive support condition: Object Decisive Support, Proximity Decisive Support, Natural Decisive Support… and so on. Natural Decisive Support: Relying on indeterminate faith, one gives alms, undertakes precepts… performs the Uposatha observance, arouses jhāna… develops insight… arouses higher knowledge… arouses attainment, indulges in conceit… grasps wrong views; relying on indeterminate virtue… wisdom… lust… aspiration… bodily pleasure… bodily pain… climate… food… lodging, one gives alms… arouses attainment, kills living beings… commits the destruction of a town. Indeterminate faith… lodging is a condition for indeterminate faith… aspiration… bodily pleasure… bodily pain, and for fruition attainment by way of decisive support condition. (1)

Aniyato dhammo niyatassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – aniyataṃ rāgaṃ upanissāya mātaraṃ jīvitā voropeti…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; aniyataṃ dosaṃ…pe… senāsanaṃ upanissāya mātaraṃ jīvitā voropeti…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; aniyato rāgo… dosaṃ…pe… senāsanaṃ mātughātikammassa…pe… saṅghabhedakammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo; paṭhamassa maggassa parikammaṃ paṭhamassa maggassa…pe… catutthassa maggassa parikammaṃ catutthassa maggassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for a determinate phenomenon by way of decisive support condition: Object Decisive Support, Proximity Decisive Support, Natural Decisive Support… and so on. Natural Decisive Support: Relying on indeterminate lust, one deprives one’s mother of life… causes a schism in the Saṅgha; relying on indeterminate hatred… lodging, one deprives one’s mother of life… causes a schism in the Saṅgha. Indeterminate lust… hatred… lodging is a condition for the act of matricide… for the act of causing a schism in the Saṅgha by way of decisive support condition; the preliminary work for the first path is a condition for the first path… the preliminary work for the fourth path is a condition for the fourth path by way of decisive support condition. (2)

Purejātapaccayādi

By way of Pre-nascence Condition, etc.

337. Aniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ). Aniyato dhammo niyatassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ[T 4.0517], vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – rūpajīvitindriyaṃ mātughātikammassa… pitughātikammassa… arahantaghātikammassa… ruhiruppādakammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo. Vatthupurejātaṃ – vatthu niyatānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

337. An indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon by way of pre-nascence condition—object pre-nascence, base pre-nascence (in brief). An indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for a determinate phenomenon by way of pre-nascence condition—object pre-nascence, base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence—the form life faculty is a condition for the act of killing one’s mother… killing one’s father… killing an arahant… causing blood to flow, by way of pre-nascence condition. Base pre-nascence—the base is a condition for determinate aggregates by way of pre-nascence condition. (2)

Pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… dve… āsevanapaccayena paccayo… dve.

It is a condition by way of post-nascence condition… two. It is a condition by way of repetition condition… two.

Kammapaccayo

Kamma Condition

338. Niyato [M 4.0184][V 4.0216] dhammo niyatassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – niyatā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. Niyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – niyatā cetanā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. Nānākkhaṇikā – niyatā cetanā vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Niyatā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (3)

338. A determinate phenomenon is a condition for a determinate phenomenon by way of kamma condition—determinate volition is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of kamma condition. A determinate phenomenon is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon by way of kamma condition—conascent and asynchronous. Conascent—determinate volition is a condition for mind-produced material phenomena by way of kamma condition. Asynchronous—determinate volition is a condition for the resultant aggregates and for materiality produced by that kamma by way of kamma condition. (The root should be done.) Determinate volition is a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-produced material phenomena by way of kamma condition. (3)

Aniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā (saṃkhittaṃ).

An indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon by way of kamma condition—conascent, asynchronous (in brief).

Vipākapaccayena paccayo… ekaṃ… āhārapaccayena paccayo… cattāri… indriyapaccayena paccayo… cattāri… jhānapaccayena paccayo… cattāri… maggapaccayena paccayo… cattāri… sampayuttapaccayena paccayo… dve… vippayuttapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi (arūpadukasadisaṃ)… atthipaccayena paccayo… satta (arūpāvacaradukasadisaṃ)… natthipaccayena paccayo… vigatapaccayena paccayo… avigatapaccayena paccayo… satta.

It is a condition by way of result condition… one… It is a condition by way of nutriment condition… four… It is a condition by way of faculty condition… four… It is a condition by way of jhāna condition… four… It is a condition by way of path condition… four… It is a condition by way of association condition… two… It is a condition by way of dissociation condition… three (similar to the immaterial dyad)… It is a condition by way of presence condition… seven (similar to the immaterial-sphere dyad)… It is a condition by way of absence condition… It is a condition by way of disappearance condition… It is a condition by way of non-disappearance condition… seven.

1. Paccayānulomaṃ

1. The Positive Exposition of Conditions

2. Saṅkhyāvāro

2. Numerical Section

339. Hetuyā [T 4.0518] cattāri, ārammaṇe tīṇi, adhipatiyā pañca, anantare tīṇi, samanantare tīṇi, sahajāte pañca, aññamaññe dve, nissaye satta, upanissaye cattāri, purejāte dve, pacchājāte dve, āsevane dve, kamme cattāri, vipāke ekaṃ, āhāre cattāri, indriye jhāne cattāri, magge cattāri, sampayutte dve, vippayutte tīṇi, atthiyā satta, natthiyā tīṇi, vigate tīṇi, avigate satta.

339. In root condition, four; in object, three; in dominance, five; in proximity, three; in contiguity, three; in conascence, five; in mutuality, two; in dependence, seven; in decisive support, four; in pre-nascence, two; in post-nascence, two; in repetition, two; in kamma, four; in result, one; in nutriment, four; in faculty and jhāna, four; in path, four; in association, two; in dissociation, three; in presence, seven; in absence, three; in disappearance, three; in non-disappearance, seven.

2. Paccanīyuddhāro

2. The Negative Exposition

340. Niyato [V 4.0217] dhammo niyatassa dhammassa sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Niyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena [M 4.0185] paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena paccayo. Niyato dhammo niyatassa ca aniyatassa ca dhammassa sahajātapaccayena paccayo. (3)

340. A determinate phenomenon is a condition for a determinate phenomenon by way of co-nascence condition… by way of strong dependence condition. A determinate phenomenon is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon by way of object condition… by way of co-nascence condition… by way of strong dependence condition… by way of post-nascence condition… by way of kamma condition. A determinate phenomenon is a condition for determinate and indeterminate phenomena by way of co-nascence condition. (3)

341. Aniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena paccayo… āhārapaccayena paccayo… indriyapaccayena paccayo. Aniyato dhammo niyatassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

341. An indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon by way of object condition… by way of co-nascence condition… by way of strong dependence condition… by way of pre-nascence condition… by way of post-nascence condition… by way of kamma condition… by way of nutriment condition… by way of faculty condition. An indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for a determinate phenomenon by way of object condition… by way of strong dependence condition… by way of pre-nascence condition. (2)

Niyato [T 4.0519] ca aniyato ca dhammā niyatassa dhammassa sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Niyato ca aniyato ca dhammā aniyatassa dhammassa sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. (2)

Determinate and indeterminate phenomena are a condition for a determinate phenomenon by way of co-nascence condition and pre-nascence condition. Determinate and indeterminate phenomena are a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon by way of co-nascence condition, post-nascence condition, nutriment condition, and faculty condition. (2)

342. Nahetuyā satta, naārammaṇe satta, naadhipatiyā satta, naanantare nasamanantare satta, nasahajāte pañca, naaññamaññe pañca, nanissaye pañca, naupanissaye satta, napurejāte cha, napacchājāte satta…pe… nasampayutte pañca, navippayutte cattāri, noatthiyā cattāri, nonatthiyā satta, novigate satta, noavigate cattāri.

342. Not by root condition seven, not by object condition seven, not by dominance condition seven, not by contiguity condition nor by immediate contiguity condition seven, not by co-nascence condition five, not by reciprocity condition five, not by dependence condition five, not by strong dependence condition seven, not by pre-nascence condition six, not by post-nascence condition seven…pe… not by association condition five, not by dissociation condition four, not by presence condition four, not by absence condition seven, not by disappearance condition seven, not by non-disappearance condition four.

343. Hetupaccayā naārammaṇe cattāri, naadhipatiyā cattāri, naanantare nasamanantare cattāri[V 4.0218], naaññamaññe dve, naupanissaye cattāri…pe… nasampayutte dve, navippayutte dve, nonatthiyā cattāri, novigate cattāri.

343. By root condition, not by object condition four, not by dominance condition four, not by contiguity condition nor by immediate contiguity condition four, not by reciprocity condition two, not by strong dependence condition four…pe…not by association condition two, not by dissociation condition two, not by absence condition four, not by disappearance condition four.

4. Paccayapaccanīyānulomaṃ

4. Contrariety and Conformity of Conditions

344. Nahetupaccayā ārammaṇe tīṇi, adhipatiyā pañca (anulomamātikā vitthāretabbā)…pe… avigate satta.

344. Not by root condition, by object condition three, by dominance condition five (the outline of conformity should be expanded)…pe…by non-disappearance condition seven.

99. Sauttaradukaṃ

345. Sauttaraṃ [T 4.0520][M 4.0186] dhammaṃ paṭicca sauttaro dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – sauttaraṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (Yāva ajjhattikā mahābhūtā. Yathā cūḷantaraduke lokiyadukasadisaṃ ninnānākaraṇaṃ.)

345. A mundane phenomenon arises dependent on a mundane phenomenon by way of root condition—dependent on one mundane aggregate, three aggregates and mind-produced materiality arise…pe… dependent on two aggregates…pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking…pe…. (Up to the internal great elements. The differentiation is similar to that in the Lesser Internal Dyad and the Worldly Dyad, with no differences made.)

Hetupaccayo

The Root Condition

346. Saraṇaṃ [V 4.0219] dhammaṃ paṭicca saraṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – saraṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (Pañca pañhā arūpāvacaradukasadisā, anulomapaṭiccasadisā.)

346. A phenomenon with defilements arises dependent on a phenomenon with defilements by way of root condition—dependent on one aggregate with defilements, three aggregates arise…pe… dependent on two aggregates…pe…. (Five questions, similar to the Immaterial Sphere Dyad, similar to the direct conditionality.)

Hetuyā pañca, ārammaṇe dve, adhipatiyā pañca…pe… avigate pañca.

By root condition five, by object condition two, by dominance condition five…pe… by non-disappearance condition five.

Anulomaṃ.

Conformity.

Saraṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca saraṇo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā [T 4.0521] – vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe paṭicca vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho. (1)

A phenomenon with defilements arises dependent on a phenomenon with defilements not by way of root condition: dependent on the aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness, the delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness arises. (1)

Araṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca araṇo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ araṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… (yāva asaññasattā). (1)

A phenomenon without defilements arises dependent on a phenomenon without defilements not by way of root condition—dependent on one rootless, undefiled aggregate, three aggregates and mind-produced materiality arise…pe… dependent on two aggregates…pe… at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking…pe… (up to non-percipient beings). (1)

Nahetuyā dve, naārammaṇe tīṇi, naadhipatiyā pañca, naanantare tīṇi, naupanissaye tīṇi, napurejāte cattāri, napacchājāte pañca, naāsevane pañca, nakamme dve, navipāke pañca, naāhāre ekaṃ, naindriye [M 4.0187] ekaṃ, najhāne ekaṃ, namagge ekaṃ, nasampayutte tīṇi, navippayutte dve, nonatthiyā tīṇi, novigate tīṇi.

Not by root condition, two; not by object condition, three; not by dominance condition, five; not by contiguity condition, three; not by strong dependence condition, three; not by pre-nascence condition, four; not by post-nascence condition, five; not by repetition condition, five; not by kamma condition, two; not by result condition, five; not by nutriment condition, one; not by faculty condition, one; not by absorption condition, one; not by path condition, one; not by association condition, three; not by dissociation condition, two; not by absence condition, three; not by disappearance condition, three.

Paccanīyaṃ.

Contrariety.

347. Saraṇaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā saraṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – saraṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paccayā tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… (yathā arūpāvacaradukassa paccayavāropi evaṃ kātabbo).

347. A phenomenon with defilements is a condition for a phenomenon with defilements to arise by way of root condition—one aggregate with defilements is a condition for three aggregates…and so on…two aggregates…and so on…(the conditional relations section of the Immaterial Sphere Dyad should also be done in the same way).

Hetuyā nava, ārammaṇe cattāri, adhipatiyā nava…pe… avigate nava.

By root condition nine, by object condition four, by dominance condition nine…and so on…by non-disappearance condition nine.

Anulomaṃ.

Forward Order.

348. Saraṇaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā saraṇo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe paccayā vicikicchāsahagato [T 4.0522] uddhaccasahagato moho. (1)

348. A phenomenon with defilements is a condition for a phenomenon with defilements to arise by way of not-root condition—the aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness are a condition for the delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness. (1)

Araṇaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā araṇo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ araṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paccayā tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… (yāva asaññasattā) cakkhāyatanaṃ paccayā cakkhuviññāṇaṃ…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ paccayā kāyaviññāṇaṃ, vatthuṃ paccayā ahetukā khandhā. Araṇaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā saraṇo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – vatthuṃ paccayā vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho. (2)

A phenomenon without defilements is a condition for a phenomenon without defilements to arise by way of not-root condition—one rootless, undefiled aggregate is a condition for three aggregates and mind-produced materiality…and so on…two aggregates…and so on…at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking…and so on…(up to non-percipient beings)—the eye base is a condition for eye-consciousness…and so on…the body base is a condition for body-consciousness; the physical base is a condition for rootless aggregates. A phenomenon without defilements is a condition for a phenomenon with defilements to arise by way of not-root condition—the physical base is a condition for the delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness. (2)

Saraṇañca araṇañca dhammaṃ paccayā saraṇo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – vicikicchāsahagate [V 4.0221] uddhaccasahagate khandhe ca vatthuñca paccayā vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho. (1)

A phenomenon with defilements and a phenomenon without defilements are conditions for a phenomenon with defilements to arise by way of not-root condition—the aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness and the physical base are conditions for the delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness. (1)

Nahetuyā [M 4.0188] cattāri, naārammaṇe tīṇi, naadhipatiyā nava, naanantare tīṇi, nasamanantare tīṇi, naaññamaññe tīṇi, naupanissaye tīṇi, napurejāte cattāri, napacchājāte nava, naāsevane nava, nakamme cattāri, navipāke nava, naāhāre ekaṃ, naindriye ekaṃ, najhāne ekaṃ, namagge ekaṃ, nasampayutte tīṇi, navippayutte dve, nonatthiyā tīṇi, novigate tīṇi.

Not by root condition, four; not by object condition, three; not by dominance condition, nine; not by contiguity condition, three; not by immediate contiguity condition, three; not by mutuality condition, three; not by proximate dependence condition, three; not by prenascent condition, four; not by postnascent condition, nine; not by repetition condition, nine; not by action condition, four; not by result condition, nine; not by nutriment condition, one; not by faculty condition, one; not by absorption condition, one; not by path condition, one; not by association condition, three; not by dissociation condition, two; not by absence condition, three; not by disappearance condition, three.

Paccanīyaṃ.

Negative.

Not by root condition, two; not by dominance condition, two; not by prenascent condition, two; not by postnascent condition, two; not by repetition condition, two; not by kamma condition, two; not by result condition, two; not by jhāna condition, one; not by path condition, one; not by dissociation condition, two (Negative).
