Hetupaccayo

The Root Condition

349. Saraṇo [V 4.0222] dhammo saraṇassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo (arūpadukasadisaṃ, cattāri).

349. A defiled phenomenon is a condition for a defiled phenomenon by way of the root condition (similar to the immaterial dyad, four).

Ārammaṇapaccayo

The Object Condition

350. Saraṇo dhammo saraṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – rāgaṃ assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi…pe… vicikicchā…pe… uddhaccaṃ…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati, diṭṭhiṃ assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati, vicikicchaṃ ārabbha [M 4.0189] …pe… uddhaccaṃ ārabbha…pe… domanassaṃ ārabbha domanassaṃ uppajjati, diṭṭhi…pe… vicikicchā…pe… uddhaccaṃ uppajjati. Saraṇo dhammo araṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – ariyā pahīne kilese…pe… vikkhambhite kilese…pe… pubbe samudāciṇṇe…pe… saraṇe khandhe aniccato…pe… vipassati, cetopariyañāṇena saraṇacittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānāti. Saraṇā khandhā cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (2)

350. A defiled phenomenon is a condition for a defiled phenomenon by way of the object condition. One savors and delights in lust; taking that as object, lust arises. Taking views… doubt… restlessness… as object, sorrow arises. One savors and delights in views; taking that as object, lust arises… sorrow arises. Taking doubt as object… taking restlessness as object… taking sorrow as object, sorrow arises. Views… doubt… restlessness arise. A defiled phenomenon is a condition for an undefiled phenomenon by way of the object condition. Noble ones review the abandoned defilements… the suppressed defilements… previously practiced defilements… they see the defiled aggregates with insight as impermanent… With the knowledge of the minds of others, one knows the mind of one who is associated with a defiled mind. The defiled aggregates are a condition for the knowledge of the minds of others, the knowledge of past lives, the knowledge of the destiny of beings according to their actions, the knowledge of the future, and for adverting, by way of the object condition. (2)

351. Araṇo dhammo araṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo; dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ paccavekkhati, pubbe…pe… jhānā…pe… ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ paccavekkhanti, phalaṃ…pe… nibbānaṃ paccavekkhanti; nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa[T 4.0524], vodānassa, maggassa, phalassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ araṇe khandhe aniccato…pe… vipassati, dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati [V 4.0223]…pe… anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Araṇo dhammo saraṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati…pe… pubbe…pe… jhānā…pe… cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ, araṇe khandhe assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. (2)

351. An undefiled phenomenon is a condition for an undefiled phenomenon by way of the object condition. Having given a gift… observed moral conduct… performed the Uposatha observance, one reviews it. Having previously… jhānas… having emerged from the noble paths, noble ones review the path, they review the fruit… they review Nibbāna. Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage, for purification, for the path, for the fruit, and for adverting, by way of the object condition. One sees the eye… the physical base… the undefiled aggregates with insight as impermanent… With the divine eye one sees a form… for the knowledge of the future, and for adverting, it is a condition by way of the object condition. An undefiled phenomenon is a condition for a defiled phenomenon by way of the object condition. Having given a gift… observed moral conduct… performed the Uposatha observance, one savors and delights in it; taking that as object, lust arises… Previously… jhānas… one savors and delights in the eye… the physical base, the undefiled aggregates; taking them as object, lust arises… sorrow arises. (2)

Adhipatipaccayo

The Dominance Condition

352. Saraṇo dhammo saraṇassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – rāgaṃ garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati… diṭṭhi uppajjati; diṭṭhiṃ garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati. Sahajātādhipati – saraṇādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Saraṇo dhammo araṇassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – saraṇādhipati cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Saraṇo dhammo saraṇassa ca araṇassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – saraṇādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (3)

352. A defiled phenomenon is a condition for a defiled phenomenon by way of the dominance condition—object dominance and conascence dominance. Object dominance: One regards lust as important, relishes and approves of it; regarding it as important, lust arises… wrong view arises; one regards wrong view as important, relishes and approves of it. Conascence dominance: The dominant defiled phenomenon is a condition by way of the dominance condition for the associated aggregates. A defiled phenomenon is a condition for an undefiled phenomenon by way of the dominance condition. Conascence dominance: The dominant defiled phenomenon is a condition by way of the dominance condition for mind-originated materiality. A defiled phenomenon is a condition for both defiled and undefiled phenomena by way of the dominance condition. Conascence dominance: The dominant defiled phenomenon is a condition by way of the dominance condition for the associated aggregates and mind-originated materiality. (3)

353. Araṇo [M 4.0190] dhammo araṇassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ [T 4.0525] …pe… uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati, pubbe…pe… jhānā…pe… ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti, phalaṃ…pe… nibbānaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, maggassa, phalassa, adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – araṇādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Araṇo dhammo saraṇassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ…pe… sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati… diṭṭhi uppajjati; pubbe suciṇṇāni…pe… jhānā…pe… cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ, araṇe khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati… diṭṭhi uppajjati. (2)

353. An undefiled phenomenon is a condition for an undefiled phenomenon by way of the dominance condition—object dominance and conascence dominance. Object dominance: Having performed generosity… morality… the observance of the Uposatha, one reflects upon it, holding it in high regard. Previously… jhānas… having emerged from the noble paths, the noble ones reflect upon the path, holding it in high regard; they reflect upon the fruit… they reflect upon Nibbāna, holding it in high regard. Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage, for purification, for the path, and for the fruit by way of the dominance condition. Conascence dominance: The dominant undefiled phenomenon is a condition for the associated aggregates and mind-originated materiality by way of the dominance condition. An undefiled phenomenon is a condition for a defiled phenomenon by way of the dominance condition. Object dominance: Having performed generosity… morality… the observance of the Uposatha, one savors and rejoices in it; having esteemed it, lust arises… wrong view arises. Previously well-practiced… jhānas… the eye… the base, one savors and rejoices in the undefiled aggregates; having esteemed them, lust arises… wrong view arises. (2)

Anantarapaccayādi

Contiguity Condition, and so on.

354. Saraṇo [V 4.0224] dhammo saraṇassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā saraṇā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ saraṇānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. Saraṇo dhammo araṇassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – saraṇā khandhā vuṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

354. A defiled phenomenon is a condition for a defiled phenomenon by way of the contiguity condition—the preceding defiled aggregates are a condition for the subsequent defiled aggregates by way of the contiguity condition. A defiled phenomenon is a condition for an undefiled phenomenon by way of the contiguity condition—the defiled aggregates are a condition for emergence by way of the contiguity condition. (2)

355. Araṇo dhammo araṇassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā araṇā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ araṇānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; anulomaṃ gotrabhussa…pe… phalasamāpattiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. Araṇo dhammo saraṇassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – āvajjanā saraṇānaṃ [T 4.0526] khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

355. An undefiled phenomenon is a condition for an undefiled phenomenon by way of the contiguity condition—the preceding undefiled aggregates are a condition for the subsequent undefiled aggregates by way of the contiguity condition; conformity is a condition for change-of-lineage… and so on… for fruition attainment by way of the contiguity condition. An undefiled phenomenon is a condition for a defiled phenomenon by way of the contiguity condition—adverting is a condition for the defiled aggregates by way of the contiguity condition. (2)

Samanantarapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… pañca… aññamaññapaccayena paccayo… dve… nissayapaccayena paccayo… satta.

By way of proximity condition… By way of conascence condition… in five ways. By way of mutuality condition… in two ways. By way of support condition… in seven ways.

Upanissayapaccayo

Decisive Support Condition.

356. Saraṇo dhammo saraṇassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo [M 4.0191] – rāgaṃ upanissāya pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; dosaṃ…pe… patthanaṃ upanissāya pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati, rāgo…pe… patthanā rāgassa…pe… patthanāya upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Saraṇo dhammo araṇassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – rāgaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti, sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ karoti, jhānaṃ uppādeti, vipassanaṃ…pe… maggaṃ…pe… abhiññaṃ…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti; dosaṃ…pe… patthanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti, rāgo…pe… patthanā saddhāya…pe… paññāya… kāyikassa sukhassa… kāyikassa dukkhassa… maggassa… phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

356. A defiled phenomenon is a condition for a defiled phenomenon by way of the decisive support condition—object decisive support, contiguity decisive support, natural decisive support, and so on. Natural decisive support: Relying on lust, one kills a living being… and so on… up to splitting the Saṅgha; relying on hatred… and so on… up to longing, one kills a living being… and so on… up to splitting the Saṅgha. Lust… and so on… up to longing, is a condition for lust… and so on… up to longing, by way of the decisive support condition. A defiled phenomenon is a condition for an undefiled phenomenon by way of the decisive support condition—contiguity decisive support, natural decisive support, and so on. Natural decisive support: Relying on lust, one gives a gift, undertakes the moral precepts… and so on… performs the Uposatha observance, generates jhāna, develops insight… and so on… the path… and so on… higher knowledge… and so on… generates meditative attainment; relying on hatred… and so on… up to longing, one gives a gift… and so on… generates meditative attainment. Lust… and so on… up to longing, is a condition for faith… and so on… up to wisdom, for bodily pleasure, for bodily pain, for the path, and for fruition-attainment by way of the decisive support condition. (2)

357. Araṇo dhammo araṇassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo[V 4.0225], anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – saddhaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti; sīlaṃ…pe… paññaṃ… kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ… kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ… utuṃ… bhojanaṃ… senāsanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti; saddhā [T 4.0527] …pe… senāsanaṃ saddhāya…pe… paññāya… kāyikassa sukhassa… kāyikassa dukkhassa… maggassa… phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

357. An undefiled phenomenon is a condition for an undefiled phenomenon by way of the decisive support condition—object decisive support, contiguity decisive support, natural decisive support, and so on. Natural decisive support: Relying on faith, one gives a gift… and so on… generates meditative attainment; relying on moral virtue… and so on… wisdom, bodily pleasure, bodily pain, climate, food, and lodging, one gives a gift… and so on… generates meditative attainment. Faith… and so on… up to lodging, is a condition for faith… and so on… up to wisdom, for bodily pleasure, for bodily pain, for the path, and for fruition-attainment by way of the decisive support condition. (1)

Araṇo dhammo saraṇassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – saddhaṃ upanissāya mānaṃ jappeti, diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti; sīlaṃ…pe… senāsanaṃ upanissāya pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati; saddhā…pe… senāsanaṃ rāgassa…pe… patthanāya upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An undefiled phenomenon is a condition for a defiled phenomenon by way of the decisive support condition—object decisive support, contiguity decisive support, natural decisive support, and so on. Natural decisive support: Relying on faith, one generates conceit, grasps a wrong view; relying on moral virtue… and so on… up to lodging, one kills a living being… and so on… up to splitting the Saṅgha. Faith… and so on… up to lodging, is a condition for lust… and so on… up to longing, by way of the decisive support condition. (2)

Purejātapaccayādi

Prenascence Condition, and so on.

358. Araṇo dhammo araṇassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… vipassati…pe… dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti, rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe…. Vatthupurejātaṃ – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa [M 4.0192] …pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… vatthu araṇānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. Araṇo dhammo saraṇassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. Vatthupurejātaṃ – vatthu saraṇānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

358. The unafflicted state is a condition for the unafflicted state by way of pre-nascence condition—object pre-nascence, base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: The eye, and so on, up to the base—one contemplates as impermanent, and so on, up to developing insight, and so on; with the divine eye, one sees forms; with the divine ear element, one hears sounds; the form base is a condition for eye-consciousness, and so on, up to the tangible base being a condition for body-consciousness, and so on. Base pre-nascence: The eye base is a condition for eye-consciousness, and so on, up to the body base being a condition for body-consciousness, and so on; the base is a condition for the unafflicted aggregates by way of pre-nascence condition. The unafflicted state is a condition for the afflicted state by way of pre-nascence condition—object pre-nascence, base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: The eye, and so on, up to the base—one savors, rejoices in; based on that, lust arises, and so on, up to sorrow arising. Base pre-nascence: The base is a condition for the afflicted aggregates by way of pre-nascence condition. (2)

Pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… dve… āsevanapaccayena paccayo… dve.

By way of post-nascence condition… two… by way of repetition condition… two.

Kammapaccayo

Kamma Condition

359. Saraṇo [T 4.0528] dhammo saraṇassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – saraṇā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā [V 4.0226] – saraṇā cetanā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. Nānākkhaṇikā – saraṇā cetanā vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (Mūlaṃ kātabbaṃ.) Saraṇā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (3)

359. The afflicted state is a condition for the afflicted state by way of kamma condition—afflicted volition is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of kamma condition. (The root should be stated.) Co-nascent, non-simultaneous. Co-nascent—afflicted volition is a condition for mind-originated materiality by way of kamma condition. Non-simultaneous—afflicted volition is a condition for resultant aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality by way of kamma condition. (The root should be stated.) Afflicted volition is a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by way of kamma condition. (3)

Araṇo dhammo araṇassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – (saṃkhittaṃ). (1)

The unafflicted state is a condition for the unafflicted state by way of kamma condition—co-nascent, non-simultaneous. Co-nascent—(abbreviated). (1)

Vipākapaccayena paccayo… ekaṃ… āhārapaccayena paccayo… cattāri… indriyapaccayena paccayo… cattāri… jhānapaccayena paccayo… cattāri… maggapaccayena paccayo… cattāri… sampayuttapaccayena paccayo… dve… vippayuttapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi (arūpadukasadisā).

By way of result condition… one… by way of nutriment condition… four… by way of faculty condition… four… by way of jhāna condition… four… by way of path condition… four… by way of association condition… two… by way of dissociation condition… three (similar to the immaterial dyad).

Atthipaccayo

Presence Condition

360. Saraṇo dhammo saraṇassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo (saṃkhittaṃ). Saraṇo dhammo araṇassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ). Saraṇo dhammo saraṇassa ca araṇassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo (saṃkhittaṃ). (3)

360. The afflicted state is a condition for the afflicted state by way of presence condition (abbreviated). The afflicted state is a condition for the unafflicted state by way of presence condition—co-nascent, post-nascent (abbreviated). The afflicted state is a condition for both the afflicted and the unafflicted states by way of presence condition (abbreviated). (3)

361. Araṇo dhammo araṇassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ). Araṇo dhammo saraṇassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ [M 4.0193] …pe… vatthuṃ assādeti abhinandati, taṃ [T 4.0529] ārabbha rāgo uppajjati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati, vatthu saraṇānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

361. The unafflicted state is a condition for the unafflicted state by way of presence condition—co-nascent, pre-nascent, post-nascent, nutriment, faculty (abbreviated). The unafflicted state is a condition for the afflicted state by way of presence condition. Pre-nascent—the eye… up to… the base is savored and rejoiced in; dependent on that, lust arises… up to… sorrow arises; the base is a condition for the afflicted aggregates by way of presence condition. (2)

Saraṇo ca araṇo ca dhammā saraṇassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ). Saraṇo ca araṇo ca dhammā araṇassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Sahajātā – saraṇā khandhā ca mahābhūtā ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – saraṇā khandhā ca kabaḷīkāro āhāro [V 4.0227] ca imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – saraṇā khandhā ca rūpajīvitindriyañca kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

The afflicted and the unafflicted states are a condition for the afflicted state by way of presence condition—co-nascent, pre-nascent (abbreviated). The afflicted and the unafflicted states are a condition for the unafflicted state by way of presence condition—co-nascent, post-nascent, nutriment, faculty. Co-nascent—the afflicted aggregates and the great elements are a condition for mind-originated materiality by way of presence condition. Post-nascent—the afflicted aggregates and physical nutriment are a condition for this body by way of presence condition. Post-nascent—the afflicted aggregates and the material life faculty are a condition for kamma-produced materiality by way of presence condition. (2)

1. Paccayānulomaṃ

1. Positive Permutation of Conditions

2. Saṅkhyāvāro

2. Enumeration Section

Suddhaṃ

Pure

362. Hetuyā cattāri, ārammaṇe cattāri, adhipatiyā pañca, anantare cattāri, samanantare cattāri, sahajāte pañca, aññamaññe dve, nissaye satta, upanissaye cattāri, purejāte dve, pacchājāte dve, āsevane dve, kamme cattāri, vipāke ekaṃ, āhāre cattāri, indriye cattāri, jhāne cattāri, magge cattāri, sampayutte dve, vippayutte tīṇi, atthiyā satta, natthiyā cattāri, vigate cattāri, avigate satta.

362. By cause, four; by object, four; by predominance, five; by contiguity, four; by immediate contiguity, four; by co-nascence, five; by mutuality, two; by support, seven; by decisive support, four; by pre-nascence, two; by post-nascence, two; by repetition, two; by kamma, four; by result, one; by nutriment, four; by faculty, four; by jhāna, four; by path, four; by association, two; by dissociation, three; by presence, seven; by absence, four; by disappearance, four; by non-disappearance, seven.

Paccanīyuddhāro

Summary of the Negative

363. Saraṇo dhammo saraṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Saraṇo dhammo araṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena [T 4.0530] paccayo… kammapaccayena paccayo. Saraṇo dhammo saraṇassa ca araṇassa ca dhammassa sahajātapaccayena paccayo. (3)

363. The afflicted state is a condition for the afflicted state by way of object condition… by way of co-nascence condition… by way of decisive support condition. The afflicted state is a condition for the unafflicted state by way of object condition… by way of co-nascence condition… by way of decisive support condition… by way of post-nascence condition… by way of kamma condition. The afflicted state is a condition for both the afflicted and the unafflicted states by way of co-nascence condition. (3)

364. Araṇo dhammo araṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena paccayo… āhārapaccayena [M 4.0194] paccayo… indriyapaccayena paccayo. Araṇo dhammo saraṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

364. The unafflicted state is a condition for the unafflicted state by way of object condition… by way of co-nascence condition… by way of decisive support condition… by way of pre-nascence condition… by way of post-nascence condition… by way of kamma condition… by way of nutriment condition… by way of faculty condition. The unafflicted state is a condition for the afflicted state by way of object condition… by way of decisive support condition… by way of pre-nascence condition. (2)

Saraṇo [V 4.0228] ca araṇo ca dhammā saraṇassa dhammassa sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Saraṇo ca araṇo ca dhammā araṇassa dhammassa sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. (2)

Defiled and undefiled states are conditions for a defiled state by way of co-nascence condition and pre-nascence condition. Defiled and undefiled states are conditions for an undefiled state by way of co-nascence condition, post-nascence condition, nutriment condition, and faculty condition. (2)

2. Paccayapaccanīyaṃ

2. The Negative Mode of Conditions

2. Saṅkhyāvāro

2. The Chapter on Enumeration

Suddhaṃ

Pure

365. Nahetuyā satta, nasamanantare satta, nasahajāte pañca, naaññamaññe pañca, nanissaye pañca, naupanissaye satta, napurejāte cha, napacchājāte satta…pe… nasampayutte pañca, navippayutte cattāri, noatthiyā cattāri, nonatthiyā satta, novigate satta, noavigate cattāri.

365. Seven are not by way of root condition, seven are not by way of immediate contiguity condition, five are not by way of co-nascence condition, five are not by way of mutuality condition, five are not by way of support condition, seven are not by way of decisive support condition, six are not by way of pre-nascence condition, seven are not by way of post-nascence condition… and so on… five are not by way of association condition, four are not by way of dissociation condition, four are not by way of presence condition, seven are not by way of absence condition, seven are not by way of disappearance condition, four are not by way of non-disappearance condition.

3. Paccayānulomapaccanīyaṃ

3. The Positive-Negative Mode of Conditions

366. Hetupaccayā naārammaṇe cattāri, naadhipatiyā cattāri…pe… nasamanantare cattāri, naaññamaññe dve, naupanissaye cattāri…pe… nasampayutte dve, navippayutte dve, nonatthiyā cattāri[T 4.0531], novigate cattāri.

366. By way of root condition, four are not by way of object condition, four are not by way of dominance condition… and so on… four are not by way of immediate contiguity condition, two are not by way of mutuality condition, four are not by way of decisive support condition… and so on… two are not by way of association condition, two are not by way of dissociation condition, four are not by way of absence condition, four are not by way of disappearance condition.

4. Paccayapaccanīyānulomaṃ

4. The Negative-Positive Mode of Conditions

367. Nahetupaccayā ārammaṇe cattāri, adhipatiyā pañca, anantare cattāri (anulomamātikā gahetabbā)…pe… avigate satta.

367. Not by way of root condition, four are by way of object condition, five are by way of dominance condition, four are by way of contiguity condition (the positive matrix should be taken)… and so on… seven are by way of non-disappearance condition.

Saraṇadukaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Defilement Dyad is concluded.

Piṭṭhidukaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Section of Final Dyads is concluded.

Dhammānulome dukapaṭṭhānaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Exposition of Dyads in the Positive Mode of Phenomena is concluded.

1-1 The Root Dyad—The Wholesome Triad

1. The Wholesome Section

1-6. Paṭiccavārādi

1-6. The Dependent Origination Section, etc.

Paccayacatukkaṃ

The Tetrad of Conditions

Hetupaccayo

Root Condition

1. Hetuṃ [T 5.0001][M 4.0195][V 4.0229] kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Hetuṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Hetuṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu kusalo ca nahetu kusalo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. (3)

1. Dependent on a wholesome root state, a wholesome root state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a wholesome root state, a wholesome non-root state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a wholesome root state, a wholesome root state and a wholesome non-root state arise by way of root condition. (3)

2. Nahetuṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nahetuṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nahetuṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu kusalo ca nahetu kusalo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. (3)

2. Dependent on a wholesome non-root state, a wholesome non-root state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a wholesome non-root state, a wholesome root state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a wholesome non-root state, a wholesome root state and a wholesome non-root state arise by way of root condition. (3)

3. Hetuṃ kusalañca nahetuṃ kusalañca dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā[V 4.0230]. Hetuṃ kusalañca nahetuṃ kusalañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu kusalo dhammo uppajjati [T 5.0002] hetupaccayā. Hetuṃ kusalañca nahetuṃ kusalañca dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu kusalo ca nahetu kusalo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. (3)

3. Dependent on a wholesome root state and a wholesome non-root state, a wholesome root state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a wholesome root state and a wholesome non-root state, a wholesome non-root state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a wholesome root state and a wholesome non-root state, a wholesome root state and a wholesome non-root state arise by way of root condition. (3)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

Object Condition

4. Hetuṃ [M 4.0196] kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu kusalo dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā (saṃkhittaṃ).

4. Dependent on a wholesome root state, a wholesome root state arises by way of object condition (abbreviated).

5. Hetuyā nava, ārammaṇe nava, adhipatiyā nava, anantare nava, samanantare nava, sahajāte nava, aññamaññe nava, nissaye nava, upanissaye nava, purejāte nava, āsevane nava, kamme nava, āhāre nava, indriye nava, jhāne nava, magge nava, sampayutte nava, vippayutte nava, atthiyā nava, natthiyā nava, vigate nava, avigate nava (anulomaṃ).

5. Hetu adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto ca nahetu adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto ca dhammā hetussa adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati… tīṇi (ārammaṇādhipatiyeva)…pe….

A rooted state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling and an unrooted state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling are conditions for a rooted state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling by way of dominance condition: object dominance... three (only object dominance)...and so on.

Upanissayapaccayādi

Strong Dependence Condition, etc.

102. Hetu adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto dhammo hetussa adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo… nava, āsevanapaccayena paccayo… nava.

102. A rooted state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is a condition for a rooted state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling by way of strong dependence condition: object strong dependence, contiguity strong dependence, natural strong dependence... nine; by way of repetition condition... nine.

103. Nahetu adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto dhammo nahetussa adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi.

103. An unrooted state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is a condition for an unrooted state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling by way of kamma condition... three.

104. Hetu adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto dhammo hetussa adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttassa dhammassa vipākapaccayena paccayo… nava…pe… avigatapaccayena paccayo… nava.

104. A rooted state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is a condition for a rooted state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling by way of result condition... nine...and so on... by way of non-cessation condition... nine.

105. Hetuyā tīṇi, ārammaṇe nava, adhipatiyā nava, anantare nava, samanantare nava, sahajāte nava, aññamaññe nava, nissaye nava, upanissaye nava, āsevane nava, kamme tīṇi, vipāke nava, āhāre [T 5.0026] tīṇi, indriye nava, jhāne tīṇi, magge nava, sampayutte nava, atthiyā nava, natthiyā nava, vigate nava, avigate nava (anulomaṃ).

105. By root condition, three; by object condition, nine; by dominance condition, nine; by contiguity condition, nine; by immediate contiguity condition, nine; by co-nascence condition, nine; by reciprocity condition, nine; by dependence condition, nine; by strong dependence condition, nine; by repetition condition, nine; by kamma condition, three; by result condition, nine; by nutriment condition, three; by faculty condition, nine; by jhāna condition, three; by path condition, nine; by association condition, nine; by presence condition, nine; by absence condition, nine; by cessation condition, nine; by non-cessation condition, nine (in the direct order).

Paccanīyuddhāro

Summary of Opposing Factors

106. Hetu [M 4.0217][V 4.0254] adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto dhammo hetussa adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo (saṃkhittaṃ).

106. A rooted state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is a condition for a rooted state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling by way of object condition... by way of co-nascence condition... by way of strong dependence condition (abbreviated).

107. Nahetuyā nava, naārammaṇe nava (saṃkhittaṃ, paccanīyaṃ).

107. By non-root condition, nine; by non-object condition, nine (abbreviated, in the reverse order).

Hetupaccayā naārammaṇe tīṇi (saṃkhittaṃ, anulomapaccanīyaṃ).

By way of root condition, by way of non-object condition, three (abbreviated, forward-reverse order).

Nahetupaccayā ārammaṇe nava (saṃkhittaṃ, paccanīyānulomaṃ).

By way of non-root condition, by way of object condition, nine (abbreviated, reverse-forward order).

(Yathā kusalattike pañhāvārassa anulomampi paccanīyampi anulomapaccanīyampi paccanīyānulomampi gaṇitaṃ, evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ.)

(Just as the reckoning was done for the forward order, the reverse order, the forward-reverse order, and the reverse-forward order in the question section of the wholesome triad, so should it be reckoned.)

Hetudukavedanāttikaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Dyad of Roots and the Triad of Feelings is concluded.

Nahetuṃ vipākaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu vipāko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… tīṇi.

(Anulomaṃ).

By way of root condition, nine; by way of object condition, nine; by way of predominance condition, nine; by way of contiguity condition, nine; by way of immediate contiguity condition, nine; by way of co-nascence condition, nine; by way of mutuality condition, nine; by way of support condition, nine; by way of decisive support condition, nine; by way of pre-nascence condition, nine; by way of kamma condition, nine; by way of result condition, nine; by way of nutriment condition, nine; by way of faculty condition, nine; by way of jhāna condition, nine; by way of path condition, nine; by way of association condition, nine; by way of dissociation condition, nine; by way of presence condition, nine; by way of absence condition, nine; by way of disappearance condition, nine; by way of non-disappearance condition, nine (in the forward order).

Nahetu-naadhipatipaccayā

110. Nahetuṃ vipākaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu vipāko dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā. (1)

Nahetupaccayā ārammaṇe ekaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ, paccanīyānulomaṃ).

Hetu vipāko dhammo hetussa vipākassa ca nahetussa vipākassa ca dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo. (3)

A rooted resultant state is a condition for an unrooted resultant state by way of the decisive support condition: immediate decisive support, natural decisive support. A rooted resultant state is a condition for both rooted resultant and unrooted resultant states by way of the decisive support condition: immediate decisive support, natural decisive support. (3)

Nahetu vipāko dhammo nahetussa vipākassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo[V 4.0257], pakatūpanissayo…pe… (itare dve anantarūpanissayo pakatūpanissayoyeva).

A non-root resultant phenomenon is a condition for a non-root resultant phenomenon by way of the strong dependence condition: immediate strong dependence, natural strong dependence… and so on (the other two are only immediate strong dependence and natural strong dependence).

117. Nahetu [T 5.0029] vipāko dhammo nahetussa vipākassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi (sahajātakammameva, saṃkhittaṃ).

3. Nevadassanenanabhāvanāyapahātabbahetukapadaṃ

3. The section on roots to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development.

1-6. Paṭiccavārādi

1–6. The Section on Dependent Origination, and so on

Paccayacatukkaṃ

The Fourfold Section on Conditions

Hetupaccayo

The Root Condition

298. Hetuṃ nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca [T 5.0076] hetu nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā (saṃkhittaṃ).

298. A state with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development arises in dependence on a state with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development, by way of root condition (in brief).

299. Hetuyā nava, ārammaṇe nava…pe… avigate nava (saṃkhittaṃ).

299. By way of root condition, nine; by way of object condition, nine... by way of non-disappearance condition, nine (in brief).

Nahetupaccayo

The Non-Root Condition

300. Nahetuṃ nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā (saṃkhittaṃ).

300. A non-root state with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development arises in dependence on a non-root state with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development, by way of non-root condition (in brief).

301. Nahetuyā ekaṃ, naārammaṇe tīṇi, naadhipatiyā nava, naanantare tīṇi, nasamanantare [V 4.0309] tīṇi, naaññamaññe tīṇi, naupanissaye tīṇi, napurejāte nava, napacchājāte nava, naāsevane nava, nakamme tīṇi, navipāke nava, naāhāre ekaṃ, naindriye ekaṃ, najhāne ekaṃ, namagge ekaṃ, nasampayutte tīṇi, navippayutte nava, nonatthiyā tīṇi, novigate tīṇi (saṃkhittaṃ).

301. By way of non-root condition, one; by way of non-object condition, three; by way of non-dominance condition, nine; by way of non-contiguity condition, three; by way of non-immediate contiguity condition, three; by way of non-mutuality condition, three; by way of non-decisive support condition, three; by way of non-pre-nascence condition, nine; by way of non-post-nascence condition, nine; by way of non-repetition condition, nine; by way of non-kamma condition, three; by way of non-result condition, nine; by way of non-nutriment condition, one; by way of non-faculty condition, one; by way of non-jhāna condition, one; by way of non-path condition, one; by way of non-association condition, three; by way of non-dissociation condition, nine; by way of non-absence condition, three; by way of non-disappearance condition, three (in brief).

Hetupaccayā naārammaṇe tīṇi (saṃkhittaṃ).

By way of root condition, not by way of object condition, three (in brief).

Nahetupaccayā ārammaṇe ekaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ).

Not by way of root condition, by way of object condition, one (in brief).

(Sahajātavāropi paccayavāropi nissayavāropi saṃsaṭṭhavāropi sampayuttavāropi paṭiccavārasadisā vitthāretabbā.)

The section on co-nascence, the section on conditions, the section on support, the section on commingling, and the section on association should be elaborated in the same way as the section on dependent origination.

7. Pañhāvāro

7. Question Section

Paccayacatukkaṃ

The Fourfold Section on Conditions

Hetupaccayo

Root Condition

302. Hetu [M 4.0262] nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo hetussa nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo… tīṇi (saṃkhittaṃ).

302. A root state with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation is a condition for a state with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation, by way of root condition… three (in brief).

303. Hetuyā [T 5.0077] tīṇi, ārammaṇe nava, adhipatiyā nava, anantare nava, samanantare nava, sahajāte nava, aññamaññe nava, nissaye nava, upanissaye nava, purejāte tīṇi, pacchājāte tīṇi, āsevane nava, kamme tīṇi, vipāke nava, āhāre tīṇi, indriye nava, jhāne tīṇi, magge nava, sampayutte nava, vippayutte pañca, atthiyā nava, natthiyā nava, vigate nava, avigate nava (saṃkhittaṃ).

303. By root condition, three; by object condition, nine; by dominance condition, nine; by contiguity condition, nine; by immediate contiguity condition, nine; by co-nascence condition, nine; by mutuality condition, nine; by support condition, nine; by decisive support condition, nine; by prenascence condition, three; by postnascence condition, three; by repetition condition, nine; by kamma condition, three; by result condition, nine; by nutriment condition, three; by faculty condition, nine; by jhāna condition, three; by path condition, nine; by association condition, nine; by dissociation condition, five; by presence condition, nine; by absence condition, nine; by disappearance condition, nine; by non-disappearance condition, nine (in brief).

Paccanīyuddhāro

Reverse Summary

304. Hetu nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo hetussa nevadassanena nabhāvanāya [V 4.0310] pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo (saṃkhittaṃ).

304. A root state with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation is a condition for a state with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation, by way of object condition… by way of co-nascence condition… by way of decisive support condition (in brief).

305. Nahetuyā nava, naārammaṇe nava (saṃkhittaṃ).

305. By non-root condition, nine; by non-object condition, nine (in brief).

Hetupaccayā naārammaṇe tīṇi (saṃkhittaṃ).

By root condition, in non-object condition, three (in brief).

Nahetupaccayā ārammaṇe nava (saṃkhittaṃ).

By non-root condition, in object condition, nine (in brief).

(Yathā kusalattike pañhāvārassa anulomampi paccanīyampi anulomapaccanīyampi paccanīyānulomampi naṇitaṃ, evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ.)

Just as in the question section of the wholesome triplet, the direct method, the reverse method, the direct-reverse method, and the reverse-direct method are set forth, so they are to be reckoned here.

Hetudukadassanenapahātabbahetukattikaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Root Dyad and the Triad of Roots to be Abandoned by Seeing is concluded.

324. Nahetuṃ [V 4.0316] nevācayagāmināpacayagāmiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā. (1)

Hetuṃ nevācayagāmināpacayagāmiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo uppajjati naārammaṇapaccayā. (1)

522. Hetuyā tīṇi, ārammaṇe nava, adhipatiyā nava…pe… purejāte tīṇi, āsevane nava, kamme tīṇi, vipāke nava…pe… avigate nava (saṃkhittaṃ).

The Fetter-Group Wholesome Triplet is concluded.

55-1. Sārammaṇaduka-kusalattikaṃ

1-7. Paṭiccavārādi

The Conditional Section, etc.

Paccayacatukkaṃ

The Conditional Tetrad

Hetupaccayo

The Root Condition

1. Sārammaṇaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sārammaṇo kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā (yathā sappaccayaṃ kusalaṃ, evaṃ vitthāretabbaṃ.)

1. Dependent on a wholesome phenomenon with an object, a wholesome phenomenon with an object arises by way of root condition. (This should be elaborated in detail in the same way as the wholesome with-a-condition.)

2. Sārammaṇaṃ [V 4.0486] akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sārammaṇo akusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā (yathā sappaccayaṃ akusalaṃ, evaṃ kātabbaṃ.)

2. Dependent on an unwholesome phenomenon with an object, an unwholesome phenomenon with an object arises by way of root condition. (This is to be done in the same way as the unwholesome with-a-condition.)

3. Sārammaṇaṃ [T 5.0239] abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sārammaṇo abyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… tīṇi.

3. Dependent on an indeterminate phenomenon with an object, an indeterminate phenomenon with an object arises by way of root condition… three.

Anārammaṇaṃ abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anārammaṇo abyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… tīṇi.

Dependent on an indeterminate phenomenon without an object, an indeterminate phenomenon without an object arises by way of root condition… three.

Sārammaṇaṃ abyākatañca anārammaṇaṃ abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca sārammaṇo abyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… tīṇi (saṃkhittaṃ).

Dependent on an indeterminate phenomenon with an object and on an indeterminate phenomenon without an object, an indeterminate phenomenon with an object arises by way of root condition… three. (In brief).

4. Hetuyā nava, ārammaṇe tīṇi, adhipatiyā pañca…pe… aññamaññe cha…pe… purejāte ekaṃ, āsevane ekaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ).

4. In root condition, nine; in object condition, three; in dominance condition, five; …pe… in mutuality condition, six; …pe… in prenascence condition, one; in repetition condition, one. (In brief).

Nahetuyā nava, naārammaṇe tīṇi, naadhipatiyā nava…pe… nakamme dve, navipāke pañca, naāhāre ekaṃ, naindriye ekaṃ, najhāne dve, namagge [M 4.0396] nava, nasampayutte tīṇi, navippayutte dve, nonatthiyā tīṇi, novigate tīṇi (saṃkhittaṃ).

Not by way of root: nine. Not by way of object: three. Not by way of dominance: nine. …pe… Not by way of kamma: two. Not by way of resultant: five. Not by way of nutriment: one. Not by way of faculty: one. Not by way of jhāna: two. Not by way of path: nine. Not by way of association: three. Not by way of dissociation: two. Not by way of absence: three. Not by way of disappearance: three. (In brief).

In root condition, three; in object condition, two; in dominance condition, four; in contiguity condition, one... in conascence condition, seven; in mutuality condition, six; in dependence condition, seven; in decisive support condition, two; in prenascence condition, one; in postnascence condition, one; in repetition condition, one; in kamma condition, three; in result condition, three; in association condition, one; in dissociation condition, two (in brief).

89. Hetuyā nava, ārammaṇe pañca, adhipatiyā pañca…pe… aññamaññe pañca, nissaye nava, upanissaye pañca, purejāte pañca, āsevane pañca, kamme…pe… magge nava, sampayutte pañca, vippayutte nava…pe… avigate nava (saṃkhittaṃ).

89. In root condition, nine; in object condition, five; in dominance condition, five… in mutuality condition, five; in dependence condition, nine; in decisive support condition, five; in prenascence condition, five; in repetition condition, five; in kamma condition… in path condition, nine; in association condition, five; in dissociation condition, nine… in non-disappearance condition, nine. (Abbreviated.)

Nahetuyā nava, naārammaṇe nava, naadhipatiyā nava…pe… nakamme tīṇi, navipāke pañca, naāhāre ekaṃ, naindriye ekaṃ, najhāne pañca, namagge nava, nasampayutte nava, navippayutte pañca, nonatthiyā nava, novigate nava (saṃkhittaṃ. Sahajātavārampi…pe… sampayuttavārampi vitthāretabbaṃ.)

In non-root condition, nine; in non-object condition, nine; in non-dominance condition, nine… in non-kamma condition, three; in non-resultant condition, five; in non-nutriment condition, one; in non-faculty condition, one; in non-jhāna condition, five; in non-path condition, nine; in non-association condition, nine; in non-dissociation condition, five; in non-presence condition, nine; in non-disappearance condition, nine. (Abbreviated. The co-nascence section, etc., and the association section should be elaborated.)

90. Bāhiro [M 4.0413] abyākato dhammo bāhirassa abyākatassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo (saṃkhittaṃ).

90. An external indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for an external indeterminate phenomenon by root condition. (Abbreviated.)

Bāhiro [V 4.0508] abyākato dhammo bāhirassa abyākatassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi.

An external indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for an external indeterminate phenomenon by kamma condition… three.

91. Hetuyā tīṇi, ārammaṇe nava, adhipatiyā nava (ajjhattiko bāhirassa gamanakāle sahajātādhipati, majjhe tīsupi sahajātādhipati)[T 5.0266], anantare nava, sahajāte nava, aññamaññe pañca, nissaye nava, upanissaye nava, purejāte nava (ārammaṇapurejātampi vatthupurejātampi), pacchājāte nava, āsevane nava, kamme tīṇi, vipāke nava, āhāre nava (tiṇṇannaṃ kabaḷīkāro āhāro), indriye nava (tiṇṇannaṃ rūpajīvitindriyaṃ), jhāne magge tīṇi, sampayutte pañca, vippayutte nava, atthiyā nava…pe… avigate nava (saṃkhittaṃ).

91. In root condition, three; in object condition, nine; in dominance condition, nine (the internal is a condition for the external at the time of movement by co-nascent dominance; in the middle case, for all three it is co-nascent dominance); in contiguity condition, nine; in co-nascence condition, nine; in mutuality condition, five; in dependence condition, nine; in decisive support condition, nine; in prenascence condition, nine (both object-prenascence and base-prenascence); in postnascence condition, nine; in repetition condition, nine; in kamma condition, three; in resultant condition, nine; in nutriment condition, nine (for the three, physical nutriment); in faculty condition, nine (for the three, the material life faculty); in jhāna and path conditions, three; in association condition, five; in dissociation condition, nine; in presence condition, nine… in non-disappearance condition, nine. (Abbreviated.)

The Conditional Tetrad

Hetupaccayo

Root Condition

92. Noupādā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca noupādā kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā (saṃkhittaṃ).

92. Dependent on a wholesome state that is not clinging, a wholesome state that is not clinging arises by root condition. (In brief).

Hetuyā ekaṃ, ārammaṇe ekaṃ…pe… avigate ekaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ).

By root condition, one; by object condition, one… and so on… by non-disappearance condition, one. (In brief).

(Sahajātavārepi…pe… pañhāvārepi sabbattha ekaṃ.)

(Also in the Conascence Section… and so on… also in the Question Section, it is one everywhere.)

93. Noupādā akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca noupādā akusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā (saṃkhittaṃ).

93. Dependent on an unwholesome state that is not clinging, an unwholesome state that is not clinging arises by root condition. (In brief).

Hetuyā ekaṃ, ārammaṇe ekaṃ…pe… avigate ekaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ).

By root condition, one; by object condition, one… and so on… by non-disappearance condition, one. (In brief).

(Sahajātavārepi [T 5.0267] …pe… pañhāvārepi sabbattha ekaṃ.)

(Also in the Conascence Section… and so on… also in the Question Section, it is one everywhere.)

94. Upādā abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca noupādā abyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. (1)

94. Dependent on an indeterminate state that is clinging, an indeterminate state that is not clinging arises by root condition. (1)

Noupādā [V 4.0509] abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca noupādā abyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Noupādā abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca upādā abyākato [M 4.0414] dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Noupādā abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca upādā abyākato ca noupādā abyākato ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. (3)

Dependent on an indeterminate state that is not clinging, an indeterminate state that is not clinging arises by root condition. Dependent on an indeterminate state that is not clinging, an indeterminate state that is clinging arises by root condition. Dependent on an indeterminate state that is not clinging, an indeterminate state that is clinging and an indeterminate state that is not clinging arise by root condition. (3)

Upādā abyākatañca noupādā abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca noupādā abyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. (1) (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

Dependent on an indeterminate state that is clinging and an indeterminate state that is not clinging, an indeterminate state that is not clinging arises by root condition. (1) (In brief.)

95. Hetuyā pañca, ārammaṇe tīṇi…pe… aññamaññe pañca…pe… purejāte ekaṃ, āsevane ekaṃ, kamme pañca, vipāke pañca…pe… avigate pañca (saṃkhittaṃ).

95. By root condition, five; by object condition, three… and so on… by mutuality condition, five… and so on… by prenascence condition, one; by repetition condition, one; by kamma condition, five; by result condition, five… and so on… by non-disappearance condition, five. (In brief).

Nahetuyā pañca, naārammaṇe tīṇi, naadhipatiyā pañca…pe… napurejāte pañca…pe… nakamme tīṇi, navipāke tīṇi, naāhāre tīṇi, naindriye tīṇi, najhāne tīṇi, namagge pañca, nasampayutte tīṇi, navippayutte tīṇi, nonatthiyā tīṇi, novigate tīṇi (saṃkhittaṃ. Sahajātavārampi…pe… sampayuttavārampi vitthāretabbaṃ.)

By non-root condition, five; by non-object condition, three; by non-dominance condition, five… and so on… by non-prenascence condition, five… and so on… by non-kamma condition, three; by non-result condition, three; by non-nutriment condition, three; by non-faculty condition, three; by non-jhāna condition, three; by non-path condition, five; by non-association condition, three; by non-dissociation condition, three; by non-absence condition, three; by non-disappearance condition, three. (In brief. The Conascence Section… and so on… and the Association Section should be elaborated.)

Root Condition, Object Condition, etc.

96. Noupādā [T 5.0268] abyākato dhammo noupādā abyākatassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo… tīṇi.

96. An indeterminate state that is not clinging is a condition for an indeterminate state that is not clinging by root condition… three.

Upādā abyākato dhammo noupādā abyākatassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

An indeterminate state that is clinging is a condition for an indeterminate state that is not clinging by object condition. (1)

Noupādā abyākato dhammo noupādā abyākatassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

An indeterminate state that is not clinging is a condition for an indeterminate state that is not clinging by object condition. (1)

Noupādā abyākato dhammo noupādā abyākatassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo… tīṇi (paṭhame dvepi adhipatī, dvīsu sahajātādhipati).

An indeterminate state that is not clinging is a condition for an indeterminate state that is not clinging by dominance condition… three (in the first, both are dominance; in the two, conascence-dominance).

Upādā [V 4.0510] abyākato dhammo noupādā abyākatassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

An indeterminate state that is clinging is a condition for an indeterminate state that is not clinging by decisive support condition. (1)

Noupādā abyākato dhammo noupādā abyākatassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1) (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

An indeterminate state that is not clinging is a condition for an indeterminate state that is not clinging by decisive support condition. (1) (In brief.)

97. Upanissaye [M 4.0415] dve, purejāte tīṇi, pacchājāte tīṇi, āsevane ekaṃ, kamme tīṇi, vipāke tīṇi, āhāre cha, indriye satta, jhāne tīṇi, magge tīṇi, sampayutte ekaṃ, vippayutte cattāri, atthiyā nava…pe… avigate nava (saṃkhittaṃ).

97. By decisive support condition, two; by prenascence condition, three; by postnascence condition, three; by repetition condition, one; by kamma condition, three; by result condition, three; by nutriment condition, six; by faculty condition, seven; by jhāna condition, three; by path condition, three; by association condition, one; by dissociation condition, four; by presence condition, nine… and so on… by non-disappearance condition, nine. (In brief).

1-7. Paṭiccavārādi

The Tetrad of Conditions

Hetupaccayo

Root Condition

98. Anupādinnaṃ [T 5.0269] kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anupādinno kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā (saṃkhittaṃ).

By root condition, one; by object condition, one… and so on… by non-disappearance condition, one. (One in all cases. In brief. Also in the Conascence Section… and so on… also in the Question Section, one, similar to the wholesome with condition.)

99. Anupādinnaṃ akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anupādinno akusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā (saṃkhittaṃ).

99. Dependent on an unwholesome state that is not clung-to, an unwholesome state that is not clung-to arises by root condition. (In brief).

Hetuyā ekaṃ…pe… avigate ekaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ. Sahajātavārepi…pe… pañhāvārepi sabbattha ekaṃ).

By root condition, one… and so on… by non-disappearance condition, one. (In brief. Also in the Conascence Section… and so on… also in the Question Section, it is one everywhere.)

100. Upādinnaṃ [V 4.0511] abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca upādinno abyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… tīṇi.

100. Dependent on an indeterminate state that is clung-to, an indeterminate state that is clung-to arises by root condition… three.

Anupādinnaṃ abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anupādinno abyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā[T 5.0270]. (1)

Dependent on an indeterminate state that is not clung-to, an indeterminate state that is not clung-to arises by root condition. (1)

Upādinnaṃ abyākatañca anupādinnaṃ abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca anupādinno abyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – upādinne khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (1) (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

Dependent on an indeterminate state that is clung-to and an indeterminate state that is not clung-to, an indeterminate state that is not clung-to arises by root condition—that is, dependent on the clung-to aggregates and the great elements, mind-originated matter arises. (1) (In brief.)

101. Hetuyā pañca, ārammaṇe dve, adhipatiyā ekaṃ…pe… purejāte dve, āsevane ekaṃ, kamme pañca, vipāke pañca…pe… avigate pañca (saṃkhittaṃ).

101. By root condition, five; by object condition, two; by dominance condition, one... etc. ... by prenascence condition, two; by repetition condition, one; by kamma condition, five; by result condition, five... etc. ... by non-disappearance condition, five. (In brief).

Nahetuyā [M 4.0416] pañca, naārammaṇe cattāri, naadhipatiyā pañca…pe… napurejāte cattāri, napacchājāte naāsevane pañca, nakamme ekaṃ, navipāke dve, naāhāre dve, naindriye dve, najhāne dve, namagge pañca, nasampayutte cattāri, navippayutte dve, nonatthiyā cattāri, novigate cattāri (saṃkhittaṃ. By non-root condition, five; by non-object condition, four; by non-dominance condition, five... etc. ... by non-prenascence condition, four; by non-postnascence condition, by non-repetition condition, five; by non-kamma condition, one; by non-result condition, two; by non-nutriment condition, two; by non-faculty condition, two; by non-jhāna condition, two; by non-path condition, five; by non-association condition, four; by non-dissociation condition, two; by non-absence condition, four; by non-disappearance condition, four. (In brief. The Conascence Section, etc., should be elaborated.)

Hetu-purejātapaccayā

By way of Root and Prenascence Conditions

102. Upādinno abyākato dhammo upādinnassa abyākatassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo… tīṇi.

102. An affected indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for an affected indeterminate phenomenon by root condition... three.

Anupādinno abyākato dhammo anupādinnassa abyākatassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo. (1)

An unaffected indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for an unaffected indeterminate phenomenon by root condition. (1)

Anupādinno abyākato dhammo anupādinnassa abyākatassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati… ekaṃ.

An unaffected indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for an unaffected indeterminate phenomenon by dominance condition: object-dominance, conascence-dominance... one.

Upādinno [V 4.0512] abyākato dhammo upādinnassa abyākatassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ (dve pañhā).

An affected indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for an affected indeterminate phenomenon by prenascence condition: object-prenascence, base-prenascence (two questions).

Anupādinno abyākato dhammo anupādinnassa abyākatassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo… dve (ārammaṇapurejātaṃyeva, ghaṭanā dve, ārammaṇapurejātampi vatthupurejātampi).

An unaffected indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for an unaffected indeterminate phenomenon by prenascence condition... two (only object-prenascence; two applications: both object-prenascence and base-prenascence).

103. Hetuyā cattāri, ārammaṇe cattāri (upādinnamūlake dve, anupādinnamūlake dve), adhipatiyā ekaṃ, anantare [T 5.0271] samanantare cattāri, sahajāte pañca, aññamaññe dve, nissaye pañca, upanissaye cattāri, purejāte cha, pacchājāte cha, āsevane ekaṃ, kamme cattāri, vipāke cattāri, āhāre nava, indriye cattāri, jhāne cattāri, magge cattāri, sampayutte dve, vippayutte cha, atthiyā nava, natthiyā cattāri, vigate cattāri, avigate nava (saṃkhittaṃ).

103. By root condition, four; by object condition, four (two rooted in the affected, two rooted in the unaffected); by dominance condition, one; by contiguity condition and proximity condition, four; by conascence condition, five; by mutuality condition, two; by support condition, five; by decisive support condition, four; by prenascence condition, six; by postnascence condition, six; by repetition condition, one; by kamma condition, four; by result condition, four; by nutriment condition, nine; by faculty condition, four; by jhāna condition, four; by path condition, four; by association condition, two; by dissociation condition, six; by presence condition, nine; by absence condition, four; by disappearance condition, four; by non-disappearance condition, nine (in brief).

Nahetuyā nava, naārammaṇe nava (saṃkhittaṃ).

By non-root condition, nine; by non-object condition, nine (in brief).

Hetupaccayā naārammaṇe cattāri (saṃkhittaṃ).

By root condition, not by object condition: four (in brief).

Nahetupaccayā ārammaṇe cattāri (saṃkhittaṃ).

Not by root condition, by object condition: four (in brief).

Mahantaradukakusalattikaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Great Intermediate Dyad and Wholesome Triad is concluded.

Paccayacatukkaṃ

The Tetrad of Conditions

1. Noupādānaṃ [T 5.0272][M 4.0417] kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca noupādāno kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā (saṃkhittaṃ).

1. Dependent on a non-clinging wholesome phenomenon, a non-clinging wholesome phenomenon arises by root condition (in brief).

Hetuyā [V 4.0513] ekaṃ, ārammaṇe ekaṃ…pe… avigate ekaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ).

By root condition, one; by object condition, one... and so on... by non-disappearance condition, one (in brief).

(Sahajātavārepi…pe… pañhāvārepi sabbattha ekaṃ.)

(Also in the conascence section... and so on... also in the question section, everywhere one.)

2. Upādānaṃ akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca upādāno akusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Upādānaṃ akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca noupādāno akusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Upādānaṃ akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca upādāno akusalo ca noupādāno akusalo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. (3)

2. Dependent on a clinging unwholesome phenomenon, a clinging unwholesome phenomenon arises by root condition. Dependent on a clinging unwholesome phenomenon, a non-clinging unwholesome phenomenon arises by root condition. Dependent on a clinging unwholesome phenomenon, both a clinging unwholesome phenomenon and a non-clinging unwholesome phenomenon arise by root condition. (3)

Noupādānaṃ akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca noupādāno akusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… tīṇi.

Dependent on a non-clinging unwholesome phenomenon, a non-clinging unwholesome phenomenon arises by root condition... three.

Upādānaṃ akusalañca noupādānaṃ akusalañca dhammaṃ paṭicca upādāno akusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… tīṇi (saṃkhittaṃ).

Dependent on a clinging unwholesome phenomenon and a non-clinging unwholesome phenomenon, a clinging unwholesome phenomenon arises by root condition... three (in brief).

3. Hetuyā nava, ārammaṇe nava (sabbattha nava), avigate nava (saṃkhittaṃ).

3. By root condition, nine; by object condition, nine (nine in all cases); by non-disappearance condition, nine (in brief).

4. Noupādānaṃ akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca noupādāno akusalo dhammo [T 5.0273] uppajjati nahetupaccayā (saṃkhittaṃ).

4. Dependent on a non-clinging unwholesome phenomenon, a non-clinging unwholesome phenomenon arises not by root condition (in brief).

5. Nahetuyā ekaṃ, naadhipatiyā nava, napurejāte nava…pe… nakamme tīṇi, navipāke nava, navippayutte nava (saṃkhittaṃ. Sahajātavārādi vitthāretabbo).

5. By non-root condition, one; by non-dominance condition, nine; by non-prenascence condition, nine... and so on... by non-kamma condition, three; by non-result condition, nine; by non-dissociation condition, nine (in brief. The section beginning with conascence should be elaborated).

6. Upādāno akusalo dhammo upādānassa akusalassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo (saṃkhittaṃ).

6. A clinging unwholesome phenomenon is a condition for a clinging unwholesome phenomenon by root condition (in brief).

7. Hetuyā nava, ārammaṇe nava, adhipatiyā nava (noupādānamūlake tīṇi, sahajātādhipati), anantare nava…pe… nissaye nava, upanissaye [M 4.0418] nava, āsevane nava, kamme [V 4.0514] tīṇi (noupādānamūlake), āhāre tīṇi, indriye tīṇi, jhāne tīṇi, magge nava, sampayutte nava, atthiyā nava…pe… avigate nava (saṃkhittaṃ).

7. By root condition, nine; by object condition, nine; by dominance condition, nine (three rooted in non-clinging, conascence-dominance); by contiguity condition, nine... and so on... by support condition, nine; by decisive support condition, nine; by repetition condition, nine; by kamma condition, three (rooted in non-clinging); by nutriment condition, three; by faculty condition, three; by jhāna condition, three; by path condition, nine; by association condition, nine; by presence condition, nine... and so on... by non-disappearance condition, nine (in brief).

8. Noupādānaṃ abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca noupādāno abyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā (saṃkhittaṃ).

8. Dependent on a non-clinging indeterminate phenomenon, a non-clinging indeterminate phenomenon arises by root condition (in brief).

9. Hetuyā ekaṃ, ārammaṇe ekaṃ…pe… avigate ekaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ).

9. By root condition, one; by object condition, one... and so on... by non-disappearance condition, one (in brief).

(Sahajātavārepi…pe… pañhāvārepi sabbattha ekaṃ.)

(Also in the conascence section... and so on... also in the question section, everywhere one.)

1-7. Paṭiccavārādi

Paccayacatukkaṃ

The Tetrad of Conditions

Hetupaccayo

Root Condition

10. Upādāniyaṃ [T 5.0274] kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca upādāniyo kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. (1)

10. Dependent on a wholesome phenomenon that is subject to clinging, a wholesome phenomenon that is subject to clinging arises by way of root condition. (1)

Anupādāniyaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anupādāniyo kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. (1) (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

Dependent on a wholesome phenomenon that is not subject to clinging, a wholesome phenomenon that is not subject to clinging arises by way of root condition. (1) (In brief.)

11. Hetuyā dve, ārammaṇe dve…pe… avigate dve (saṃkhittaṃ. Lokiyalokuttaradukakusalasadisaṃ. Sahajātavārampi…pe… pañhāvārampi vitthāretabbaṃ.)

11. In root condition, two; in object condition, two... and so on... in non-disappearance condition, two (in brief. Similar to the Mundane and Supramundane Dyad and the Wholesome Triad. The conascence section... and so on... and the question section should also be elaborated).

(Sahajātavārepi…pe… pañhāvārepi sabbattha ekaṃ.)

(Also in the conascence section... and so on... also in the question section, everywhere one.)

13. Upādāniyaṃ [V 4.0515] abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca upādāniyo abyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. (1)

13. Dependent on an indeterminate phenomenon that is subject to clinging, an indeterminate phenomenon that is subject to clinging arises by way of root condition. (1)

Anupādāniyaṃ abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anupādāniyo abyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā[T 5.0275]. Anupādāniyaṃ abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca upādāniyo abyākato [M 4.0419] dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Anupādāniyaṃ abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca upādāniyo abyākato ca anupādāniyo abyākato ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. (3)

Dependent on an indeterminate phenomenon that is not subject to clinging, an indeterminate phenomenon that is not subject to clinging arises by way of root condition. Dependent on an indeterminate phenomenon that is not subject to clinging, an indeterminate phenomenon that is subject to clinging arises by way of root condition. Dependent on an indeterminate phenomenon that is not subject to clinging, both an indeterminate phenomenon that is subject to clinging and an indeterminate phenomenon that is not subject to clinging arise by way of root condition. (3)

Upādāniyaṃ abyākatañca anupādāniyaṃ abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca upādāniyo abyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. (1) (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

Dependent on an indeterminate phenomenon that is subject to clinging and an indeterminate phenomenon that is not subject to clinging, an indeterminate phenomenon that is subject to clinging arises by way of root condition. (1) (In brief.)

1. Nadassanena pahātabbaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nadassanena pahātabbo kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā (saṃkhittaṃ).

1. Dependent on a wholesome state not to be abandoned by vision, a wholesome state not to be abandoned by vision arises by way of root condition (in brief).

Hetuyā ekaṃ, ārammaṇe ekaṃ, adhipatiyā ekaṃ…pe… avigate ekaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ. Sahajātavārepi…pe… pañhāvārepi sabbattha ekaṃ).

By way of root condition, one; by way of object condition, one; by way of dominance condition, one... by way of non-disappearance condition, one (in brief). In the conascence section too... and in the question section too, there is one in every case.

3. Dassanena pahātabbaṃ akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca dassanena pahātabbo akusalo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – vicikicchāsahagate khandhe paṭicca vicikicchāsahagato moho. (1)

3. Dependent on an unwholesome state to be abandoned by vision, an unwholesome state to be abandoned by vision arises by way of non-root condition—dependent on the aggregates accompanied by doubt, delusion accompanied by doubt arises. (1)

Nadassanena pahātabbaṃ akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nadassanena pahātabbo akusalo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā. (1) (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

Dependent on an unwholesome state not to be abandoned by vision, an unwholesome state not to be abandoned by vision arises by way of non-root condition. (1) (In brief.)

4. Nahetuyā dve, naadhipatiyā dve, napurejāte dve…pe… nakamme dve, navipāke dve, navippayutte dve (saṃkhittaṃ. Sahajātavārepi…pe… sampayuttavārepi sabbattha vitthāretabbaṃ).

4. By way of non-root condition, two; by way of non-dominance condition, two; by way of non-prenascence condition, two... by way of non-kamma condition, two; by way of non-resultant condition, two; by way of non-dissociation condition, two (in brief). In the conascence section too... and in the association section too, it should be elaborated everywhere.

5. Dassanena [M 4.0430] pahātabbo akusalo dhammo dassanena pahātabbassa akusalassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo. (1)

5. An unwholesome state to be abandoned by vision is a condition for an unwholesome state to be abandoned by vision by way of root condition. (1)

Nadassanena pahātabbo akusalo dhammo nadassanena pahātabbassa akusalassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo. (1) (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

An unwholesome state not to be abandoned by vision is a condition for an unwholesome state not to be abandoned by vision by way of root condition. (1) (In brief.)

6. Hetuyā dve, ārammaṇe tīṇi (dassane ekaṃ, nadassane dve), adhipatiyā tīṇi (dassanena pahātabbamūlakaṃ ekaṃ, nadassane dve[T 5.0292], ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati, ekārammaṇādhipati), anantare dve (dassanamūlakaṃ ekaṃ, nadassane ekaṃ), samanantare dve, sahajāte dve…pe… upanissaye tīṇi, āsevane dve, kamme dve, āhāre dve…pe… sampayutte dve, atthiyā dve, natthiyā dve…pe… avigate dve (saṃkhittaṃ).

6. By way of root condition, two; by way of object condition, three (one for vision, two for non-vision); by way of dominance condition, three (one rooted in what is to be abandoned by vision, two not so rooted; object-dominance, conascence-dominance, single-object-dominance); by way of proximity condition, two (one rooted in vision, one not so rooted); by way of contiguity condition, two; by way of conascence condition, two… by way of decisive support condition, three; by way of repetition condition, two; by way of kamma condition, two; by way of nutriment condition, two… by way of association condition, two; by way of presence condition, two; by way of absence condition, two… by way of non-disappearance condition, two (in brief).

7. Nadassanena pahātabbaṃ abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nadassanena pahātabbo abyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā (saṃkhittaṃ).

7. Dependent on an indeterminate state not to be abandoned by vision, an indeterminate state not to be abandoned by vision arises by way of root condition (in brief).

Hetuyā ekaṃ, ārammaṇe ekaṃ…pe… avigate ekaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ).

By way of root condition, one; by way of object condition, one... by way of non-disappearance condition, one (in brief).

By root condition, two; by object condition, two; … by non-disappearance condition, two. (In brief. Similar to the unwholesome section of the Dyad on Dhammas to be Abandoned by Seeing. To be elaborated in full in all cases in the Conascence Section … and the Question Section.)

12. An unwholesome state with a root to be abandoned by seeing arises dependent on an unwholesome state with a root to be abandoned by seeing by way of root condition. (1)

Nadassanena pahātabbahetukaṃ akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nadassanena pahātabbahetuko akusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nadassanena pahātabbahetukaṃ akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca dassanena pahātabbahetuko akusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. (2)

An unwholesome state with a root not to be abandoned by seeing arises dependent on an unwholesome state with a root not to be abandoned by seeing by way of root condition. An unwholesome state with a root to be abandoned by seeing arises dependent on an unwholesome state with a root not to be abandoned by seeing by way of root condition. (2)

Dassanena pahātabbahetukaṃ akusalañca nadassanena pahātabbahetukaṃ akusalañca dhammaṃ paṭicca dassanena pahātabbahetuko akusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. (1)

An unwholesome state with a root to be abandoned by seeing arises dependent on both an unwholesome state with a root to be abandoned by seeing and an unwholesome state with a root not to be abandoned by seeing, by way of root condition. (1)

Dassanena [T 5.0294] pahātabbahetukaṃ akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca dassanena pahātabbahetuko akusalo dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā… tīṇi (nadassane dve, ghaṭane ekaṃ, saṃkhittaṃ).

An unwholesome state with a root to be abandoned by seeing arises dependent on an unwholesome state with a root to be abandoned by seeing by way of object condition … three (in the 'not by seeing' case, two; in the combination case, one; in brief).

13. Hetuyā cattāri, ārammaṇe cha, adhipatiyā dve (sabbattha cha), avigate cha (saṃkhittaṃ).

13. By root condition, four; by object condition, six; by dominance condition, two (in all, six); by non-disappearance condition, six. (In brief).

14. Dassanena pahātabbahetukaṃ akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nadassanena pahātabbahetuko akusalo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā.

14. An unwholesome state with a root not to be abandoned by seeing arises dependent on an unwholesome state with a root to be abandoned by seeing, not by way of root condition.

An unwholesome state with a root not to be abandoned by seeing arises dependent on an unwholesome state with a root not to be abandoned by seeing, not by way of root condition. (In brief).

15. Nahetuyā dve, naadhipatiyā cha…pe… nakamme cattāri, navipāke cha, navippayutte cha (saṃkhittaṃ. Sahajātavārādi vitthāretabbo).

15. By non-root condition, two; by non-dominance condition, six; … by non-kamma condition, four; by non-resultant condition, six; by non-dissociation condition, six. (In brief. The sections beginning with Conascence should be elaborated.)

16. Dassanena pahātabbahetuko akusalo dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa akusalassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo (saṃkhittaṃ).

17. Hetuyā tīṇi, ārammaṇe nava, adhipatiyā tīṇi (dassane ekaṃ, nadassane dve), anantare nava, samanantare nava, sahajāte cha…pe… upanissaye nava, āsevane nava, kamme cattāri, āhāre cattāri, indriye cattāri…pe… sampayutte cha, atthiyā cha, natthiyā nava…pe… avigate cha (saṃkhittaṃ).

17. By root condition, three; by object condition, nine; by dominance condition, three (in the 'seeing' case, one; in the 'not-seeing' case, two); by proximity condition, nine; by contiguity condition, nine; by conascence condition, six; … by decisive support condition, nine; by repetition condition, nine; by kamma condition, four; by nutriment condition, four; by faculty condition, four; … by association condition, six; by presence condition, six; by absence condition, nine; … by non-disappearance condition, six. (In brief).

By root condition, one; by object condition, one; … by non-disappearance condition, one. (In brief).

(Sahajātavārepi…pe… pañhāvārepi sabbattha ekaṃ.)

(In the conascence section … in the question section, it is everywhere one.)

23. Savitakkaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca savitakko kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Savitakkaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca avitakko kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā[V 4.0534]. Savitakkaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca savitakko kusalo ca avitakko kusalo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. (3)

23. A wholesome state with applied thought arises dependent on a wholesome state with applied thought by way of root condition. A wholesome state without applied thought arises dependent on a wholesome state with applied thought by way of root condition. Wholesome states with and without applied thought arise dependent on a wholesome state with applied thought by way of root condition. (3)

Avitakkaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca avitakko kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Avitakkaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca savitakko kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. (2)

Savitakkaṃ kusalañca avitakkaṃ kusalañca dhammaṃ paṭicca savitakko kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. (1) (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

24. Hetuyā cha, ārammaṇe cha (sabbattha cha), avigate cha (saṃkhittaṃ).

Avitakko [V 4.0535] kusalo dhammo avitakkassa kusalassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi.

Savitakko kusalo ca avitakko kusalo ca dhammā savitakkassa kusalassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi (saṃkhittaṃ).

Wholesome states with and without applied thought are a condition for a wholesome state with applied thought by way of object condition... three. (In brief.)

26. Hetuyā cattāri, ārammaṇe nava, adhipatiyā nava (heṭṭhā tīsu sahajātādhipati, avitakke ekaṃ, sahajātādhipati), anantare nava, samanantare nava, sahajāte cha…pe… upanissaye nava, āsevane nava, kamme cattāri, āhāre cattāri, indriye cattāri, jhāne cha, magge cha, sampayutte cha, atthiyā cha, natthiyā nava, vigate nava, avigate cha (saṃkhittaṃ).

26. By root condition, four; by object condition, nine; by dominance condition, nine (in the three foregoing cases, by co-nascent dominance; in the case of the state without applied thought, one case is by co-nascent dominance); by contiguity condition, nine; by immediate contiguity condition, nine; by co-nascence condition, six; ... by support condition, nine; by repetition condition, nine; by kamma condition, four; by nutriment condition, four; by faculty condition, four; by jhāna condition, six; by path condition, six; by association condition, six; by presence condition, six; by absence condition, nine; by disappearance condition, nine; by non-disappearance condition, six. (In brief.)

Nahetuyā nava, naārammaṇe nava (saṃkhittaṃ).

By non-root condition, nine; by non-object condition, nine. (In brief.)

Hetupaccayā naārammaṇe cattāri (saṃkhittaṃ).

By root condition, not by object condition, four. (In brief.)

Nahetupaccayā ārammaṇe nava (saṃkhittaṃ).

By non-root condition, in object condition, nine. (In brief.)

29. Savitakkaṃ akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca savitakko akusalo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā. (1)

30. Nahetuyā tīṇi, naadhipatiyā pañca, nakamme tīṇi…pe… navippayutte pañca. (Saṃkhittaṃ. Sahajātavārādi vitthāretabbo.)
